more.t: מֶֽלֶךְ־ הַנֶּגֶב (Daniel 11:5), the king of the south, with six points, and צָפֹנָה וָנֶגְבָּה (Bereishis 13:14), northward and southward: it is the south.

אֶרֶץ הַנֶּגֶב נְתַתָּנִי, you have given me a southern land, which he explains as a waste and parched land; and so כַּֽאֲפִיקִים בַּנֶּֽגֶב (Tehillim 126:4), like streams in the Negev, כְּסוּפוֹת בַּנֶּגֶב (Yeshayahu 21:1), like whirlwinds in the Negev, and מַשָּׂא בַּֽהֲמוֹת נֶגֶב (Yeshayahu 30:6), the burden of the beasts of the Negev.

more.h: Drying, in Targum and in Chazal
more.t: חָֽרְבוּ פְּנֵי הָֽאֲדָמָֽה (Bereishis 8:13), the face of the ground was dry, which the Targum renders נְגוּבוּ אַפֵּי אַרְעָא; and Chazal (Taharos 10:8) say מנגבן והן טהורין, he wipes them dry and they are clean. They use the word much besides.

וְדָוִד קָם מֵאֵצֶל הַנֶּגֶב (Shmuel I 20:41), David rose from beside the Negev, נֶגֶב יְהוּדָה (Shmuel I 27:10), the Negev of Yehudah, אֶל־ נֶגֶב וְאֶל־צִקְלַג (Shmuel I 30:1), to the Negev and to Tziklag, and עָרֵי הַנֶּגֶב סֻגְּרוּ (Yirmiyahu 13:19), the cities of the Negev are shut up: all of them may be the wilderness and the place of drought and dryness, or the south. Or they are level ground, the wilderness being level too; and the south itself is called נֶגֶב, the Negev, because that quarter has much drought and no settlement as the others have, for its heat.

יבשׁ.sense: To be dry and to dry a thing up, and the dry land; and in the same letters a second sense, to be shamed, with pesukim in Yoel he allows either way.

more.t: כִּי יָֽבְשׁוּ אֲפִיקֵי מָיִם (Yoel 1:20), the water channels are dried up; יָֽבְשׁוּ עַצְמוֹתֵינוּ (Yechezkel 37:11), our bones are dried; יָֽבְשָׁה הָאָֽרֶץ (Bereishis 8:14), the earth was dry; וַיִּיבַשׁ הַנָּחַל (Melachim I 17:7), the brook dried up. The sense, he says, is dryness.

On הֵן יַעְצֹר בַּמַּיִם וְיִבָשׁוּ (Iyov 12:15), He holds back the waters and they dry up, Rabbi Yonah wrote that the vav takes a chirik and the yod is quiescent. He says he did not find it so in the accurate books, but with a sheva under the vav and a chirik under the yod.

אֲשֶׁר־ הוֹבִישׁ (Yehoshua 2:10), how He dried up the waters of Yam Suf; הוֹבַשׁתִּי עֵץ לָח (Yechezkel 17:24), I dried up the green tree; וְהֹבִישׁוּ כֹּל מְצוּלוֹת יְאֹר (Zecharyah 10:11), and all the depths of the river shall be dried. Rabbi Yonah set that last as a word standing alone, and he says there is no need: in that pasuk a wind of trouble passes in the sea and strikes up its waves, and the winds dry all the depths of the river. So too תְּיַבֶּשׁ ־גָּֽרֶם (Mishlei 17:22), it dries the bone, and גּוֹעֵר בַּיָּם וַיַּבְּשֵׁהוּ (Nachum 1:4), He rebukes the sea and dries it, where he holds the written yod is the prefix and the root's own yod has dropped, leaving its vowel behind; Rabbi Yehudah said the reverse, and some, his father among them, read it as a form that takes an object outright.

וְנוֹזְלִים עַל־ יַבָּשָׁה (Yeshayahu 44:3), streams on the dry ground, and וְתֵֽרָאֶה הַיַּבָּשָׁה (Bereishis 1:9), let the dry land appear, which may be a noun or an adjective; with a tav for the heh, וְיַבֶּשֶׁת יָדָיו יָצָֽרוּ (Tehillim 95:5), His hands formed the dry land. In another pattern the adjective: עֵץ יָבֵשׁ (Yechezkel 17:24), a dry tree, and נַפְשֵׁנוּ יְבֵשָׁה (Bamidbar 11:6), our soul is dried up.

לֹֽא־עַתָּה יֵבוֹשׁ יַֽעֲקֹב (Yeshayahu 29:22), Yaakov shall not now be shamed; גַּם־ בּוֹשׁ לֹֽא־ יֵבוֹשׁוּ (Yirmiyahu 6:15), they are not ashamed at all; יֵבשׁוּ רֹֽדְפַי (Yirmiyahu 17:18), let my pursuers be shamed; and where it takes an object, הֹבַשְׁתָּ הַיּוֹם אֶת־פְּנֵי כָל־עֲבָדֶיךָ (Shmuel II 19:6), today you have shamed the face of all your servants.

הַגֶּפֶן הוֹבִישָׁה (Yoel 1:12), the vine is shamed, and הוֹבִישׁ תִּירוֹשׁ (Yoel 1:10), the new wine is shamed, he takes by way of figure, as though the vine had shame when it does not give its fruit as it should, like הֹבִישׁוּ אִכָּרִים (Yoel 1:11), the farmers are shamed, and הֹבִישׁוּ חֲכָמִים (Yirmiyahu 8:9), the wise are shamed. But those two may be read instead as a sense of drying and ceasing.

נעם.sense: To be pleasant or lovely: words that please, ways of pleasantness, the sweet singer of Israel. The sense, he says, is known, and belongs to beauty.

more.t: נָעַמְתָּ לִּי מְאֹד (Shmuel II 1:26), you were very pleasant to me; וְשָׁמְעוּ אֲמָרַי כִּי נָעֵֽמוּ (Tehillim 141:6), they shall hear my words, for they are pleasant; וְדַעַת לְֽנַפְשְׁךָ יִנְעָֽם (Mishlei 2:10), knowledge shall be pleasant to your soul.

נְעִמוֹת בִּימִינְךָ נֶֽצַח (Tehillim 16:11), pleasures at Your right hand for ever; כָּל־הוֹן יָקָר וְנָעִֽים (Mishlei 24:4), all precious and pleasant wealth; וּנְעִים זְמִרוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (Shmuel II 23:1), the sweet singer of Israel; הַנֶּאֱהָבִים וְהַנְּעִימִם (Shmuel II 1:23), the beloved and the pleasant; נִטְעֵי נַֽעֲמָנִים (Yeshayahu 17:10), plantings of pleasantness; דְּרָכֶיהָ דַרְכֵי־ נֹעַם (Mishlei 3:16), her ways are ways of pleasantness; and וּבַל־אֶלְחַם בְּמַנְעַמֵּיהֶֽם (Tehillim 141:4), let me not eat of their dainties.

כִּֽי־ נָעִים כִּֽי־תִשְׁמְרֵם בְּבִטְנֶךָ (Mishlei 22:18) may instead be read from נָע וָנָד (Bereishis 4:12), wandering and moving: if you do not keep them in your belly they will soon be on the move and gone.

מתק.sense: To be sweet and to make sweet: sweetness of speech, sweeter than honey, the sleep of a labourer, and by a borrowing evil sweet in the mouth and sweet light.

more.t: מָֽתְקוּ ־לוֹ רִגְבֵי נָחַל (Iyov 21:33), the clods of the valley are sweet to him, and מְתָקוֹ רִמָּה (Iyov 24:20), which he reads either as the worm being sweet to him or as the worm's mouth being sweetened from him.

אִם־ תַּמְתִּיק בְּפִיו רָעָה (Iyov 20:12), though evil be sweet in his mouth, which he calls a borrowed use and takes without an object; and אֲשֶׁר יַחְדָּו נַמְתִּיק סוֹד (Tehillim 55:15), with whom we sweetened counsel together, where it takes one.

וּמֶתֶק שְׂפָתַיִם יֹסִיף לֶֽקַח (Mishlei 16:21), sweetness of lips adds learning; הֶֽחֳדַלְתִּי אֶת־ מָתְקִי (Shoftim 9:11), shall I leave my sweetness; חִכּוֹ מַֽמְתַּקִּים (Shir HaShirim 5:16), his palate is sweetness; מַה־ מָּתוֹק מִדְּבַשׁ (Shoftim 14:18), what is sweeter than honey; וַתְּהִי בְפִי כִּדְבַשׁ לְמָתֽוֹק (Yechezkel 3:3), which he explains as being sweet in his mouth as honey is sweet to a man; מְתוּקָה שְׁנַת הָֽעֹבֵד (Koheles 5:11), sweet is the sleep of the labourer; and by a borrowing, וּמָתוֹק הָאוֹר (Koheles 11:7), and the light is sweet.

סבא.sense: To drink deep and be drunk; from it wine itself is named, and the man who sells it; and by the same letters a nation of the sons of Kush.

more.t: וְנִסְבְּאָה שֵׁכָר (Yeshayahu 56:12), let us fill ourselves with strong drink; זוֹלֵל וְסֹבֵֽא (Devarim 21:20), a glutton and a drunkard; אַל־תְּהִי בְסֹֽבְאֵי ־יָיִן (Mishlei 23:20), be not among the drinkers of wine; וּכְסָבְאָם סְבוּאִים (Nachum 1:10), and drunken as with their drink. סָבָאִים מִמִּדְבָּר (Yechezkel 23:42) he takes as men who have drunk and are drunk.

The wine itself is named from it: סָבְאֵךְ מָהוּל בַּמָּֽיִם (Yeshayahu 1:22), your wine is mixed with water. And so the wine-seller was called סובא, a drinker, as the poet has it, and as Chazal (Avodah Zarah 70b) speak of a woman who sells wine, מסוביתא, the wine-woman, who handed over her key.

כּוּשׁ וּסְבָאִים אַנְשֵׁי מִדָּה (Yeshayahu 45:14), Kush and the Sevaim, men of stature, where it is the name of a nation of the sons of Kush; and מֽוּבָאִים סָבָאִים מִמִּדְבָּר may be read that way as well.

זלל.sense: A glutton, one who eats much meat, set beside the drunkard; and in a second sense, lightness and contempt.

more.t: זוֹלֵל וְסֹבֵֽא (Devarim 21:20), a glutton and a drunkard, and בְּזֹֽלְלֵי בָשָׂר לָֽמוֹ (Mishlei 23:20), among those who gorge on meat: one who eats much meat is called זולל, a glutton, as one who drinks much wine is called סובא, a drunkard.

וְאִם־תּוֹצִיא יָקָר מִזּוֹלֵל (Yirmiyahu 15:19), if you bring out the precious from the vile, and כִּי הָיִיתִי זוֹלֵלָֽה (Eichah 1:11), for I have become despised. The noun is כְּרֻם זֻלֻּת לִבְנֵי אָדָֽם (Tehillim 12:9), which he reads as: when the wicked are lifted high, there is contempt for the sons of men. Rabbi Yonah put הָרִים נָזֹֽלּוּ (Yeshayahu 64:2), the mountains flowed down, under this root, and he holds the right view is that it belongs to נזל, flowing.

איב.sense: To be an enemy; its sense, he says, is hatred.

more.t: One line: וְאָֽיַבְתִּי אֶת־אֹיְבֶיךָ (Shemos 23:22), I will be an enemy to your enemies, and the noun וְאֵיבָה אָשִׁית (Bereishis 3:15), I will put enmity; the sense is hatred.

צרר.sense: To harass and be an enemy, and the straits that come of it; and a second sense, to bind up: a bundle of silver, and צְרוֹר, a pebble.

more.t: וְצָֽרְרוּ אֶתְכֶם (Bamidbar 33:55), they shall harass you; צָרוֹר אֶת־הַמִּדְיָנִים (Bamidbar 25:17), harass the Midianites; כי צֹֽרֲרִים הֵם לָכֶם (Bamidbar 25:18), for they harass you; and וְצַרְתִּי אֶת־ צֹֽרְרֶֽיךָ (Shemos 23:22), I will harass those who harass you. It may be that וִֽיהוּדָה לֹֽא־ יָצֹר אֶת־אֶפְרָֽיִם (Yeshayahu 11:13), Yehudah shall not harass Efraim, is from this root.

מִן־ הַמֵּצַֽר (Tehillim 118:5), out of the strait, and בֵּין הַמְּצָרִֽים (Eichah 1:3), between the straits. Rabbi Yehudah put וְהֵצַר לְךָ (Devarim 28:52), it shall press you, and וַֽהֲצֵרֹתִי לָֽאָדָם (Tzefaniah 1:17), I will press men hard, under this root; he says he has written them at צוּר, along with צַר וְאוֹיֵב (Esther 7:6), an adversary and an enemy, and צַר ־לִי מְאֹד (Shmuel II 24:14), I am in great straits, and it may be that the root of them all is צָרַר.

Rabbi Yehudah set in another sense וְכִֽעֲסַתָּה צָֽרָתָהּ (Shmuel I 1:6), her rival vexed her, and לִצְרֹר לְגַלּוֹת עֶרְוָתָהּ (Vayikra 18:18), to take a rival and uncover her nakedness; he says he has explained the rival at צוּר.

מִי צָֽרַר ־מַיִם בַּשִּׂמְלָה (Mishlei 30:4), who has bound up water in a garment; צֹֽרֵר ־מַיִם בְּעָבָיו (Iyov 26:8), He binds up water in His clouds; כִּצְרוֹר אֶבֶן בְּמַרְגֵּמָה (Mishlei 26:8), as one binds a stone in a sling; and in the passive, וּמְבֻקָּעִים וּמְצֹֽרָרִֽים (Yehoshua 9:4), split and bound up. The noun is צְֽרוֹר ־הַכֶּסֶף לָקַח בְּיָדוֹ (Mishlei 7:20), he took the bundle of silver in his hand, and צְרוֹר הַמֹּר דּוֹדִי לִי (Shir HaShirim 1:13), my beloved is a bundle of myrrh to me: their sense is binding.

וַתִּֽהְיֶינָה צְרֻרוֹת (Shmuel II 20:3), they were shut up till the day of their death, which he holds belongs to binding: as though they were bound and not loosed to marry a man. And וְלֹֽא־יִפּוֹל צְרוֹר אָֽרֶץ (Amos 9:9), not a pebble shall fall to the ground, and אֲשֶֽׁר־לֹֽא־נִמְצָא שָׁם גַּם־ צְרֽוֹר (Shmuel II 17:13), where not even a pebble was found, he explains as a stone, and it is like צוּר, a rock, the two being one sense.

מיר.sense: To exchange one thing for another, and the תמורה, what is given in its place; on one pasuk he adds a second sense, of magnifying.

more.t: הֵמִיר כְּבוֹדוֹ (Yirmiyahu 2:11), he exchanged his glory; וְלֹֽא־ יָמִיר אֹתוֹ (Vayikra 27:10), he shall not exchange it; וְלֹא יָמֵר (Yechezkel 48:14), he shall not exchange, said of the first of the land; and the noun, וְהָֽיָה־הוּא וּתְמֽוּרָתוֹ (Vayikra 27:10), it and what is exchanged for it. Their sense is the exchanging of one thing for another.

הַֽהֵימִיר גּוֹי אֱלֹהִים (Yirmiyahu 2:11), has a nation exchanged its gods: the yod written between the heh and the first root letter is the quiescent letter of הֵקִים, he raised up, and הֵשִׁיב, he brought back, and here it is written against the usual way. He suggests the word is built to carry two senses at once. One is exchange, that a nation has changed its gods for other gods although they are no gods. The other is from וּבִכְבוֹדָם תִּתְיַמָּֽרוּ (Yeshayahu 61:6), and in their glory you shall vaunt yourselves, so that הֵימִיר follows the pattern of הֵיטִיב, he did good, and the sense is: has a nation magnified other gods that are not its own, when neither of them is a god.

חלף.sense: To pass by and be gone; to change a thing or renew it, and changes of garments; and a sense of cutting through, so that knives are called מַֽחֲלָפִים, cutters.

more.t: חָלַף הָלַךְ לֽוֹ (Shir HaShirim 2:11), it has passed and gone; וְחָֽלַפְתָּ מִשָּׁם וָהָלְאָה (Shmuel I 10:3), you shall pass on from there; וְיַֽחֲלֹף וְֽלֹא־אָבִין לֽוֹ (Iyov 9:11), He passes by and I do not perceive Him; כְּסוּפוֹת בַּנֶּגֶב לַֽחֲלֹף (Yeshayahu 21:1), like whirlwinds in the Negev sweeping through; חָלְפוּ חֹק (Yeshayahu 24:5), they passed over the statute. All of them, he says, are a sense of passing.

וְהַֽחֲלִיפוּ שִׂמְלֹֽתֵיכֶֽם (Bereishis 35:2), change your garments; וַתַּֽחֲלֵף אֶת־מַשְׂכֻּרְתִּי (Bereishis 31:41), you changed my wages; כַּלְּבוּשׁ תַּֽחֲלִיפֵם וְֽיַֽחֲלֹֽפוּ (Tehillim 102:27), You change them like a garment and they pass away; אִֽם־יִכָּרֵת וְעוֹד יַֽחֲלִיף (Iyov 14:7), though it be cut down it will yet renew, meaning it will renew its shoots; וְקַשְׁתִּי בְּיָדִי תַֽחֲלִֽיף (Iyov 29:20), my bow renews in my hand, which he explains as my strength and my might renewing my honour for me; and יַֽחֲלִיפוּ כֹחַ (Yeshayahu 40:31), they shall renew strength.

more.h: A change of garments, and in place of
more.t: וַיְגַלַּח וַיְחַלֵּף שִׂמְלֹתָיו (Bereishis 41:14), he shaved and changed his garments; חֲלִפוֹת שְׂמָלֹת (Bereishis 45:22), changes of raiment; וּשְׁלשִׁים חֲלִפֹת בְּגָדִֽים (Shoftim 14:12), thirty changes of garments: all in the sense of renewal and exchange. One thing coming in another's place is עֲשֶׂרֶת אֲלָפִים בַּחֹדֶשׁ חֲלִיפוֹת (Melachim I 5:28), ten thousand a month by courses, these going and those coming. And חֵלֶף עֲבֹֽדַתְכֶם (Bamidbar 18:31), in return for your service, with six points, is what the Targum gives for תַּחַת (Bereishis 4:25), in place of.

אִם־ יַֽחֲלֹף וְיַסְגִּיר (Iyov 11:10), if He cut through and shut up; וְהָאֱלִילִים כָּלִיל יַֽחֲלֹֽף (Yeshayahu 2:18), the idols shall wholly pass away; תַּחְלְפֵהוּ קֶשֶׁת נְחוּשָֽׁה (Iyov 20:24), a bow of brass shall strike him through; and the nouns עַד־בּוֹא חֲלִיפָתִֽי (Iyov 14:14), until my change come, אֲשֶׁר אֵין חֲלִיפוֹת לָמוֹ (Tehillim 55:20), who have no changes, and כָּל־בְּנֵי חֲלֽוֹף (Mishlei 31:8), all the sons of passing. All of these are a sense of cutting off, and the people of the world are called בני חלוף, sons of passing, because death and cutting off from the world come upon them.

His father explains כֶּחָצִיר יַֽחֲלֹֽף (Tehillim 90:5), like grass that passes, from this: if they are there at night they are not there in the morning, for the grass is cut off, the word standing alone in that sense. And if בַּבֹּקֶר יָצִיץ וְחָלָף (Tehillim 90:6), in the morning it blossoms and is renewed, is like וְעוֹד יַֽחֲלִיף (Iyov 14:7), it will yet renew, then by evening it is cut down and dried.

Knives are called מחלפים, מַֽחֲלָפִים תִּשְׁעָה וְעֶשְׂרִֽים (Ezra 1:9), twenty nine knives, because they cut; and אֶת־שֶׁבַע מַחְלְפוֹת רֹאשִׁי (Shoftim 16:13), the seven locks of my head, are the curls of the hair, called so because they are like knives, or because change and exchange come over them when they whiten in old age.

שׁפח.sense: The שִׁפְחָה, a maidservant, with no masculine formed from it; and in a second sense the מִשְׁפָּחָה, a family, and so a tribe, and so a whole nation.

more.t: כְּעֵינֵי שִׁפְחָה אֶל־יַד גְּבִרְתָּהּ (Tehillim 123:2), as the eyes of a maid to the hand of her mistress; עֲבָדִים וּשְׁפָחוֹת (Koheles 2:7), menservants and maidservants; אֵין לְשִׁפְחָֽתְךָ כֹל (Melachim II 4:2), your maidservant has nothing. No masculine noun is formed from it: for the male one says עֶבֶד, a servant, and for the female אָמָה or שפחה, a maid.

מִשְׁפָּחָה וּמִשְׁפָּחָה (Esther 9:28), every single family, and לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתֵיהֶם יָֽצְאוּ מִן־הַתֵּבָֽה (Bereishis 8:19), they went out of the ark by their families. A tribe is called by it too: וַיַּקְרֵב אֶת־ מִשְׁפַּחַת יְהוּדָה (Yehoshua 7:17), he brought near the family of Yehudah, the tribe that is taken drawing near by families (Yehoshua 7:14).

וְאִם־ מִשְׁפַּחַת מִצְרַיִם (Zecharyah 14:18), and if the family of Mitzrayim; עַל כָּל־ הַמִּשְׁפָּחָה אֲשֶׁר הֶעֱלֵיתִי מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם (Amos 3:1), against the whole family I brought up from the land of Mitzrayim; מִכֹּל מִשְׁפְּחוֹת הָֽאֲדָמָה (Amos 3:2), of all the families of the earth. And by a borrowing, וּפָֽקַדְתִּי עֲלֵיהֶם אַרְבַּע מִשְׁפָּחוֹת (Yirmiyahu 15:3), I will appoint over them four kinds.

שֹפח.sense: He gives no sense here. The entry is one pasuk of Yeshayahu, with a note that the word is treated at the letter samech.

more.t: The one pasuk is Yeshayahu 3:17, on קָדְקֹד בְּנוֹת צִיּוֹן, the crown of the daughters of Tzion. Of the word itself he says nothing here, only that he has already treated it at the letter samech.

אמה.sense: A maidservant, which he says is the same as a maid; but in one pasuk some read אַמָּתָהּ with a dagesh, and it is her arm.

more.t: וְגַם אֶת־בֶּן־ הָֽאָמָה (Bereishis 21:10), and also the son of the maidservant: the heh at the end is the feminine ending, and the root's own last heh drops, showing again in וְאַמְהֹתָיו וַיֵּלֵֽדוּ (Bereishis 20:17), and his maidservants, and they bore. Their sense is known, that they are maids.

וַתִּשְׁלַח אֶת־ אֲמָתָהּ (Shemos 2:5), she sent her maidservant. The reading is disputed: some read אַמָּתָהּ with a dagesh, from אַמָּה אָרְכּוֹ (Shemos 30:2), a cubit its length, and so Rav Saadiah Gaon explained it in his Arabic commentary, that she stretched out her arm.

צום.sense: To fast, and צוֹם, a fast; though where a fast is called and teshuvah is not the matter, his father wrote that צוֹם is a gathering.

more.t: לָמָּה צַּמְנוּ וְלֹא רָאִיתָ (Yeshayahu 58:3), why have we fasted and You did not see, וַיָּצֻמוּ שִׁבְעַת יָמִים (Shmuel I 31:13), they fasted seven days, וַיָּצָם דָּוִד צוֹם (Shmuel II 12:16), and וְצוּמוּ עָלַי וְאַל תֹּאכְלוּ וְאַל תִּשְׁתּוּ (Esther 4:16), fast for me and do not eat and do not drink. The noun is וַיִּקְרְאוּ צוֹם (Yonah 3:5), they called a fast, with the feminine plural דִּבְרֵי הַצֹּמוֹת (Esther 9:31), of which he says only that it is known.

הֲצוֹם צַמְתֻּנִי אָנִי (Zechariah 7:5) he reads: did you fast on My account? Did I command you to fast? It was for your fathers' sins that the House was destroyed. And what have you settled with Me by your fasting or by your eating and drinking, on the way of אִם צָדַקְתָּ מַה תִּתֶּן לוֹ (Iyov 35:7), if you are righteous, what do you give Him? That is, do justice, truth, kindness and mercy and you will not fast at all, for the House you fast over will be built, and you will rejoice in its building and eat and drink.

On קִרְאוּ צוֹם וְהֹשִׁיבוּ אֶת נָבוֹת בְּרֹאשׁ הָעָם (Melachim I 21:9) his father wrote that it is not a word for fasting but for assembling, from צומת הגידין in the Talmud, the meeting of the sinews; and so every calling of a צוֹם that is not in a matter of teshuvah, and so בְּיוֹם צוֹם (Yirmiyahu 36:6), on a day of assembly.

צמת.sense: To cut off; all of the forms, he ends, are one sense of כריתה, cutting off.

more.t: צָמְתוּ בַבּוֹר חַיָּי (Eichah 3:53), they cut off my life in the pit. In the passive, בְּעֵת יְזֹרְבוּ נִצְמָתוּ (Iyov 6:17), when they grow hot they are cut off; and some explain that one as נתחברו, they were joined together, from צומת הגידין in the words of Chazal. The noun is לַצְּמִיתֻת לַקֹּנֶה אֹתוֹ (Vayikra 25:30), cut off to the one who bought it.

more.h: Where the verb takes an object
more.t: צִמְּתַתְנִי קִנְאָתִי (Tehillim 119:139), my zeal has cut me off, בִּעוּתֶיךָ צִמְּתוּתֻנִי (Tehillim 88:17), Your terrors have cut me off, אוֹתוֹ אַצְמִית (Tehillim 101:5), him will I cut off, הִצְמַתָּה כָּל זוֹנֶה מִמֶּךָּ (Tehillim 73:27), You have cut off everyone who strays from You, and וּמְשַׂנְאַי אַצְמִיתֵם (Tehillim 18:41), I will cut off those who hate me.

נצח.sense: The text here breaks off after מְנַצְּחִים לְהַעֲבִיד אֶת הָעָם, overseers set over the people at their work, and runs on into words of reaching.

more.h: What the rest of it holds
more.t: כִּי שִׂיחַ וְכִי שִׂיג לוֹ (Melachim I 18:27), which he reads as that he has business with another, or is taken up with the overtaking of his enemies in war; all of them, he says, are ההדבקה וההגעה, cleaving to a thing and reaching it. שִׂיג is a noun with its nun missing, as שִׂיא is in אִם יַעֲלֶה לַשָּׁמַיִם שִׂיאוֹ (Iyov 20:6), though his loftiness mount to the heavens. Written with a samech, וְתַסֵּג וְלֹא תַפְלִיט (Michah 6:14) is that she reaches pregnancy and does not bring it forth but casts it.

סלה.sense: To tread down and trample; and in a second sense, to be set at a price.

more.t: סָלִיתָ כָּל שׁוֹגִים מֵחֻקֶּיךָ (Tehillim 119:118) and סִלָּה כָל אַבִּירַי (Eichah 1:15). Their sense may be taken from מסלה, a highway, even though the two are separate roots: you have trodden and trampled all who stray from Your statutes, and he trod and trampled all my mighty ones in my midst.
לֹא תְסֻלֶּה בְּכֶתֶם אוֹפִיר (Iyov 28:16), of which he says לא תעריך, it is not to be valued; and he points to what he has already written at the root סָלָא.

רבע.sense: To be four-square; and the number four, with רֶבַע and רְבִיעִית for a fourth part and רְבִיעִי for fourth.

more.t: רָבוּעַ יִהְיֶה הַמִּזְבֵּחַ (Shemos 27:1), that its sides be equal, its length as its breadth; so רְבִיעִית of the terumah (Yechezkel 45:20), that it be square, its length as its breadth, and מְזוּזוֹת עֲצֵי שָׁמֶן מֵאֵת רְבִעִית (Melachim I 6:33), that on all its sides they were squared, which Targum Yonasan renders מִן אַרְבְּעָה סִטְרֵיהוֹן מְרַבְּעִין, squared from their four sides. Also מְרֻבַּע סָבִיב (Yechezkel 45:2) and וְרֹחַב מֵאָה אַמָּה מְרֻבָּעַת (Yechezkel 40:47), a hundred cubits broad, squared.

more.h: The number, and the fourth part
more.t: לְאַרְבָּעָה רָאשִׁים (Bereishis 2:10), to four heads, and אֶל אַרְבַּעַת מִקְצוֹעֵי הֶחָצֵר (Yechezkel 46:21), to the four corners of the court; for the feminine, without a heh, וְאַרְבַּע צֹאן (Shemos 21:37), four sheep. וְאֶת הַכִּבְשָׂה יְשַׁלֵּם אַרְבַּעְתָּיִם (Shmuel II 12:6) is two times four, double as the law has it, since of one who steals a sheep four sheep are said for the one. The part of the four is רֶבַע הַהִין (Shemos 29:40), a quarter of a hin, with אֶל אַרְבַּעַת רְבָעָיו (Yechezkel 43:16), וּמִסְפָּר אֶת רֹבַע יִשְׂרָאֵל (Bamidbar 23:10), and רְבִיעִת הַהִין (Shemos 29:40).

יוֹם רְבִיעִי (Bereishis 1:19), the fourth day, בְּנֵי רְבִעִים (Melachim II 10:30), sons of the fourth generation, and in another pattern וְעַל רִבֵּעִים (Shemos 34:6), and upon the fourth generation.

Rabbi Yonah wrote that לְרִבְעָהּ תֶּבֶל הוּא (Vayikra 18:23) is derived from this sense of four, and לֹא תַרְבִּיעַ כִּלְאַיִם (Vayikra 19:19) stands here as well. The right account, he says, is that they are of the sense of אָרְחִי וְרִבְעִי זֵרִיתָ (Tehillim 139:3), my path and my lying down, which is what the Targum puts for וַתִּרְבַּץ תַּחַת בִּלְעָם (Bamidbar 22:27), and she lay down under Bilam, rendering it וּרְבַעַת.

שׁכל.sense: To be bereaved of children, and where the verb takes an object, to bereave; and in another sense אֶשְׁכּוֹל, a cluster.

more.t: כַּאֲשֶׁר שָׁכֹלְתִּי שָׁכָלְתִּי (Bereishis 43:14), as I have been bereaved, I am bereaved; לָמָה אֶשְׁכַּל גַּם שְׁנֵיכֶם (Bereishis 27:45), which he reads as why should I be bereaved of both of you, or on account of both of you; and כֵּן תִּשְׁכַּל מִנָּשִׁים (Shmuel I 15:33), more than the rest of the women. The adjective is וַאֲנִי שְׁכוּלָה וְגַלְמוּדָה (Yeshayahu 49:21), and the nouns וְלֹא אֵדַע שְׁכוֹל (Yeshayahu 47:8), I shall not know bereavement, שְׁכוֹל לְנַפְשִׁי (Tehillim 35:12) and שְׁכוֹל וְאַלְמֹן (Yeshayahu 47:9), bereavement and widowhood.

רְחֵלֶיךָ וְעִזֶּיךָ לֹא שִׁכֵּלוּ (Bereishis 31:38), your ewes and your she-goats did not lose their young, תְּפַלֵּט פָּרָתוֹ וְלֹא תְשַׁכֵּל (Iyov 21:10), his cow calves and does not lose her calf, וְלֹא תְשַׁכֵּל לָכֶם הַגֶּפֶן (Malachi 3:11), the vine will not cast its fruit for you, and מְשַׁכֵּלָה וַעֲקָרָה (Shemos 23:26), one that loses her young and one that is barren. The adjective is כְּדֹב שַׁכּוּל (Hoshea 13:8), a bereaved bear, and וְשַׁכֻּלָה אֵין בָּהֶם (Shir HaShirim 4:2), with a patach under the shin; the noun is שִׁכּוּל, with the plural בְּנֵי שִׁכֻּלָיִךְ (Yeshayahu 49:20), the shin there carrying a chirik.

more.h: Where the verb takes an object
more.t: שִׁכַּלְתִּי אִבַּדְתִּי אֶת עַמִּי (Yirmiyahu 15:7), I have bereaved, I have destroyed My people; כַּאֲשֶׁר שִׁכְּלָה נָשִׁים חַרְבֶּךָ (Shmuel I 15:33), as your sword has bereaved women; אֹתִי שִׁכַּלְתֶּם (Bereishis 42:36), you have bereaved me; מִחוּץ תְּשַׁכֶּל חֶרֶב (Devarim 32:25); אַעֲבִיר בָּאָרֶץ וְשִׁכְּלָתָּה (Yechezkel 14:15); וְחַיָּה רָעָה וְשִׁכְּלֻךְ (Yechezkel 5:17); and וְהָאָרֶץ מְשַׁכָּלֶת (Melachim II 2:19), the land bereaving. Also רֶחֶם מַשְׁכִּיל (Hoshea 9:14), a womb that bereaves, and כְּגִבּוֹר מַשְׁכִּיל (Yirmiyahu 50:9).

On וְלֹא יִהְיֶה מִשָּׁם עוֹד מָוֶת וּמְשַׁכָּלֶת he says the word of being already stated stands for two, the sense being that she will not be bereaving; or else משכלות is a noun. He weighs too whether וְהָאָרֶץ מְשַׁכָּלֶת takes only two, like מְשַׁכֵּלָה וַעֲקָרָה, and so of וּמְשַׁכֶּלֶת in Yechezkel 36:13.

אֵין אֶשְׁכּוֹל לֶאֱכוֹל (Michah 7:1), no cluster to eat, וְאֶשְׁכּוֹל עֲנָבִים אֶחָד (Bamidbar 13:23), one cluster of grapes, and אֶשְׁכֹּל הַכֹּפֶר (Shir HaShirim 1:11). The plurals are וְשָׁדַיִךְ לְאַשְׁכֹּלוֹת (Shir HaShirim 7:8), with a patach under the alef, כְּאֶשְׁכְּלוֹת הַגֶּפֶן (Shir HaShirim 7:9), with a segol, אַשְׁכְּלֹת מְרֹרֹת (Devarim 32:32), clusters of bitterness, and הִבְשִׁילוּ אַשְׁכְּלֹתֶיהָ עֲנָבִים (Bereishis 40:10), its clusters ripened into grapes. The single berries are called עֲנָבִים, grapes, and what holds them is called an אֶשְׁכּוֹל, for which he gives the name in his own vernacular.

נצר.sense: To guard and to keep; the נוֹצְרִים are watchmen; in a second sense, laid waste; and נֵצֶר, a shoot or a branch.

more.t: עֵדֹתֶיךָ נָצָרְתִּי (Tehillim 119:22), I have kept Your testimonies, נֹצֵר תְּאֵנָה יֹאכַל פִּרְיָהּ (Mishlei 27:18), one who tends a fig tree eats its fruit, לְנֹצְרֵי בְרִיתוֹ (Tehillim 25:10), to those who keep His covenant, נְצֹר לְשׁוֹנְךָ מֵרָע (Tehillim 34:14), guard your tongue from evil, and וּבְרִיתְךָ יִנְצֹרוּ (Devarim 33:9); all of them, he ends, are guarding. With the first root letter dropped, צוֹר תְּעוּדָה (Yeshayahu 8:16), which Targum Yonasan renders נְבִיָא טַר סַהֲדוּתָא, prophet, keep the testimony.

more.h: What is kept out of reach
more.t: וּנְצֻרוֹת וְלֹא יְדַעְתָּם (Yeshayahu 48:6) are things kept back and too high to be reached and known; וְהַנִּשְׁאָר וְהַנָּצוּר (Yechezkel 6:12) is one kept from being reached; and שִׁית זוֹנָה וּנְצֻרַת לֵב (Mishlei 7:10) is שמורת לב, guarded of heart, meaning that no man can take her and entice her, but she entices men.

מִמִּגְדַּל נוֹצְרִים (Melachim II 17:9) are the lookouts who stand in the tower, a tower not for settlement but for the watchman to stand in. So too קָרְאוּ נֹצְרִים בְּהַר אֶפְרָיִם (Yirmiyahu 31:6): the watchmen and keepers call out קומו ונעלה ציון, arise and let us go up to Tzion. Or נצרים may be a people named for their place, but the first is the right one. Rabbi Yonah explained נֹצְרִים בָּאִים מֵאֶרֶץ הַמֶּרְחָק (Yirmiyahu 4:16) as a people named after Nevuchadnetzar, and his father explains it so as well.

וּבַנְּצוּרִים יָלִינוּ (Yeshayahu 65:4) and כְּעִיר נְצוּרָה (Yeshayahu 1:8) are of the sense of חרבה, ruin. From this his father reads וּנְצֻרַת לב as חרבת דעת, ruined of understanding, writing that so it stands in the words of the philosopher, ישבו עולמם בחרבן שכלם, they settle their world in the ruin of their intellect; and he said it of the harlot, that she is חרבת שכל, ruined of mind.

וְנֵצֶר מִשָּׁרָשָׁיו יִפְרֶה (Yeshayahu 11:1), a shoot will grow from his roots, and כְּנֵצֶר נִתְעָב (Yeshayahu 14:19); their sense is יונק או ענף, a sucker or a branch. כְּנֵצֶר נִתְעָב is that as a man throws away the loathsome shoot that does not thrive, pulling it out of its pit and casting it off, so you were cast out of your grave.

נטר.sense: To keep and to guard, and so to keep a grudge; and from it the מַטָּרָה, the mark set up to be shot at, and the court of the guard.

more.t: הֲיִנְטֹר לְעוֹלָם (Yirmiyahu 3:5), will He keep it forever, וְנוֹטֵר הוּא לְאֹיְבָיו (Nachum 1:2), He keeps it for His enemies, לֹא אֶטּוֹר לְעוֹלָם (Yirmiyahu 3:12), I will not keep it forever, לֹא תִקֹּם וְלֹא תִטֹּר (Vayikra 19:18), do not take revenge and do not bear a grudge, and שָׂמֻנִי נֹטֵרָה אֶת הַכְּרָמִים (Shir HaShirim 1:6), they set me to keep the vineyards; all of them are guarding. The Targum of וַיִּשְׁמֹר (Bereishis 26:5) is וּנְטַר.

The thing set up for arrows to be shot at is called a מַטָּרָה: וַיְקִימֵנִי לוֹ לְמַטָּרָה (Iyov 16:12), He set me up for Himself as a mark, and with an alef in place of the heh, כַּמַּטָּרָא לַחֵץ (Eichah 3:12). Derived from the same sense is בַּחֲצַר הַמַּטָּרָה (Yirmiyahu 32:2), the court of the guard, as it is said in this matter וַיֶּאֱסֹף אֹתָם אֶל מִשְׁמָר (Bereishis 42:17), he gathered them into ward; and בְּשַׁעַר הַמַּטָּרָה (Nechemiah 12:39), where the guards stood.

מסך.sense: To mix: a spirit of confusion poured into a people, and the mixing of water with wine; and מֶסֶךְ and מִמְסָךְ, mixed wine.

more.t: מָסַךְ בְּקִרְבָּהּ רוּחַ עִוְעִים (Yeshayahu 19:14), which he takes as תערובות ובלבול, mixture and confusion. So also of the tempering that is the mixing of water with wine: מָסְכָה יֵינָהּ (Mishlei 9:2), she has mixed her wine, and וּשְׁתוּ בְּיַיִן מָסָכְתִּי (Mishlei 9:5), drink of the wine I have mixed.
מָלֵא מֶסֶךְ (Tehillim 75:9), full of mixture; and in another pattern לַחְקוֹר מִמְסָךְ (Mishlei 23:30), to search out mixed wine, and לַמְנִי מִמְסָךְ (Yeshayahu 65:11).

Rabbi Yonah put כָּל אֶבֶן יְקָרָה מְסֻכָתֶךָ (Yechezkel 28:13) under this root in one of its senses, meaning mixed with you. The right account, he says, is that it is from the root שֹוךְ, of the sense of הָסֵר מְשׂוּכָּתוֹ (Yeshayahu 5:5), remove its hedge; and though the one is written with a samech and the other with a shin they are one, the sense being that your hedge is of precious stones.

אשׁר.sense: אֲשֶׁר, the relative word, standing also for if, for so, for in order that, and for and; אֲשֵׁרָה, a worshipped tree; אַשְׁרֵי, happy; and אֲשֻׁרַי, steps.

more.t: הָאֲנָשִׁים אֲשֶׁר שָׁלַח מֹשֶׁה (Bamidbar 13:16), the men Moshe sent, and וְקָם הַבַּיִת אֲשֶׁר בָּעִיר (Vayikra 25:30): of these he says only that their sense is known. It stands in place of אִם, if: אֲשֶׁר נָשִׂיא יֶחֱטָא (Vayikra 4:22) and אֶת הַבְּרָכָה אֲשֶׁר תִּשְׁמְעוּ (Devarim 11:27) are if a ruler sins, if you listen. In place of כֵּן, so, in Shaul's words to Shmuel, אֲשֶׁר שָׁמַעְתִּי בְּקוֹל (Shmuel I 15:20). In place of לְמַעַן, in order that: אֲשֶׁר יִיטַב לְךָ וּלְבָנֶיךָ אַחֲרֶיךָ (Devarim 4:40). And in place of a vav: טוֹב אֲשֶׁר יָפֶה (Koheles 5:17) and עָוֹן אֲשֶׁר חֵטְא (Hoshea 12:9) are good and fair, iniquity and sin.

more.h: אֲשֶׁר with a letter before it
more.t: The kaf of likeness is added to it, כַּאֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה (Vayikra 8:34), as he did, and so in many places; sometimes it is missing, and אֲשֶׁר רְאִיתֶם אֶת מִצְרַיִם (Shemos 14:13) stands for כאשר ראיתם, as you have seen. A beis comes on it for because: בַּאֲשֶׁר אַתְּ אִשְׁתּוֹ (Bereishis 39:9), because you are his wife. And a beis comes on it to point at a place: בַּאֲשֶׁר כָּרַע שָׁם נָפַל שָׁדוּד (Shoftim 5:26), where he sank there he fell slain, and וּבַאֲשֶׁר חֲלָלִים שָׁם הוּא (Iyov 39:30).

לֹא תִטַּע לְךָ אֲשֵׁרָה כָּל עֵץ (Devarim 16:21): any tree that they serve, or that they plant in honour of the one they serve, is called an אֲשֵׁרָה. Its plural takes the masculine ending, בָּמוֹת וּמַצֵּבוֹת וַאֲשֵׁרִים (Melachim I 14:23), and so וְאֶת אֲשֵׁרָיו תִּכְרֹתוּן (Shemos 34:13), you shall cut down its asheiros, and וַאֲשֵׁרֵיהֶם תִּשְׂרְפוּן בָּאֵשׁ (Devarim 12:3).

more.h: אַשְׁרֵי, and calling a man happy
more.t: אַשְׁרֵי הָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר לֹא הָלַךְ (Tehillim 1:1), happy is the man who has not walked, and אַשְׁרֶיךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל מִי כָמוֹךָ (Devarim 33:29). It is a plural noun on the weight of אַחֲלֵי אֲדֹנִי (Melachim II 5:3), except that its alef is of the root while the alef of אחלי is added. The verb is to say of someone that he is happy: בְּאָשְׁרִי כִּי אִשְּׁרוּנִי בָּנוֹת (Bereishis 30:13), כִּי אֹזֶן שָׁמְעָה וַתְּאַשְּׁרֵנִי (Iyov 29:11), רָאוּהָ בָנוֹת וַיְאַשְּׁרוּהָ (Shir HaShirim 6:9), and וְתֹמְכֶיהָ מְאֻשָּׁר (Mishlei 3:18), of whom they say אשריו, happy is he.

תָּמֹךְ אֲשֻׁרַי (Tehillim 17:5) are דרכי או רגלי, my ways or my feet; so בַּאֲשֻׁרוֹ אָחֲזָה רַגְלִי (Iyov 23:11) and לֹא תִמְעַד אֲשֻׁרָיו (Tehillim 37:31), not even one of his steps will slip, the word being feminine like רגל, a foot. In another pattern, with a dagesh, אִם תִּטֶּה אַשֻּׁרִי מִנִי הַדָּרֶךְ (Iyov 31:7); all such are נתיב ודרך, track and way. The simple verb is וְאִשְׁרוּ בְּדֶרֶךְ בִּינָה (Mishlei 9:6), and where it takes an object it is to lead along a way: וְאַל תְּאַשֵּׁר בְּדֶרֶךְ רָעִים (Mishlei 4:14), do not tread, וְאַשֵּׁר בַּדֶּרֶךְ לִבֶּךָ (Mishlei 23:19), which he glosses as the known way that I taught you, the way of wisdom, מְאַשְּׁרֵי הָעָם הַזֶּה (Yeshayahu 9:15), those who lead this people, and אַשְּׁרוּ חָמוֹץ (Yeshayahu 1:17), lead the oppressed; or in these the alef stands for a yud, מְיַשְּׁרֵי, those who set this people straight.

עַל דֶּרֶךְ אָשׁוּר (Hoshea 13:7) may be the simple verb of this root; or it may be from אֲשׁוּרֶנּוּ וְלֹא קָרוֹב (Bamidbar 24:17), I behold him but not near, its alef the one that speaks of itself, the sense being that as a leopard is ready to tear, so I watch and look to tear them, as he says אֶפְגְּשֵׁם כְּדֹב שַׁכּוּל (Hoshea 13:8), I will meet them like a bereaved bear. תִּדְהָר וּתְאַשּׁוּר (Yeshayahu 41:19) is עץ ממין ארז, a tree of the cedar kind; Rabbi Yonah wrote that it goes by an Arabic name and that it is what is called בוס"ו in the vernacular, and the Targum says אֶשְׁכְּרוֹעִין. Targum Yonasan puts קַרְשֵׁךְ עָשׂוּ שֵׁן בַּת אֲשֻׁרִים (Yechezkel 27:6) as דַפִּין דְאֶשְׁכְּרוֹעִין מְכַבְשִׁין בְּשֵׁן דְפִיל, planks of it pressed with elephant's ivory, taking בַּת אֲשֻׁרִים as one word, though it is two.

קום.sense: To rise and to stand; to stand fast and be confirmed; קוֹמָה, height; קָמָה, standing grain; יְקוּם, all that lives; and מָקוֹם, a place.

more.t: וְלֹא קָם נָבִיא עוֹד (Devarim 34:10), no prophet arose again, קוּם הִתְהַלֵּךְ בָּאָרֶץ (Bereishis 13:17), arise and walk about the land, יָקֻם אָבִי וְיֹאכַל (Bereishis 27:31), let my father rise and eat, קוּם נָא שְׁבָה (Bereishis 27:19), and וַיָּקָם הָעָם כָּל הַיּוֹם הַהוּא (Bamidbar 11:32), the people rose all that day. In וְקָאם שָׁאוֹן בְּעַמֶּךָ (Hoshea 10:14) a quiescent alef is written for the middle letter of the root.

more.h: When eyes are said to rise
more.t: וְעֵינָיו קָמָה (Shmuel I 4:15) and כִּי קָמוּ עֵינָיו מִשֵּׂיבוֹ (Melachim I 14:4): rising is said of the eye because when a man's eyes dim in old age the cords of the eye pucker, and the eye rises and draws upward. Some read it by its context as a wasting of the eyes, and Targum Yonasan puts כָּלוּ עֵינֵיהֶם (Yirmiyahu 14:6) as קָמָא עֵינֵיהוֹן, and renders both of these with קָמָה.

more.h: Those who rise against a man
more.t: כָּל הַקָּמִים עָלֶיךָ (Shmuel II 18:31), all who rise against you, שְׁאוֹן קָמֶיךָ (Tehillim 74:23), and in another pattern וּמִכַּף מֶלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל הַקּוֹמִים עָלָי (Melachim II 16:7). Enemies are called קמים because they rise against the one opposite them for harm. On וְאֶל יֹשְׁבֵי לֵב קָמָי (Yirmiyahu 51:1) some read קמי by the alphabet turned about as כשדים, Kasdim, as in יֹשְׁבֵי כַשְׂדִּים (Yirmiyahu 51:35). He holds it may rather be that ארץ כשדים is short of its word, the sense being those who dwell in the land of Kasdim, with לֵב קָמָי in its plain sense, the heart of my adversaries, as תַּהֲרֹס קָמֶיךָ (Shemos 15:7) and לְשִׁמְצָה בְּקָמֵיהֶם (Shemos 32:25).

וְרָמֵי הַקּוֹמָה גְּדוּעִים (Yeshayahu 10:33), the high of stature hewn down, and וְאֶכְרֹת קוֹמַת אֲרָזָיו (Yeshayahu 37:24), the tallest of its cedars, which he takes as a figure for the great men and the officers; also זֹאת קוֹמָתֵךְ דָּמְתָה לְתָמָר (Shir HaShirim 7:8) and וַיִּפֹּל מְלֹא קוֹמָתוֹ (Shmuel I 28:20). Standing grain before it is reaped is called קָמָה because it all stands up together: מִגָּדִישׁ וְעַד קָמָה (Shoftim 15:5) and בְּקָמוֹת פְּלִשְׁתִּים (Shoftim 15:5).

וְקָמָה בְּיָדְךָ מַמְלֶכֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל (Shmuel I 24:21) is that it will stand and hold; so לֹא תָקוּם וְלֹא תִהְיֶה (Yeshayahu 7:7), וְקָם הַבַּיִת אֲשֶׁר בָּעִיר (Vayikra 25:30), and וַיָּקָם שְׂדֵה עֶפְרוֹן (Bereishis 23:17), that it stood and was made good in his hand. Where the verb takes an object it confirms: וּמַאֲמַר אֶסְתֵּר קִיַּם (Esther 9:32), Esther's word confirmed it, קַיְּמֵנִי כִּדְבָרֶךָ (Tehillim 119:28), and וְחָרְבוֹתֶיהָ אֲקוֹמֵם (Yeshayahu 44:26), I will raise up her ruins. From the same, וָאוֹלֵךְ אֶתְכֶם קוֹמְמִיּוּת (Vayikra 26:13) is with an upright stature, fearing no man, on the way of יֹצְאִים בְּיָד רָמָה (Shemos 14:8); and וְלֹא תִהְיֶה לָכֶם תְּקוּמָה (Vayikra 26:37).

וַיִּמַח אֶת כָּל הַיְקוּם (Bereishis 7:23) and וְאֵת כָּל הַיְקוּם אֲשֶׁר בְּרַגְלֵיהֶם (Devarim 11:6) are a general name for every living thing on the earth; אִם לֹא נִכְחַד קִימָנוּ (Iyov 22:20) is יְקוּמֵנוּ, that in truth our standing was not blotted out altogether in the mabul, since Noach and his sons were left. The place is וְשַׂמְתִּי לְךָ מָקוֹם (Shemos 21:13), mostly masculine, feminine in וְלֹא עוֹד תְּשׁוּרֶנּוּ מְקוֹמוֹ (Iyov 20:9), with the plural בְּאַחַד הַמְּקוֹמֹת (Shmuel II 17:9); and וְזֶה מְקוֹם לֹא יָדַע אֵל (Iyov 18:21) lacks the word it is bound to, the place of a man who did not know Hashem. Chazal called the Holy One by the name מָקוֹם, since He is the place of the world and the world is not His place, as He is also called מעון, a dwelling, in מְעֹנָה אֱלֹהֵי קֶדֶם (Devarim 33:27); and some read רֶוַח וְהַצָּלָה יַעֲמוֹד לַיְּהוּדִים מִמָּקוֹם אַחֵר (Esther 4:14) as a hint at Him, since they did not wish to write the Name in the Megillah, it being written together with the books of Madai and Paras.

נחל.sense: To take as a possession, and to give one; נַחֲלָה, an inheritance; and נַחַל, the valley the water runs down, named so even when dry.

more.t: וְאֵלֶּה אֲשֶׁר נָחֲלוּ בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל (Yehoshua 14:1), כִּי לֹא נִנְחַל אִתָּם (Bamidbar 32:19), we will not take a possession with them, and לִנְחֹל אֶת הָאָרֶץ (Bamidbar 34:18). The simple verb, he says, takes one object only, the inheritance itself, so that יִנְחֲלוּ לָכֶם אֶת הָאָרֶץ (Bamidbar 34:17) is that they take possession on your behalf.

וְסָלַחְתָּ לַעֲוֹנֵנוּ וּלְחַטָּאתֵנוּ וּנְחַלְתָּנוּ (Shemos 34:9) is take us for Your own, that we be Your inheritance, as וְהֵם עַמְּךָ וְנַחֲלָתֶךָ (Devarim 9:29), they are Your people and Your inheritance; and so of Yehudah (Zechariah 2:16), that Yehudah will be His inheritance forever on the holy soil. כִּי אַתָּה תִנְחַל בְּכָל הַגּוֹיִם (Tehillim 82:8) he reads with the opening of the mizmor, עַד מָתַי תִּשְׁפְּטוּ עָוֶל and קוּמָה אֱלֹהִים שָׁפְטָה הָאָרֶץ: in whatever nation the poor and the robbed are found, they are His people and His inheritance, and He will take them for His own and save them from the hand of their oppressors.

אֵלֶּה אֲשֶׁר נִחַל מֹשֶׁה בְּעַרְבוֹת מוֹאָב (Yehoshua 13:32) and כִּי אַתָּה תַּנְחִיל אֶת הָעָם הַזֶּה (Yehoshua 1:6), you will give this people its inheritance; so בְּיוֹם הַנְחִילוֹ אֶת בָּנָיו (Devarim 21:16) and בְּהַנְחֵל עֶלְיוֹן גּוֹיִם (Devarim 32:8). In the passive, כֵּן הָנְחַלְתִּי לִי יַרְחֵי שָׁוְא (Iyov 7:3), months of emptiness were given me for a portion; and turned back on itself, וְהִתְנַחַלְתֶּם אֹתָם (Vayikra 25:46), which he reads as מהם, of them, like הֵם יָצְאוּ אֶת הָעִיר (Bereishis 44:4).

וְנִחַלְתְּ בָּךְ לְעֵינֵי גוֹיִם (Yechezkel 22:16) may be taken from this root, though he explained it at חָלַל; its proper form would be וְנִנְחַלְתְּ, and but for the ches it would carry a dagesh. The reading is that until now you were My inheritance, but since you have sinned you are not: you will be inherited by yourself and not by Me.

פָּרַץ נַחַל מֵעִם גָּר (Iyov 28:4), וְהָיָה מֵהַנַּחַל תִּשְׁתֶּה (Melachim I 17:4), you will drink from the נַחַל, with the dual אֶל כָּל אֲשֶׁר יָבוֹא שָׁם נַחֲלַיִם יִחְיֶה (Yechezkel 47:9) and the plural כָּל הַנְּחָלִים הֹלְכִים אֶל הַיָּם (Koheles 1:7), all the streams go to the sea. The valley down which the waters run is called a נַחַל, and even when there is no water in it the place still carries the name, as וְהָעִיר אֲשֶׁר בַּנַּחַל (Devarim 2:36). אֶל נַחַל אֵיתָן (Devarim 21:4) had water in it, since it is written there that they wash their hands; and וּצְדָקָה כְּנַחַל אֵיתָן (Amos 5:24) is one whose waters sweep down with force. In נַהֲרֵי נַחֲלֵי דְּבַשׁ וְחֶמְאָה (Iyov 20:17) one construct comes upon another.
לַמְנַצֵּחַ אֶל הַנְּחִילוֹת (Tehillim 5:1) is the name of a tune they knew. Rabbeinu Hai explained the word from נחיל של דבורים, a swarm of bees, that its tune was like the hum of bees.

יאר.sense: The יְאֹר: the water drawn off from a river in channels onto the fields, and so the Nilus, and the Chidekel as well.

more.h: River, or channel from a river
more.t: עַל שְׂפַת הַיְאֹר (Shemos 2:3), on the bank of the יאור, כָּל הַמַּיִם אֲשֶׁר בַּיְאֹר (Shemos 7:20), all the water in the יאור, and עַל יְאֹרֵיהֶם וְעַל אַגְמֵיהֶם (Shemos 7:19). By Onkelos the יאור is the river itself, since he renders יְאֹר as נַהֲרָא; but יְאֹרֵיהֶם he renders with another word, because it stands bound to their rivers. The יאור is the water that is drawn off and led in streams from the river onto the fields.

Because the waters of the נילוס are drawn off and run over the fields to water them, it is called a יאור; and so the חדקל is called a יאור, אֶחָד הֵנָּה לִשְׂפַת הַיְאֹר וְאֶחָד הֵנָּה לִשְׂפַת הַיְאֹר (Daniel 12:5). In וְעָלְתָה כָאֹר כֻּלָּהּ (Amos 8:5) the yud is hidden, and the word stands for כיאור.

אחז.sense: To take hold and to grasp; and from it אֲחֻזָּה, a holding of land, because a man takes hold in the place and is held fast by it.

more.t: חִיל אָחַז (Shemos 15:14), trembling took hold, אָחַזְתָּ שְׁמֻרוֹת עֵינָי (Tehillim 77:5), You held my eyelids, לֶאֱחֹז בְּכַנְפוֹת הָאָרֶץ (Iyov 38:13), to take hold of the corners of the earth, וָאֹחֵז בְּפִילַגְשִׁי (Shoftim 20:6), and וֶאֱחֹז לְךָ אֶחָד מֵהַנְּעָרִים (Shmuel II 2:21). In the passive, נֶאֱחַז בַּסְּבַךְ (Bereishis 22:13), caught in the thicket, כַּדָּגִים שֶׁנֶּאֱחָזִים (Koheles 9:12), like fish that are caught, and וַיֵּאָחֲזוּ בָהּ (Bereishis 46:27). Also וְכֶבֶשׁ בַּזָּהָב לַכִּסֵּא מָאֳחָזִים (Divrei HaYamim II 9:18) and מְאַחֵז פְּנֵי כִסֵּה (Iyov 26:9).

אֲחֻזֵי חֶרֶב (Shir HaShirim 3:8), holding the sword, has the form of what is acted upon, in the way of חָגוּר כְּלֵי מִלְחָמָה (Shoftim 18:11), girded with weapons of war, and לָבוּשׁ בַּדִּים (Yechezkel 9:2), clothed in linen.

more.h: The beams that hold the walls
more.t: וַיֶּאֱחֹז אֶת הַבַּיִת (Melachim I 6:10) is that he roofed it with cedar beams, which Targum Yonasan renders וְטַלֵּיל יַת בֵּיתָא; and he called it a taking hold because the beams take hold of this wall and of the wall opposite, as it also says לְבִלְתִּי אֲחֹז בְּקִירוֹת הַבָּיִת (Melachim I 6:6) and וְלֹא יִהְיוּ אֲחוּזִים בְּקִיר הַבָּיִת (Yechezkel 41:6).

תְּנוּ לִי אֲחֻזַּת קֶבֶר (Bereishis 23:4), give me a holding for a burial place, and וְהָיוּ לָכֶם לַאֲחֻזָּה (Vayikra 25:45). An inheritance is called so because a man takes hold in the place and is held by it on its account, as וַיֵּאָחֲזוּ בָהּ (Bereishis 46:27) and וְנֹאחֲזוּ בְתֹכְכֶם (Bamidbar 32:30).

וַאֲחֻזַּת מֵרֵעֵהוּ (Bereishis 26:26) is a man's name; the Mesorah on it is לית שום בר נש, that it is no man's name at all. The Targum's view is וְסִיעַת מְרַחֲמוֹהִי, the company of his friends; and a man's company is called an אחוזה because they hold to him and do not part from him in his going out and his coming in.

כנר.sense: Of the sense he says only that it is known; the entry sets out the word's forms, its plural and its feminine plural.

more.t: כִּנּוֹר וְעוּגָֽב (Bereishis 4:21), kinnor and ugav, and וַיְהִי לְאֵבֶל כִּנֹּרִי (Iyov 30:31), my kinnor is turned to mourning. The plural is וְקוֹל כִּנּוֹרַיִךְ לֹא יִשָּׁמַע עֽוֹד (Yechezkel 26:13), the sound of your kinnoros will be heard no more, and in the feminine form וּבְכִנֹּרוֹת וּבִנְבָלִים (Shmuel II 6:5), with kinnoros and nevalim, and תָּלִינוּ כִּנֹּרוֹתֵֽינוּ (Tehillim 137:2), we hung up our kinnoros. Of all of them he says only ידוע, it is known.

יין.sense: Wine. Of the word itself he says only that it is known, and the entry is on how it binds to what comes after it.

more.h: Where a word is left out
more.t: The word stands alone in וְיַיִן לַנֶּסֶךְ רְבִיעִית הַהִין (Bamidbar 15:5), wine for a drink offering, a quarter of a hin, and binds as יֵין: יִשְׁתּוּ יֵין נְסִיכָם (Devarim 32:38), let them drink the wine of their offering. In אֶת־כּוֹס הַיַּיִן הַֽחֵמָה (Yirmiyahu 25:15), the cup of the wine, the wrath, and הִשְׁקִיתָנוּ יַיִן תַּרְעֵלָֽה (Tehillim 60:5), You gave us wine of reeling to drink, the bound word is missing, and one reads היין יֵין החמה, the wine, the wine of wrath, and יין יֵין התרעלה, wine, the wine of reeling. He allows that the qualifying word in one of them may be a description of the wine rather than a noun it is bound to, and then nothing is left out.

כְּיֵין הַטּוֹב (Shir HaShirim 7:10), like the good wine, where the bound form is joined to the description itself, as בְּחֵיל כָּבֵד (Yeshayahu 36:2), with a heavy army, and אֶל־מֵי הַמָּרִֽים (Bamidbar 5:23), to the bitter water.
He finds the plural in the feminine in the words of Chazal, in the Mishnah in Shekalim: יינות, wines, שמנים וסלתות, oils and fine flours.

ינה.sense: To wrong a man in his money, taking what is another's in buying and selling or otherwise, whether he knows of it or not.

more.t: וְלֹא תוֹנוּ אִישׁ אֶת־עֲמִיתוֹ (Vayikra 25:17), you shall not wrong one another, הוֹנוּ בָֽךְ (Yechezkel 22:7), they wronged in you, and וְהַֽאֲכַלְתִּי אֶת־ מוֹנַיִךְ (Yeshayahu 49:26), I will feed those who wrong you. He calls it taking other men's money in a sale or in some other way, with their knowledge or without it.

From the light form, הָעִיר הַיּוֹנָֽה (Tzefaniah 3:1), the oppressing city, מִפְּנֵי חֶרֶב הַיּוֹנָֽה (Yirmiyahu 46:16), before the oppressing sword, and מִפְּנֵי חֲרוֹן הַיּוֹנָה (Yirmiyahu 25:38). Rabbi Yonah takes נִינָם יָחַד (Tehillim 74:8), we will wrong them together, in this sense as well, and Targum Yonasan renders that and the two before it so.

וְלֹֽא־ יוֹנוּ עוֹד נְשִׂיאַי אֶת־עַמִּי (Yechezkel 45:8), my princes will no more wrong my people, which he reads as taking their inheritance by force, and לְהֽוֹנֹתָם מֵֽאֲחֻזָּתָם (Yechezkel 46:18), to wrong them out of their holding. Targum Yonasan renders it so, that the ruler shall not take of the people's inheritance to wrong them out of their own.

Chazal (Bava Metzia 58b) said there is wronging in words as well, and that this is what וְגֵר לֹֽא־ תוֹנֶה (Shemos 22:20), you shall not wrong a ger, means: לֹֽא־תוֹנֶה, do not wrong him, in words, and וְלֹא תִלְחָצֶנּוּ, do not oppress him, in money. One is not to say to a ger, remember your earlier deeds; nor to the son of gerim, remember your fathers' deeds; nor to a Jew who has come back in teshuvah, remember your earlier deeds.
Rabbi Yehudah put וְאַֽחֲרִיתוֹ יִהְיֶה מָנֽוֹן (Mishlei 29:20) in this root and this sense. He holds it more likely from the root נִין.

אכל.sense: To eat; and so fire eating, a land eating its dwellers, the sword eating; all one sense, since eating is itself consuming and destroying.

more.t: וְאָֽכַלְתָּ וְשָׂבָֽעְתָּ (Devarim 11:15), you will eat and be satisfied, and by way of figure אָֽכְלָה וּמָחֲתָה פִיהָ (Mishlei 30:20), she ate and wiped her mouth. The noun is וַיִּתֶּן־ אֹכֶל בֶּֽעָרִים (Bereishis 41:35), he put food in the cities, and in other forms בְּכֹחַ הָֽאֲכִילָה הַהִיא (Melachim I 19:8), by the strength of that eating, and וּמַֽאֲכַל שֻׁלְחָנוֹ (Melachim I 10:5), the food of his table. מַכֹּלֶת לְבֵיתוֹ (Melachim I 5:25), food for his house, is missing its alef, its full form being מַֽאֲכֹלֶת. Of the sense of eating a thing that is food he says only that it is known.

אֵשׁ אֹֽכְלָה הוּא (Devarim 4:24), He is a consuming fire; in the passive וְנֶֽאֱכַל גָּדִישׁ (Shemos 22:18), a stack is consumed, אֻכְּלוּ כְּקַשׁ יָבֵשׁ (Nachum 1:10), they were consumed like dry stubble, and וְהַסְּנֶה אֵינֶנּוּ אֻכָּֽל (Shemos 3:2), the bush was not consumed. The noun is מַֽאֲכֹלֶת אֵֽשׁ (Yeshayahu 9:4), food for the fire, and כְּמַאֲכֹלֶת אֵשׁ (Yeshayahu 9:18).

וְאָֽכַלְתָּ אֶת־כָּל־הָֽעַמִּים (Devarim 6:16), you will consume all the peoples, אָלָה אָכְלָה אֶרֶץ (Yeshayahu 24:6), a curse has devoured the land, and אֶרֶץ אֹכֶלֶת יֽוֹשְׁבֶיהָ (Bamidbar 13:32), a land that eats its dwellers. On הֲלָנֶצַח תֹּאכַל חֶרֶב (Shmuel II 2:26), will the sword devour for ever, he says the verb answers to the sword, as if to say, if your sword eats for ever, as וְחַרְבִּי תֹּאכַל בָּשָׂר (Devarim 32:42), my sword will eat flesh; or else it is eating in earnest, said by way of figure, as the pasuk says the sword is filled with blood and made fat with fat (Yeshayahu 34:6).

חֶרֶב תְּאֻכְּלוּ (Yeshayahu 1:20), which he reads as בחרב תאכלו, by the sword you will be eaten: if you listen you will eat the good of the land, and if you refuse you will not be eaters but eaten by the sword.

כִּֽי־ יֽוֹכְלוּ אַתִּיקִים מֵהֵנָה (Yechezkel 42:5), which he glosses as their taking up the corners from them, and so Targum Yonasan renders. In the language of Chazal too (Bava Basra 14a), כמה לוחות אוכלות בארון, how much room the luchos take up in the Aron.

more.h: The knife, and all one sense
more.t: The knife is called מאכלת because it eats and makes an end: וַיִּקַּח אֶת־ הַֽמַּֽאֲכֶלֶת (Bereishis 22:10), he took the knife, and in the plural וּֽמַֽאֲכָלוֹת מְֽתַלְּעֹתָיו (Mishlei 30:14), his jaw teeth are knives. All that come from this root are one sense, he says, since eating bread and any food is itself consuming, burning and destroying. His father writes that לְהָכִיל לְמַעַן בָּרָֽק (Yechezkel 21:33) is of this root and this sense, its proper form being להאכיל, to feed.

סכן.sense: To be of use, to profit; and separately being accustomed to a thing, an officer set over stores, warming, and מִסְכֵּן, a poor man.

more.t: הוֹכֵחַ בְּדָבָר לֹא יִסְכּוֹן (Iyov 15:3), arguing with a word that does not profit, and כִּֽי־תֹאמַר מַה־ יִּסְכָּן ־לָךְ (Iyov 35:3), for you say, what does it profit you. הַלְאֵל יִסְכָּן ־גָּבֶר (Iyov 22:2) he reads as, can a man profit Hashem by his righteousness and the uprightness of his deeds, since he profits himself alone and not Hashem. Ibn Ezra reads the same words as reproof: can a man reprove Hashem, or will a wise man reprove between the two.

הַסְכֶּן ־נָא עִמּוֹ וּשְׁלָם (Iyov 22:21), where he says the verb takes an object with the word דְּרָכֶיךָ, your ways, understood: let your ways profit with Him, and be at peace. So too וְֽכָל־דְּרָכַי הִסְכַּֽנְתָּה (Tehillim 139:3), which he glosses as הועלת, You profited, that is, You put profit in them.

In another sense, הַֽהַסְכֵּן הִסְכַּנְתִּי (Bamidbar 22:30), which he glosses as ההרגל הרגלתי, the habit, I was accustomed. He allows הַסְכֶּן־נָא עִמּוֹ, be of use with Him, to be read this way as well, be accustomed with Him so as to be with Him always; and some read וְֽכָל־דְּרָכַי הִסְכַּֽנְתָּה so too, You are accustomed to my ways, that is, You know them always.

more.h: Stores, and the one set over them
more.t: בֹּא אֶל־ הַסֹּכֵן הַזֶּה (Yeshayahu 22:15), which he glosses as the one appointed over the treasury, and so עָרֵי מִסְכְּנוֹת (Shemos 1:11), cities of stores, their sense being storehouses. Rabbi Yonah put וּתְהִי־לוֹ סֹכֶנֶת (Melachim I 1:2) here as well, in the sense of stores. Right and straight in his own eyes is that סוכנת means one who is of use, as מַה־יִּסְכָּן־לָךְ, what does it profit you; she is to be of use to him against the cold, which is why the pasuk goes on וְשָֽׁכְבָה בְחֵיקֶךָ, and she will lie in your bosom.

Others explained סוכנת as one who warms, and the same words of the pasuk bear it out: he did not know her, but she warmed him and lay with him, since she was forbidden to him by לא ירבה לו נשים, he shall not take many wives, and he already had eighteen. On this he reads בּוֹקֵעַ עֵצִים יִסָּכֶן בָּֽם (Koheles 10:9) as warming himself with them in the labour of them, and he notes that in Arabic a hot thing is called by this word.

Some read יִסָּכֶן בם from סכנה, danger, on the strength of how much Chazal use the word: the Mishnah in Gittin has המפרש והיוצא בשיירא, one who sets out to sea and one who goes with a caravan, and והמסוכן, the man in danger, and the Mishnah in Chullin השוחט את המסוכנת, one who slaughters a beast at the point of death. הַֽמְסֻכָּן תְּרוּמָה (Yeshayahu 40:20) Rabbi Yonah put with the storehouses; he himself takes it from טוֹב יֶלֶד מִסְכֵּן (Koheles 4:13), better a poor youth, and הָאִישׁ הַמִּסְכֵּן (Koheles 9:15), the poor man, since the Targum of עָנִי (Devarim 24:12), poor, is מִסְכֵּן. So the pasuk speaks of the poor man who cannot make his idol of silver and gold as the rich do (Yeshayahu 40:19), and so seeks out wood that will not rot. The noun of this sense is אֶרֶץ אֲשֶׁר לֹא בְמִסְכֵּנֻת (Devarim 8:9), a land where there is no poverty.

חלד.sense: Time, a man's span or the age he lives in; and separately an animal named beside the mouse, which Chazal call חולדה, the chuldah.

more.t: מִֽמְתִים מֵחֶלֶד (Tehillim 17:14), pointed בשש נקודות, with six dots, which he glosses as אנשי הזמן, the men of the age; וְחֶלְדִּי כְאַיִן נֶגְדֶּךָ (Tehillim 19:6), my time is as nothing before You; זְכָר־אֲנִי מֶה־ חָלֶד (Tehillim 89:48), what my time is; הַֽאֲזִינוּ כָּל־ישְׁבֵי חָֽלֶד (Tehillim 49:2), the men of the age; and וּֽמִצָּהֳרַיִם יָקוּם חָלֶד (Iyov 11:17), which he reads as your time rising and growing brighter than noon.
הַחֹלֶד וְהָֽעַכְבָּר (Vayikra 11:29), the choled and the mouse. It is the one Chazal (Pesachim 9a) call חולדה, the chuldah, and in la'az מושתיל"א.

חדל.sense: To cease, to leave off what one was doing; and separately חָדֶל as a word for the age, which he calls a turning about of חֶלֶד, time.

more.t: עַד כִּֽי־ חָדַל לִסְפֹּר (Bereishis 41:49), until he ceased counting; חָֽדְלוּ גִבּוֹרֵי בָבֶל לְהִלָּחֵם (Yirmiyahu 51:30), the mighty men of Bavel ceased fighting; הַקֹּלוֹת יֶחְדָּלוּן (Shemos 9:29), the thunder will cease; חֲדַל מִמֶּנּוּ וְנַֽעַבְדָה אֶת־מִצְרָיִם (Shemos 14:12), leave us be and let us serve Mitzrayim; and מֵֽחֲדֹל לְהִתְפַּלֵּל בַּֽעַדְכֶם (Shmuel I 12:23), from ceasing to daven for you. Where what ceased is a doing he supplies it: חָדְלוּ רֹגֶז (Iyov 3:16), which he glosses as חדלו מעשות רוגז, they ceased from making rage.

The description is חָדֵל, ceasing, as וַֽחֲדַל אִישִׁים (Yeshayahu 53:3), ceasing of men; and where the verb takes an object, הֶֽחֳדַלְתִּי אֶת־דִּשְׁנִי (Shoftim 9:9), shall I leave off my fatness, where the chet takes a kamatz for the beauty of the thing.

עִם־יוֹשְׁבֵי חָֽדֶל (Yeshayahu 38:11), which he glosses as יושבי הזמן, the dwellers of the age, and calls a turning about of מִֽמְתִים מֵחֶלֶד (Tehillim 17:14), the men of the age. The description from it is מֶה־ חָדֵל אָֽנִי (Tehillim 39:5), what my span is; and some read שְׁעֵה מֵעָלָיו וְיֶחְדָּל (Iyov 14:6) in this sense.

טוב.sense: Good; and so rich and full, and fair of appearance. He takes טוֹב, good, for the description and טוּב, goodness, for the noun.

more.t: מַה־ טֹּבוּ אֹֽהָלֶיךָ יַֽעֲקֹב (Bamidbar 24:5), how good are your tents, Yaakov; וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים אֶת־הָאוֹר כִּי־ טוֹב (Bereishis 1:4), Hashem saw the light, that it was good; הֲטוֹבָה הִוא אִם־רָעָה (Bamidbar 13:19), is it good or bad; צַדִּקִים וְטֹבִים מִמֶּנּוּ (Melachim I 2:32), more righteous and better than he; and הֱטִיבוֹתָ כִּי הָיָה עִם־לְבָבֶֽךָ, you did well that it was in your heart.

וַנִּשְׂבַּֽע־לֶחֶם וַנִּֽהְיֶה טוֹבִים (Yirmiyahu 44:17), we had our fill of bread and were well, which he glosses as עשירים ומלאים, rich and full. כִּי טֹבֹת הֵנָּה (Bereishis 6:2), that they were good, he glosses as יפות, beautiful, and שֶׁבַע פָּרֹת הַטֹּבֹת (Bereishis 41:26), the seven good cows, as שמנות ויפות, fat and fair. So too בָּחוּר וָטוֹב (Shmuel I 9:2), a young man and good, and וְאֵין אִישׁ מִבְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל טוֹב מִמֶּנּוּ, no man of Yisrael better than he, which he glosses as fair of appearance, as Targum Yonasan renders שַׁפִּיר, fair.

טוֹבָתִי בַּל־עָלֶֽיךָ (Tehillim 16:2), my good is not upon You, and without the heh וְהָיָה הַטּוֹב הַהוּא (Bamidbar 10:32), and that good will be. When it is bound the cholam turns to a shuruk: וְרַב־ טוּב לְבֵית יִשְׂרָאֵל (Yeshayahu 63:7), great goodness to the house of Yisrael, טוּב הָאָרֶץ תֹּאכֵֽלוּ (Yeshayahu 1:19), you will eat the good of the land, and אֲנִי אַֽעֲבִיר כָּל־ טוּבִי עַל־פָּנֶיךָ (Shemos 33:19), I will pass all My goodness before you.

He holds טוֹב with the cholam a description and טוּב with the shuruk a noun, the same word whether bound or standing alone, and that this is the right account, since מִבְחַר וְטֽוֹב ־לְבָנוֹן (Yechezkel 31:16), the choice and the good of Levanon, is bound and still keeps the cholam.

שׁפר.sense: To be fair and pleasing; the שׁוֹפָר, of which he says only that it is known; and אֶשְׁפָּר, which he takes as a portion of meat.

more.t: אַף־נַֽחֲלָת שָֽׁפְרָה עָלָֽי (Tehillim 16:6), my inheritance is pleasing to me, and הַנֹּתֵן אִמְרֵי־ שָֽׁפֶר (Bereishis 49:21), who gives goodly words. The Targum of יְפֵה־תֹאַר (Bereishis 39:6), fair of form, is שַׁפִּיר בְּרֵיוָא, fair in appearance, and so in Aramaic מִלְכִּי יִשְׁפַּר עֲלָיךְ (Daniel 4:24), let my counsel be pleasing to you.

בְּרוּחוֹ שָׁמַיִם שִׁפְרָה (Iyov 26:13), by His wind the heavens were made fair. He weighs several accounts: the beis of ברוחו, by His wind, is added, or the heh of שפרה is; or the root is of four letters, on the pattern of מְתַֽחֲרֶה בָאָרֶז (Yirmiyahu 22:15), vying with the cedar; or, as some explain, שִׁפְרָה means He spread them like a tent, from שַׁפְרִירוֹ (Yirmiyahu 43:10), his tent, the heh standing in place of the doubled letter, as בָּֽזְאוּ נְהָרִים (Yeshayahu 18:2) stands for בזזו, they plundered.

שׁוֹפַר תְּרוּעָה (Vayikra 25:9), a shofar of teruah, and שֽׁוֹפְרוֹת הַיּֽוֹבְלִים (Yehoshua 6:4), the shofros of the yovel, of which he says only that they are known. כַּשּׁוֹפָר הָרֵם קוֹלֶךָ (Yeshayahu 58:1) he reads as, raise your voice as you would were you blowing a shofar.

וְאֶשְׁפָּר אֶחָד (Shmuel II 6:19), one eshpar, where the alef is added and the word means a portion of meat; he suggests it may be drawn from the first sense, a fair portion. Chazal (Pesachim 36b) made it a word compounded of three, אחד מששה בפר, one of six in a bull.

ריח.sense: To smell; and by extension to sense a thing. He allows that רֵחַיִם, the millstones, may be of this root as well.

more.t: אַף לָהֶם וְלֹא יְרִיחֽוּן (Tehillim 115:6), they have a nose and do not smell; אֶת־רֵיחַ הַנִּיחֹחַ (Bereishis 8:21), the sweet savour, which Hashem smelled; and וְלֹא אָרִיחַ בְּרֵיחַ נִיחֹֽחֲכֶֽם (Vayikra 26:31), I will not smell your sweet savours. Of the sense itself he says only that it is known.

וּמֵרָחוֹק יָרִיחַ מִלְחָמָה (Iyov 39:25), from afar he smells the battle, which he takes by way of widening for sensing; so too בַּהֲרִיחוֹ אֵשׁ (Shoftim 16:9), when it senses fire. On וַֽהֲרִיחוֹ (Yeshayahu 11:3), his smelling in the fear of Hashem, he says that by the least hint he will know that a man is righteous, which is why the pasuk goes on that he will not judge by the sight of his eyes, smell being the lightest of the senses.

He allows רחים, millstones, to be of this root: לֹא־יַֽחֲבֹל רֵחַיִם וָרָכֶב (Devarim 24:6), he shall not take the millstones or the upper stone in pledge, and קְחִי רֵחַיִם וְטַֽחֲנִי קָמַח (Yeshayahu 47:2), take the millstones and grind meal. Since they are two stones the word is said in the dual. On one account the lower stone alone is the רחים, millstones, being the larger and the main part of the work of the two, and the upper is called רֶכֶב, the upper stone.

He allows further that the word is said of the two together and not of the lower alone, since the lower by itself is called שֶׁכֶב, the lower stone, as the upper is called רֶכֶב, the upper stone, and so the Mishnah in Bava Basra keeps the millstones three from the lower stone, which is four from the upper. On that reading the pasuk forbids taking the two in pledge, and even the upper alone, since the work is not done but by both together; it named the upper because it is the easier of the two to take, the lower being fixed in place.

תמר.sense: The palm, which he describes as even and straight, with no branches until its crown; and so anything tall and straight, smoke included.

more.t: זֹאת קֽוֹמָתֵךְ דָּֽמְתָה לְתָמָר (Shir HaShirim 7:8), your stature is like a palm, גַּם־ תָּמָר וְתַפּוּחַ (Yoel 1:12), the palm and the apple too, and וְשִׁבְעִים תְּמָרִים (Shemos 15:27), seventy palms, of which he says only that they are known.

כְּתֹמֶר מִקְשָׁה (Yirmiyahu 10:5), which he explains as a palm that is even and straight, since the palm puts out no branches until high up at its crown, and all its trunk below is even and straight. And with a cholam, וְהִיא יוֹשֶׁבֶת תַּֽחַת־ תֹּמֶר (Shoftim 4:5), she sat under a palm.

וְתִֽמֹרָה בֵּין־כְּרוּב לִכְרוּב (Yechezkel 41:14), a palm figure between one keruv and the next, מִקְלְעוֹת כְּרוּבִים וְתִמֹרֹת (Melachim I 6:29), carvings of keruvim and palm figures, and וְאֶל־אַיִל תִּֽמֹרִֽים (Yechezkel 40:16), palm figures on the post. Some of them Targum Yonasan renders צורת דקלים, the form of palms, and some כוֹתְרָן, crowns.

וְתִֽימְרוֹת עשׁן (Yoel 3:3), columns of smoke. Because the palm is a tall straight tree, a tall straight thing is likened to it, as עַמּוּד עָשָׁן (Shoftim 20:40), a pillar of smoke, and as Chazal speak of smoke, משתעלה העשן תמרתו, once its column of smoke goes up. They said too (Yoma 38a) that the house of Avtinas were expert in the ketores and would not teach it, and that craftsmen brought from Alexandria of Mitzrayim could compound as they did but could not raise the smoke as they did: theirs went up in a column, straight as a stick, while the others' scattered this way and that.

ענג.sense: To take delight; its sense, he says, is a man delighting himself, and pleasantness in the enjoyment of the soul.

more.t: וְהִתְעַנַּגְתֶּם מִזִּיז כְּבוֹדָֽהּ (Yeshayahu 66:11), you will delight in the abundance of her glory; וְהִתְעַנְּגוּ עַל־רֹב שָׁלֽוֹם (Tehillim 37:11), they will delight in abundant peace; וְתִתְעַנַּג בַּדֶּשֶׁן נַפְשְׁכֶֽם (Yeshayahu 55:2), let your soul delight in fatness; and מֵֽהִתְעַנֵּג וּמֵרֹךְ (Devarim 28:56), from delicacy and from tenderness.

בְּהֵיכְלֵי עֹנֶג (Yeshayahu 13:22), palaces of delight; with a tav added, לֹֽא־נָאוֶה לִכְסִיל תַּֽעֲנוּג (Mishlei 19:10), delight is not fitting for a fool, and in the feminine plural וְתַֽעֲנֻגוֹת בְּנֵי הָאָדָם (Koheles 2:8), the delights of men. The description is וְהֶֽעָנֹג מְאֹד (Devarim 28:54), the very delicate man, and הָֽרַכָּה בְךָ וְהָֽעֲנֻגָּה (Devarim 28:56), the tender and delicate woman among you.

פנק.sense: To pamper: מְפַנֵּק מִנֹּעַר עַבְדּוֹ (Mishlei 29:21), one who pampers his servant from his youth.

more.t: One line. He glosses מְפַנֵּק as מענגו ומעדנו, giving him delight and delicacy, and notes that the Targum of מַֽעֲדַנֵּי־מֶֽלֶךְ (Bereishis 49:20), royal delicacies, is תַפְנוּקֵי מַלְכִין, the delights of kings.

זבל.sense: To dwell with; a dwelling is called זבול, and from it the house built for Hashem is a בֵּית זְבֻל, a house of dwelling.

more.t: הַפַּעַם יִזְבְּלֵנִי אִישִׁי (Bereishis 30:20), which he glosses as ידור עמי, he will dwell with me, since a dwelling is called זבול; בָּנֹה בָנִיתִי בֵּית זְבֻל לָךְ (Melachim I 8:13), I have built You a house of dwelling; and with a heh added, שֶׁמֶשׁ יָרֵחַ עָמַד זְבֻלָה (Chavakuk 3:11), the sun and the moon stood in their dwelling.

ארם.sense: אַרְמוֹן, a palace, which he explains as the great and high house; most of the entry is on the forms of its plural.

more.t: כִּֽי־ אַרְמוֹן נֻטָּשׁ (Yeshayahu 32:14), the palace is forsaken, and וְאַרְמוֹן עַל־מִשְׁפָּטוֹ יֵשֵֽׁב (Yirmiyahu 30:18), the palace will stand where it should, on the pattern of פַּֽעֲמוֹן, a bell. The plural is feminine, אַרְמְנוֹת בֶּן־הֲדָֽד (Amos 1:4), the palaces of Ben Hadad, and וְאָכְלָה אַרְמְנֹתֶֽיהָ (Amos 1:7), it will devour her palaces, where the cholam falls away. That is either because the word is bound, since unbound one says אַרְמוֹנוֹת, palaces, or, and this he holds right, because it is another pattern altogether, one that does not change when bound; and indeed עַל־ אַרְמְנוֹת בְּאַשְׁדּוֹד (Amos 3:9), on the palaces in Ashdod, is not bound and still has the sheva, unless such forms are bound to the serving letter, as the language does in places.

וְהִשְׁלַכְתֶּנָה הַֽהַרְמוֹנָה (Amos 4:3), with a heh in place of the alef. Its sense is the great and high house, and he allows that the alef of the word is itself added, saying he will bring it again at the root רום, to be high. Targum Yonasan renders that phrase וְיִגְלוּן יַתְהוֹן לְהָלְאָא מִן טוּרֵי חַרְמִינֵי, they will exile them beyond the mountains of Charmini; he renders מִנִּי וְאַשְׁכְּנַז (Yirmiyahu 51:27), Minni and Ashkenaz, as הוּרְמִינֵי, Hurmini; and he renders וּלְמִנִּי מָצוֹר וְעַד־נָהָר (Michah 7:12), and from Matzor and to the river, with חוּרְמִינִי רַבְּתָא, greater Churmini.

פכה.sense: Water flowing out; and from it the flask called פך, since the oil is brought out and poured from it.

more.t: One line, on וְהִנֵּה־מַיִם מְפַכִּים (Yechezkel 47:2), which he glosses as יוצאים, coming out; and from this, he says, the flask of oil is called פך, since they bring out and pour the oil from it.

אפל.sense: Darkness; because the pasuk sets חשֶׁךְ וַֽאֲפֵלָה, darkness and gloom, side by side, the gloom seems to be more than the darkness.

more.t: בַּֽאֲפֵלוֹת נְהַלֵּֽךְ (Yeshayahu 59:9), we walk in thick darkness, and the adjective וְאָפֵל וְלֹֽא־נֹגַֽהּ לֽוֹ (Amos 5:20), dark with no brightness to it. Another form is וַתֹּפַע כְּמוֹ־ אֹֽפֶל (Iyov 10:22), and a third is מַֽאֲפֵל, as וַיָּשֶׂם מַֽאֲפֵל בֵּינֵיכֶם וּבֵין הַמִּצְרִים (Yehoshua 24:7), He put darkness between you and the Egyptians.

אֶרֶץ מַאְפֵּלְיָה (Yirmiyahu 2:31): in all books it is one word, but its sense is two, and some exact books point it מְאַפֵּלְיָה. The divine Name is attached to it because the darkness is so great, as שַׁלְהֶבֶתְיָֽה (Shir HaShirim 8:6) is for the greatness of the flame. So with anything a man wishes to magnify: כְּֽהַרְרֵי־אֵל (Tehillim 36:7), the mountains of Hashem, עִיר־גְּדוֹלָה לֵֽאלֹהִים (Yonah 3:3), a city great to Hashem, and וַתְּהִי לְחֶרְדַּת אֱלֹהִֽים (Shmuel I 14:15). Or the yud is a relative ending and the word is an adjective for the land, like the yud of תחתיה, the lower, and שׁלישׁיה, the third.

כִּי אֲפִילֹת הֵֽנָּה (Shemos 9:32): dark and hidden under the ground, or else late in coming up. Chazal use the word so in הא בחרפי הא באפלי, this of the early and this of the late, and in speaking of a year that was אפלה, a late year, in which the growths were not to be made out.

מות.sense: To die, and to be dead; the noun מָוֶת, death; and where the verb takes an object, to put a man to death.

more.t: וַיָּמָת לִבּוֹ בְּקִרְבּוֹ (Shmuel I 25:37), his heart died within him: he was struck dumb and was as a dead man, or else he died outright. וַיָּמָת תַּחְתָּיו מִפְּנֵי הָֽרָעָב (Yirmiyahu 38:9) he glosses קרוב למות, near to death. And לָמָּה נָמוּת לְעֵינֶיךָ (Bereishis 47:19) is said of the ground as well, for ground lying waste is like a dead thing, not bringing out grass and fruit trees as it should.

בִּשְׁנַת־ מוֹת הַמֶּלֶךְ עֻזִּיָּהוּ (Yeshayahu 6:1): Chazal explained it as the year he was struck with tzaraas, as אַל־נָא תְהִי כַּמֵּת (Bamidbar 12:12), let her not be as one dead; and so Targum Yonasan, בְּשַׁתָּא דְאִתְנַגַע בָּהּ מַלְכָּא, in the year the king was stricken.

more.h: Why death comes in the plural
more.t: מְמוֹתֵי תַֽחֲלֻאִים יָמֻתוּ (Yirmiyahu 16:4) and מְמוֹתֵי חָלָל בְּלֵב יַמִּֽים (Yechezkel 28:8). Death is spoken of in the plural because a man is sometimes put to death by many stabs, or by hard sufferings; and one who drowns does not die at one stroke. So too מוֹתֵי עֲרֵלִים תָּמוּת בְּיַד־זָרִים (Yechezkel 28:10) and בְּנֵי תְמוּתָֽה (Tehillim 79:11).

Targum Yonasan renders וּכְבוֹדוֹ מְתֵי רָעָב (Yeshayahu 5:13) as וְיַקִירֵהוֹן מִיתוּ בְכַפְנָא, their honoured men died of hunger, taking the word from this root. By the way of grammar that is not sound, because of the sheva under the mem.

more.h: Chastening a son, not killing him
more.t: Some explain וְאֶל־ הֲמִיתוֹ אַל־תִּשָּׂא נַפְשֶֽׁךָ (Mishlei 19:18) from this root: chasten your son gently, not so as to kill him with blows. He has already explained the pasuk at the root הָמָה.

פטר.sense: To let go: to release, to dismiss, to open; and the firstborn is פֶּטֶר כָּל־רֶחֶם, the opening of every womb.

more.t: וַיִּפְטַר מִפְּנֵי שָׁאוּל (Shmuel I 19:10), he got away from before Shaul, where the verb does nothing to anything else. Where it takes an object it is to dismiss: כִּי לֹֽא־ פָטַר יְהֽוֹיָדָע הַכֹּהֵן אֶת־הַמַּחְלְקֽוֹת (Divrei HaYamim II 23:5), he did not send the divisions away nor let them go, but held them back.

The word is common in the Mishnah as פטור, exempt, whose opposite is חייב, liable. So he reads פְּטוּרִים in Divrei HaYamim I 9:33: exempt from other work, since they were busy with the work of song day and night and sat in the chambers.

פּוֹטֵֽר מַיִם רֵאשִׁית מָדוֹן (Mishlei 17:14): like one who lets the water go and opens it at the start, and it runs where no man can bring it back; so is the beginning of a quarrel. And יַפְטִירוּ בְשָׂפָה (Tehillim 22:8), they let the words out with the lip and open them.

פֶּטֶר כָּל־רֶחֶם (Shemos 13:2) and פִּטְרַת כָּל־רֶחֶם (Bamidbar 8:16) are ענין השלוח והפתיחה, a sense of sending out and of opening; the Targum renders וְהָֽאֲנָשִׁים שֻׁלְּחוּ (Bereishis 44:3), the men were sent away, with וְגֻבְרַיָּא אִתְפַּטָּרוּ. The firstborn is called so because he is the sending out of the womb, its opening and its first breaking through, and so וּפְטוּרֵי צִצִּים (Melachim I 6:19), where the buds and blossoms opened out.

בושׁ.sense: To be ashamed, with בוּשָׁה and בשֶׁת for shame; and in the same letters a second sense, to be long in coming.

more.t: בְּךָ בָטְחוּ וְלֹא־ בֽוֹשׁוּ (Tehillim 22:6), they trusted in You and were not shamed; כִּי בְֹשְׁתִּי לִשְׁאוֹל מִן־הַמֶּלֶךְ (Ezra 8:22), I was ashamed to ask of the king; וְלֹא יִתְבּשָֽׁשׁוּ (Bereishis 2:25), they were not ashamed. He notes that בּוֹשָׁה וְחָפֵרָה (Yirmiyahu 15:9) is stressed on the earlier syllable and וּבוֹשָׁה הַֽחַמָּה (Yeshayahu 24:23) on the last. Where the verb takes an object it is to shame another: עֲצַת־עָנִי תָבִישׁוּ (Tehillim 14:6), you would shame the counsel of the poor, and מֵבִישׁ וּמַחְפִּֽיר (Mishlei 19:26).

בָּשְׁנָה אֶפְרַיִם יִקָּח (Hoshea 10:6). Rabbi Yonah wrote that the nun was added to disgrace the Baal, that it should be called בשנה, as in וְהַבֹּשֶׁת אָֽכְלָה אֶת־יְגִיעַ אֲבוֹתֵינוּ (Yirmiyahu 3:24), the shameful thing devoured our fathers' toil. It can also be taken at its plain sense, as the same pasuk says וְיֵבוֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל מֵֽעֲצָתֽוֹ, Yisrael will be ashamed of its counsel.
וְהֶֽחֱזִיקָה בִּמְבֻשָֽׁיו (Devarim 25:11) are his testicles, which are the place of shame; and עֶרְיָה־ בֹשֶׁת (Michah 1:11) is nakedness uncovered, as וַֽחֲשׂוּפַי שֵׁת (Yeshayahu 20:4).

וַיָּחִילוּ עַד־ בֹּוֹשׁ (Shoftim 3:25) and וַיִּפְצְרוּ־בוֹ עַד־ בֹּשׁ (Melachim II 2:17), they waited, and they pressed him, until it was long; בֹשֵׁשׁ מֹשֶׁה (Shemos 32:1), Moshe was long in coming down, and מַדּוּעַ בֹּשֵׁשׁ רִכְבּוֹ לָבוֹא (Shoftim 5:28), why is his chariot so long in coming. All of these are ענין איחור, a sense of being late.

אחר.sense: Behind and after: אָחוֹר, the back, which is also the west; אַֽחֲרִית, the end of a thing and what comes of it; אַחֵר, another; and the verb, to be late.

more.t: וַיֵּֽלְכוּ אֲחֹרַנִּית (Bereishis 9:23), they went backwards. On וְאַתָּה הֲסִבֹּתָ אֶת־לִבָּם אֲחֹֽרַנִּֽית (Melachim I 18:37) Rav Saadiah reads: You have turned their heart, which until now was backward. His father reads it of turning their heart back from the faith of the Baal, since they recognized that its libation was falsehood.

טוֹב אַֽחֲרִית דָּבָר מֵרֵֽאשִׁיתוֹ (Koheles 7:8), the end of a matter is better than its beginning. Reward is called אַֽחֲרִית because it is the close of the deed: כִּי אִם־יֵשׁ אַֽחֲרִית וְתִקְוָתְךָ לֹא תִכָּרֵֽת (Mishlei 23:18), and לָתֵת לָכֶם אַֽחֲרִית וְתִקְוָֽה (Yirmiyahu 29:11), to give you an end and a hope.

Men's children are called אַֽחֲרִית because they are left after them, וְאַֽחֲרִיתָם בַּחֶרֶב אֶהֱרֹג (Amos 9:1), which he says is spoken of the people; so וְלֹא לְאַֽחֲרִיתוֹ (Daniel 11:4), that he did not leave the kingship to his son. In וְאַֽחֲרִיתֵךְ בַּחֶרֶב תִּפּוֹל (Yechezkel 23:25) it is your people: the pasuk had said אַפֵּךְ וְאָזְנַיִךְ, your nose and your ears, a figure for the heads, and the head is first to the people, going out and coming in before them, while the people are the end. Targum Yonasan renders עַמִיךְ, your people.

more.h: The back, and so the west
more.t: The western side is called אָחוֹר, וְאָחוֹר וְֽלֹא־אָבִין לֽוֹ (Iyov 23:8), and the western sea is הַיָּם הָאַֽחֲרוֹן (Devarim 11:24), because the face is the east and the back the west, a man's face being toward the rising of the sun. On that same order the south is called ימין, the right, and the north שמאל, the left. And אַחֵר is another than oneself: וְאִישׁ אַחֵר יִקָּחֶֽנָּה (Devarim 20:7), בְּגָדִים אֲחֵרִים (Vayikra 6:4), other garments.

Of a man whose doings are at the end and in waiting: לַֽמְאַֽחֲרִים עַל־הַיָּיִן (Mishlei 23:30), those who stay all day until evening over the drinking of wine, as מְאַֽחֲרֵי בַנֶּשֶׁף (Yeshayahu 5:11); and so מְאַֽחֲרֵי ־שֶׁבֶת (Tehillim 127:2), busy at their work all day until evening. His father writes that כִּי־בֹא יָבֹא לֹא יְאַחֵֽר (Chavakuk 2:3) is not like these, but means it will not come at the end, from אַֽחֲרִית which is the end, and so Targum Yonasan renders לְאָחֽוֹר (Yeshayahu 42:23) as לְסוֹפָא, at the end.

Rabbi Yonah brought a further sense into this root for יִרְבּוּ עַצְּבוֹתָם אַחֵר מָהָרוּ (Tehillim 16:4), reading it as a prayer that the sorrows of those who hurry to strife may increase. He holds that wrong, since the root מהר is not found in the light form in the sense of haste, only in the sense of a marriage payment, מָהֹר יִמְהָרֶנָּה לּוֹ לְאִשָּֽׁה (Shemos 22:15). The right reading in his eyes is from the second sense, another: the sorrows of those who pay a marriage price to another god will increase, that is, they give gifts to another god and offer and pour out to it; the close of the pasuk proves it, בַּל־אַסִּיךְ נִסְכֵּיהֶם מִדָּם, I will not pour out their libations of blood.

נכר.sense: To recognize; and in the same letters its opposite, to disown and make oneself strange, with נֵכָר and נָכְרִי for the foreign and the foreigner.

more.t: וְלֹא הִכִּירוֹ כִּֽי־הָיוּ יָדָיו (Bereishis 27:23), he did not know him because his hands were so; וְאֵינָם מַכִּירִים לְדַבֵּר יְהוּדִית (Nechemiah 13:24), they did not know how to speak Yehudis; and of showing a face favour, לֹֽא־ תַכִּירוּ פָנִים בַּמִּשְׁפָּט (Devarim 1:17), you shall not recognize faces in judgment, and הַֽכֵּר ־פָּנִים לֹֽא־טוֹב (Mishlei 28:21). The noun is הַכָּרַת פְּנֵיהֶם עָנְתָה בָּם (Yeshayahu 3:9). Of all this he says ענין ההכרה ידוע, the sense of recognizing is known.

more.h: The lad known by his doings
more.t: גַּם בְּמַֽעֲלָלָיו יִתְנַכֶּר ־נָעַר (Mishlei 20:11). His father explains it the other way about, not by recognition but by strangeness: the lad makes himself strange by his doings, for if his deed is clean and upright they say this is no lad's doing.

The second sense, the opposite of the first: בְּיוֹם נָכְרוֹ (Ovadiah 1:12); וַֽיְנַכְּרוּ אֶת־הַמָּקוֹם הַזֶּה (Yirmiyahu 19:4), they made this place strange; פֶּן־ יְנַכְּרוּ צָרֵימוֹ (Devarim 32:27); וַיִּתְנַכֵּר אֲלֵיהֶם (Bereishis 42:7), he made himself a stranger to them; וְהִיא מִתְנַכֵּרָֽה (Melachim I 14:5). All of them are ענין ההכחשה והזרות, a sense of denial and of strangeness.

כָּל־בֶּן־ נֵכָר (Shemos 12:43), אֱלֹהֵי נֵֽכַר ־הָאָרֶץ (Devarim 31:16); and with a yud, אִישׁ נָכְרִי (Devarim 17:15), מַלְבּוּשׁ נָכְרִֽי (Tzefaniah 1:8), foreign clothing, הֲלוֹא נָכְרִיּוֹת נֶחְשַׁבְנוּ לוֹ (Bereishis 31:15), are we not reckoned to him as strangers. The right account, he holds, is that נֶכֶר is both a noun and an adjective: in לְאֵל נֵכָֽר (Tehillim 81:10) it is an adjective, and where another word stands in front of it in the construct it is a noun, as וּבְנֵי הַנֵּכָר (Yeshayahu 56:5) and אֱלֹהֵי הַנֵּכָר (Bereishis 35:2).
נִכַּר אֹתוֹ אֱלֹהִים בְּיָדִי (Shmuel I 23:7), which he glosses מסר והסגיר, handed him over and shut him up.

זור.sense: To press or squeeze out; a wound and its healing are both called מָזוֹר; to sneeze; and to be strange, זָר being a stranger.

more.t: וַיָּזַר אֶת־הַגִּזָּה (Shoftim 6:38), he pressed out the fleece; וַתִּשְׁכַּח כִּי־רֶגֶל תְּזוּרֶהָ (Iyov 39:15), that a foot may crush them; וְהַזּוּרֶה תִּבָּקַע אֶפְעֶֽה (Yeshayahu 59:5). Of it he says ענין מעיכה ידוע, the sense of pressing is known.

more.h: A form whose doer is not named
more.t: לֹא־ זֹרוּ וְלֹא חֻבָּשׁוּ (Yeshayahu 1:6): on the view of Rabbi Yehudah the grammarian it is a form whose doer is not named. In his own view it is a past verb standing without an object, on the pattern of מַה־טֹּבוּ אֹֽהָלֶיךָ יַֽעֲקֹב (Bamidbar 24:5); and though it is past in the light form, so we find אָז הָֽלְמוּ עִקְּבֵי־סוּס (Shoftim 5:22). On זֹרוּ רְשָׁעִים מֵרָחֶם (Tehillim 58:4) he says it may be a light past or, on Rabbi Yonah's view, a form whose doer is not named.

more.h: מָזוֹר, the wound and the cure
more.t: A blow is called מָזוֹר because it is pressed: וְלֹֽא־יִגְהֶה מִכֶּם מָזֽוֹר (Hoshea 5:13), and וַיַּרְא אֶפְרַיִם אֶת־חָלְיוֹ וִֽיהוּדָה אֶת־ מְזֹרוֹ (Hoshea 5:13), Efrayim saw his sickness and Yehudah his wound. The healing is called מָזוֹר too, since healing comes by pressing the wound, as לֹא־ זֹרוּ וְלֹא חֻבָּשׁוּ (Yeshayahu 1:6); so אֵֽין־דָּן דִּינֵךְ לְמָזוֹר (Yirmiyahu 30:13), none judges your cause for healing.

וַיְזוֹרֵר הַנַּעַר (Melachim II 4:35), the lad sneezed, which he gives in the vernacular, and the Targum of עֲטִישֹׁתָיו תָּהֶל אוֹר (Iyov 41:10) is זְרִירוֹי. This too is near the first sense, since a man in sneezing presses himself.

רוּחִֽי זָרָה לְאִשְׁתִּי (Iyov 19:17), my spirit is strange to my wife; לֹא־ זָרוּ מִתַּֽאֲוָתָם (Tehillim 78:30), they did not turn away from their craving; לְאִישׁ זָר (Vayikra 22:12), a stranger; מוּזָר הָיִיתִי לְאֶחָי (Tehillim 69:9), I was a stranger to my brothers; נָזֹרוּ אָחֽוֹר (Yeshayahu 1:4), they turned away backward; and וְהָיָה לָכֶם לְזָרָא (Bamidbar 11:20), where the alef stands in place of a heh.
