כִּסְּתָה כְלִמָּה פָנָי (Tehillim 69:8), disgrace has covered my face, and in the plural מִכְּלִמּוֹת וָרֹק (Yeshayahu 50:6), from disgrace and spitting; in another pattern וּכְלִמּוּת עוֹלָם אֲשֶׁר לֹא תִשָּׁכֵחַ (Yirmiyahu 23:40), everlasting disgrace that is not forgotten.
גַּם הַכְלִים לֹא יָדָעוּ (Yirmiyahu 6:15), they did not even know how to be disgraced: they felt nothing when a man put them to shame for the evil of their deeds.

חרף.sense: To revile a man by laying his faults open; also to expose oneself, and to be designated; and in another sense, the winter.

more.t: עַם חֵרֵף נַפְשׁוֹ לָמוּת (Shoftim 5:18), a people that laid its life open to death: they showed themselves in the battle to die, and so בְּחָרְפָם בַּפְּלִשְׁתִּים (Shmuel II 23:9). Others take that one as sharpening, in the way of וְכִלְיוֹתַי אֶשְׁתּוֹנָן (Tehillim 73:21), my heart grown hot and sharpened against them. The Targum renders אֲשֶׁר חִצָּיו שְׁנוּנִים (Yeshayahu 5:28), whose arrows are sharpened, and כְּחֶרֶב חַדָּה (Yeshayahu 49:2), like a sharp sword, with words from these letters, and Chazal speak of a sharp knife. By the Targum's own reading of בְּחָרְפָם בַּפְּלִשְׁתִּים it is a word of reviling, as he renders חֶרְפָּה (Bereishis 34:14) too.

חֵרַפְתִּי אֶת מַעַרְכוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל (Shmuel I 17:10), I have taunted the ranks of Yisrael, אֶת מִי חֵרַפְתָּ וְגִדַּפְתָּ (Yeshayahu 37:23), whom have you taunted and blasphemed, and כִּי לֹא אוֹיֵב יְחָרְפֵנִי (Tehillim 55:13), it is no enemy who taunts me. He ties this to a word of clearing away, since reviling is the uncovering of a man's blemishes and the publishing of them. The noun is חֶרְפָּה שָׁבְרָה לִבִּי (Tehillim 69:21), disgrace has broken my heart.

וְהִוא שִׁפְחָה נֶחֱרֶפֶת לְאִישׁ (Vayikra 19:20): designated for a man and known to be his, and Chazal use the word this way. They read the pasuk of a Canaanite maidservant half slave and half free betrothed to an eved ivri, and that is why it says וְהָפְדֵּה לֹא נִפְדָּתָה (Vayikra 19:20), redeemed and not redeemed.

לֹא יֶחֱרַף לְבָבִי (Iyov 27:6): some take it from בִּימֵי חָרְפִּי (Iyov 29:4), which means the days of my youth. His father reads it as drawing back, my heart will not go back on what I said, that I have not sinned, and he brings the Arabic word for a thing that draws back.

וְקַיִץ וָחֹרֶף (Bereishis 8:22), summer and winter, בֵּית הַחֹרֶף (Amos 3:15), the winter house, and מֵחֹרֶף עָצֵל לֹא יַחֲרֹשׁ (Mishlei 20:4), the sluggard will not plough because of the winter. So וְכָל בֶּהֱמַת הָאָרֶץ עָלָיו תֶּחֱרָף (Yeshayahu 18:6): every beast of the land will stand there through the winter days.

כרה.sense: To dig; and in other senses, to buy a thing, and to set out a great meal.

more.t: בּוֹר כָּרָה וַיַּחְפְּרֵהוּ (Tehillim 7:16), he dug a pit and hollowed it out; כִּי יִכְרֶה אִישׁ בֹּר (Shemos 21:33), if a man digs a pit; כֹּרֶה שַּׁחַת (Mishlei 26:27), one who digs a trap. אָזְנַיִם כָּרִיתָ לִּי (Tehillim 9:7 in his edition) he reads as ears dug open for me to hear, since burnt offering and sin offering You did not ask, in the way of הִנֵּה שְׁמֹעַ מִזֶּבַח טוֹב (Shmuel I 15:22), to listen is better than sacrifice.

בְּקִבְרִי אֲשֶׁר כָּרִיתִי לִי (Bereishis 50:5), in my grave that I dug for myself: it may be that Yaakov dug and hollowed his grave in his lifetime. Others take it from the sense of buying, and though Avraham bought the place it is as if Yaakov bought it, or because he bought Esav's share for a pot of lentils.

וּמִכְרֵה מֶלַח (Tzefaniah 2:9), a salt pit, and נְוֹת כְּרֹת רֹעִים (Tzefaniah 2:6), the place shepherds dig to pen their flocks. He allows also that וּמִכְרֵה מֶלַח is a mound of salt, like the word כרי that Chazal use for a heap of grain, in the blessing they say when a man begins to measure it.

וַיִּכְרֶה לָהֶם כֵּרָה גְדוֹלָה (Melachim II 6:23), he made them a great feast, and יִכְרוּ עָלָיו חַבָּרִים (Iyov 40:30), the fishermen feast over him, are a sense of eating. At לְהַכְרוֹת אֶת דָּוִד (Shmuel II 3:35) the word is written with a kaf and read with a beis, and Chazal take both: first to feed him a little, and at the end much. Menachem ben Saruk and Rabbi Yehudah wrote that the kaf is what is written, but he says he found it so in no accurate sefer he had seen, and Rabbi Yonah wrote that he too found it written so in no accurate sefer. His father writes in Sefer HaGalui that כָּרָה is the large meal and בָרָה the small one, so that Chazal mean they pressed him first to eat a little, as in וְאֶבְרֶה מִיָּדָהּ (Shmuel II 13:6), the little a sick man eats, and afterwards to eat much.

וְגַם מַיִם תִּכְרוּ מֵאִתָּם (Devarim 2:6), you shall buy water from them, and וָאֶכְּרֶהָ לִּי (Hoshea 3:2), I bought her for myself; the nouns וְנָתַתִּי מִכְרָם (Bamidbar 20:19), I will pay their price, and וְרָחֹק מִפְּנִינִים מִכְרָהּ (Mishlei 31:10), her worth is far above pearls. He allows that עַל מִכְרָם בַּכֶּסֶף צַדִּיק (Amos 2:6), the righteous sold for silver, belongs here too, since elsewhere the pasuk says לִקְנוֹת בַּכֶּסֶף דַּלִּים (Amos 8:6), to buy the poor for silver.

חצב.sense: To hew and quarry, cutting stone out of the rock; he glosses the whole root as cutting, in the way of carving.

more.t: וְגַם יֶקֶב חָצֵב בּוֹ (Yeshayahu 5:2), he hewed a winepress in it; וּבֹרֹת חֲצוּבִים (Devarim 6:11), hewn cisterns; כִּי חָצַבְתָּ לְּךָ פֹּה קָבֶר (Yeshayahu 22:16), that you have hewn yourself a grave here; and תַּחְצֹב נְחֹשֶׁת (Devarim 8:9), from whose hills you may hew copper. In the passive, לָעַד בַּצּוּר יֵחָצְבוּן (Iyov 19:24), cut into the rock forever, and הַבִּיטוּ אֶל צוּר חֻצַּבְתֶּם (Yeshayahu 51:1), look to the rock you were hewn from.
עַל כֵּן חָצַבְתִּי בַּנְּבִיאִים (Hoshea 6:5) he takes as a figure for how much He spoke through them, as though He were cutting them to pieces with His words.
וְאַבְנֵי מַחְצֵב (Melachim II 13:13 in his edition), quarried stones; and הַמַּחְצֶבֶת רַהַב (Yeshayahu 51:9), that hewed Rahav down.

ישׁב.sense: To sit, and to dwell; also to stay on in a place, even standing, and to be settled and remain in it.

more.t: אַבְרָם יָשַׁב בְּאֶרֶץ כְּנָעַן (Bereishis 13:12), Avram dwelt in the land of Canaan; וְעֵלִי הַכֹּהֵן יֹשֵׁב עַל הַכִּסֵּא (Shmuel I 1:9), Eli the kohen sitting on the seat; and בַּסֻּכֹּת תֵּשְׁבוּ (Vayikra 23:42), in booths you shall dwell.

אָנֹכִי אֵשֵׁב עַד שׁוּבֶךָ (Shoftim 6:18), I will stay until you return, he glosses as waiting, and so of your having lingered at Kadesh. אַשְׁרֵי יוֹשְׁבֵי בֵיתֶךָ (Tehillim 84:5), happy are those who stay in Your house, holds even of a man on his feet, and so וַיֵּשֶׁב תַּחַת הָאֵלָה (Shoftim 6:11), he sat under the terebinth. He sets out four senses at the close: sitting itself, lingering, a man's long remaining in a place, and standing firm.

לָכֵן קָרָאתִי לָזֹאת רַהַב הֵם שָׁבֶת (Yeshayahu 30:7): since Yisrael go down to Egypt and ask for help that will not avail them, He calls Yerushalayim this, meaning that those who sit in her will be strong and will trust in Hashem rather than go seeking help, for sitting still is more strength to them than going.

more.h: The resident and the hired man
more.t: The word for one who has long remained in a place: כְּשָׂכִיר כְּתוֹשָׁב (Vayikra 25:40), as a hired man and as a resident, and תּוֹשַׁב כֹּהֵן (Vayikra 22:10), a kohen's resident. The תּוֹשָׁב is acquired as a possession forever, the pierced servant; the שָׂכִיר is acquired for a term of years and goes free in the sixth. The resident and hired man spoken of at the Pesach are gentiles and uncircumcised.

מוֹשִׁיב יְחִידִים בַּיְתָה (Tehillim 68:7), He settles the solitary in a house; הוֹשֵׁב אֶת אָבִיךָ וְאֶת אַחֶיךָ (Bereishis 47:6), settle your father and your brothers; and the land itself is spoken of as settled, אֶל אֶרֶץ נוֹשָׁבֶת (Shemos 16:35), to an inhabited land. Rabbi Yonah takes וְכֹל מוֹשַׁב בֵּית צִיבָא עֲבָדִים (Shmuel II 9:12) as a word describing people, all who sat and dwelt in the house of Tziva.

דור.sense: To dwell; a heaped fire; and a generation, the span of a man's life in the world.

more.t: מִדּוּר בְּאָהֳלֵי רֶשַׁע (Tehillim 84:11), than to dwell in the tents of wickedness, is like מגור, and the Targum renders גּוּר (Bereishis 26:3), sojourn, with this word. So דּוֹרִי נִסַּע וְנִגְלָה (Yeshayahu 38:12): my dwelling in this world has been pulled up and carried off.

וְגַם דּוּר הָעֲצָמִים תַּחְתֶּיהָ (Yechezkel 24:5), heap the bones under it, is a command; and the noun אַגְדִּיל הַמְּדוּרָה (Yechezkel 24:9), I will make the pile great, with מְדֻרָתָהּ אֵשׁ וְעֵצִים הַרְבֵּה (Yeshayahu 30:33), its pile is fire and much wood. All of it is a great burning.

דּוֹר הֹלֵךְ וְדוֹר בָּא (Koheles 1:4), a generation goes and a generation comes, with the plurals דּוֹר דּוֹרִים (Tehillim 72:5), generation after generation, and דֹּרוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל (Shoftim 3:2), the generations of Bnei Yisrael. It is taken from the span of a man's life, and he allows דּוֹרִי נִסַּע וְנִגְלָה here as well, the time of my life, holding it one with the first sense: all the days a man dwells in the world are his דּוֹר.

פתח.sense: To open; from it the doorway and the key. Also to loosen and set free, to engrave, and the drawing of a sword.

more.t: וְדַלְתֵי שָׁמַיִם פָּתָח (Tehillim 78:23), He opened the doors of heaven; פּוֹתֵחַ אֶת יָדֶךָ (Tehillim 145:16), You open Your hand; וְאִגֶּרֶת פְּתוּחָה בְּיָדוֹ (Nechemiah 6:5), an open letter in his hand; and וּכְפִתְחוֹ עָמְדוּ כָל הָעָם (Nechemiah 8:5), which he reads of opening the mouth to read in the Torah, all the people standing.

לַפֶּתַח חַטָּאת רֹבֵץ (Bereishis 4:7), sin crouches at the doorway. The פֶּתַח is what lies outside the doors of the gate, and it carries the name because it stays open even when the doors are shut. The key is וַיִּקְחוּ אֶת הַמַּפְתֵּחַ וַיִּפְתָּחוּ (Shoftim 3:25), they took the key and opened; Targum Yonasan renders מַפְתֵּחַ בֵּית דָּוִד (Yeshayahu 22:22) as the key of the Beis HaMikdash and the rule of the house of David.

מַגְבִּיהַּ פִּתְחוֹ מְבַקֶּשׁ שָׁבֶר (Mishlei 17:19), he who raises his opening seeks ruin. Some take it of a man who speaks loftily over other people, and so it is explained in the words of Chazal. He himself takes it of a man taken up with great buildings, in the way Chazal said that whoever busies himself with building grows poor.

וַיְפַתַּח הַגְּמַלִּים (Bereishis 24:32), he unharnessed the camels; פַּתֵּחַ חַרְצֻבּוֹת רֶשַׁע (Yeshayahu 58:6), loose the bonds of wickedness; אַל יִתְהַלֵּל חֹגֵר כִּמְפַתֵּחַ (Melachim I 20:11), let one girding his belt not boast like one loosing it; and אֲסִירָיו לֹא פָתַח בָּיְתָה (Yeshayahu 14:17), he did not release his prisoners homeward. הִנְנִי מְפַתֵּחַ פִּתֻּחָהּ (Zechariah 3:9) he reads as though the stone had been in confinement all the while the work stood idle, and now it is released and set into the building.

וּפִתַּחְתָּ עֲלֵיהֶם (Shemos 28:9), you shall engrave upon them; פִּתּוּחֵי חֹתָם תְּפַתַּח אֶת שְׁתֵּי הָאֲבָנִים (Shemos 28:11), engrave the two stones as a seal is engraved. He allows הִנְנִי מְפַתֵּחַ פִּתֻּחָהּ here as well: a fine stone is finished by the figures and flowers and knobs cut into it, so the pasuk speaks by figure of bringing it to its full form for the building.

וְהֵמָּה פְתִחוֹת (Tehillim 55:22), and they are drawn swords; he counts here also וְאֶת אֶרֶץ נִמְרֹד בִּפְתָחֶיהָ (Michah 5:5), the land of Nimrod with her blades. Rabbi Yonah reads חֶרֶב חֶרֶב פְּתוּחָה (Yechezkel 21:33), sword, sword drawn, and חֶרֶב פָּתְחוּ רְשָׁעִים (Tehillim 37:14), the wicked have drawn a sword, in one of his explanations as polishing and sharpening. He answers that there is no need for it: the sense is only the drawing of the sword from its sheath, as opening is said of bringing a prisoner out of confinement and freeing him.

Three pesukim and a word. וַהֲדַס וְעֵץ שָׁמֶן (Yeshayahu 41:19), myrtle and oil tree; יַעֲלֶה הֲדַס (Yeshayahu 55:13), a myrtle will come up; עֹמֵד בֵּין הַהֲדַסִּים (Zechariah 1:8), standing among the myrtles. The tree, he says, is known.

סבב.sense: To go round a thing and encircle it; and the turning of a thing about, which he brings back to this one sense.

more.t: וְסָבַב בֵּית אֵל (Shmuel I 7:16), he went round to Beis El; סֹבּוּ צִיּוֹן וְהַקִּיפוּהָ (Tehillim 48:13), go round Tzion and encircle her; סוֹבֵב סֹבֵב הוֹלֵךְ הָרוּחַ (Koheles 1:6), round and round goes the wind; and וְהִנֵּה תְסֻבֶּינָה אֲלֻמֹּתֵיכֶם (Bereishis 37:7), your sheaves came round about.

וַיַּסֵּב אֱלֹהִים אֶת הָעָם (Shemos 13:18), He turned the people about; וַיַּסֵּב חִזְקִיָּהוּ פָּנָיו אֶל הַקִּיר (Yeshayahu 38:2), Chizkiyahu turned his face to the wall; וַתִּסֹּב הַמְּלוּכָה (Melachim I 2:15), the kingship came round to another; and כִּי הָיְתָה סִבָּה (Melachim I 12:15), it was a turn of events.

Rabbi Yonah divided the root into three senses and answered Rabbi Yehudah, who wrote them all as one. He holds Rabbi Yehudah straight and right: not one of the pesukim Rabbi Yonah wondered at escapes the sense of going round and encircling, since no rolling, returning or reversing happens without a turn.

עַד שֶׁהַמֶּלֶךְ בִּמְסִבּוֹ (Shir HaShirim 1:12), while the king was at his table, and רֹאשׁ מְסִבָּי (Tehillim 140:10), the head of those round me: the claim that these are a sense apart, drawn from Chazal's rule that a man does not eat until he reclines, he rejects. They used to sit round about at the food and drink, and while eating they leaned to the left as a mark of standing, so the leaning itself took the name; no other leaning in the world is called by it. The Targum renders וַיֵּשְׁבוּ לֶאֱכָל לֶחֶם (Bereishis 37:25), they sat down to eat bread, with a word of going round.

more.h: A woman shall go round a man
more.t: נְקֵבָה תְּסוֹבֵב גָּבֶר (Yirmiyahu 31:21) he takes as a figure: Knesses Yisrael is likened to a woman seeking her husband, as the pasuk elsewhere says that they will seek Hashem their God and David their king (Hoshea 3:5).

סעד.sense: To support and sustain; the bread that stays a man's heart, and the hand that holds him up.

more.t: וְלֶחֶם לְבַב אֱנוֹשׁ יִסְעָד (Tehillim 104:15), bread sustains a man's heart, has its one object. וְסַעֲדוּ לִבְּכֶם (Bereishis 18:5), sustain your hearts, carries a second with it, since the sense is sustain your hearts with bread, the bread being what sustains the heart; and so סְעָד לִבְּךָ פַּת לֶחֶם (Shoftim 19:5), stay your heart with a morsel of bread.

more.h: Where the word for a meal comes from
more.t: בֹּאָה אִתִּי הַבַּיְתָה וּסְעָדָה (Melachim I 13:7), come home with me and take food: from this, he says, Chazal called a meal סעודה.

סְעָדֵנִי וְאִוָּשֵׁעָה (Tehillim 119:117), hold me up and I will be saved; וִימִינְךָ תִסְעָדֵנִי (Tehillim 18:36), Your right hand upholds me; וְסָעַד בַּחֶסֶד כִּסְאוֹ (Mishlei 20:28), his throne is upheld by kindness. The מִסְעָד of Melachim I 10:12 he has already explained in his entry on סלל. The sense of them all is support and propping.

שׁכח.sense: To forget; also to make a thing forgotten, and to be forgotten.

more.t: וְשָׁכַחְתָּ עֹמֶר בַּשָּׂדֶה (Devarim 24:19), you forget a sheaf in the field; שְׁכֵחֻנִי עַמִּי (Yirmiyahu 18:15), My people have forgotten Me; and in the passive כִּי נִשְׁכַּח זִכְרָם (Koheles 9:5), their memory is forgotten, with נִשְׁכַּחְתִּי כְּמֵת מִלֵּב (Tehillim 31:13), I am forgotten like a dead man out of mind. The word for one who forgets is שֹׁכְחֵי אֱלוֹהַּ (Tehillim 50:22), those who forget God. It is said of causing forgetting too: לְהַשְׁכִּיחַ אֶת עַמִּי שְׁמִי (Yirmiyahu 23:27), to make My people forget My name.

תִּשְׁכַּח יְמִינִי (Tehillim 137:5) names no object, and the thing forgotten is the playing, since the right hand moves the strings of the harp. He reads the pasuk of the singers: when the Bavlim told them to sing they answered how shall we sing, and each of them said, if I forget you, Yerushalayim, and play while she lies in ruin, let my right hand forget its playing.

וְיִשְׁתַּכְּחוּ בָעִיר אֲשֶׁר כֵּן עָשׂוּ (Koheles 8:10) he reads of the righteous. When wicked men die others rise up in their place, as the pasuk says וּמֵעָפָר אַחֵר יִצְמָחוּ (Iyov 8:19), from the dust another springs; those who are from a holy place go off and keep out of their sight because of the violence done to them, and the men who did what was true and upright hide themselves and make themselves forgotten in the city.

נשׁם.sense: Breath, the breathing that is life and the movement that goes with it; and the תִּנְשֶׁמֶת, a bird and also a creeping thing, that carries the name.

more.t: It seems to him that the spirit of every living thing is called by this word, which is why it leans on רוח: כֹּל אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁמַת ־רוּחַ חַיִּים בְּאַפָּיו (Bereishis 7:22), all in whose nostrils was the breath of the spirit of life. To have breath is to have movement.

וַיְהִי חָלְיוֹ חָזָק מְאֹד עַד אֲשֶׁר לֹא־נֽוֹתְרָה־בּוֹ נְשָׁמָֽה (Melachim I 17:17), his sickness was so heavy that no breath was left in him: his breathing was stopped and his movement came to nothing. At Daniel 10:17, where no breath was left in me, he says the words are put strongly beyond their measure, since the man was speaking as he said them.

Ibn Ezra writes on כֹּל אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁמַת־רוּחַ חַיִּים (Bereishis 7:22) that it goes back to man, since we find the word of no one but man. Many say it is called so because it comes from the heavens, and if those are two roots, he says, there are many like it.

more.h: The bird and the creeping thing
more.t: וְאֶת־ הַתִּנְשֶׁמֶת וְאֶת־הַקָּאָת (Vayikra 11:18) is one of the kinds of birds, and they said it is named so because whoever sees it is struck dumb. Rashi writes that it is the one called צואיט"א. The same name is among the creeping things, וְהַחֹמֶט וְהַתִּנְשָֽׁמֶת (Vayikra 11:30), and Rashi writes that this one is called טלפ"א.

יחד.sense: Oneness: the single and only one, and many joined together so that they look like one.

more.t: רַךְ וְיָחִיד לִפְנֵי אִמִּֽי (Mishlei 4:3), tender and an only child before my mother, and וְרַק הִיא יְחִידָה (Shoftim 11:34), she was his only child. Both belong, he says, to the sense of one.

more.h: The soul as the single one
more.t: The soul is called יְחִידָה, מִיַּד־כֶּלֶב יְחִידָתִֽי (Tehillim 22:21), my only one from the power of the dog, because it stands single over against the parts and powers of the body, which are many and are not of its kind.

יַּחַד יָבֹאוּ גְדוּדָיו (Iyov 19:12), his troops come on together, is also from one, since many joined look like a single thing. His own view is that the vav of יַחְדָּו is the mark of the plural set over a singular, as in עָלָיו and אֵלָיו; mostly it carries no yod, but we find עָלָו [עָלָיו] בַּשָּׁמַיִם יַרְעֵם (Shmuel I 2:10), He thunders against them in heaven, without one. Three places have יַחְדָּיו with a yod (Yirmiyahu 46:12, 46:21 and 49:3), and he says it is put so because singleness and plurality are gathered together in it.
יַחֵד לְבָבִי לְיִרְאָה שְׁמֶֽךָ (Tehillim 86:11), make my heart one to fear Your name.

מהל.sense: Diluted, mixed with water. Nothing in his entry here touches circumcision, which he files elsewhere.

more.t: One line, on סָבְאֵךְ מָהוּל בַּמָּֽיִם (Yeshayahu 1:22), your wine is mixed with water, which he glosses as mixed. His father brings support from the Arabic, which says of a thing that has been mingled מהל"א מהל"י.

מול.sense: To circumcise, and more widely to cut off; and a second word מוּל, facing, over against.

more.t: וּמַלְתֶּם אֵת עָרְלַת לְבַבְכֶם (Devarim 10:16), circumcise the foreskin of your heart, and וַיָּמָל אֶת־בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל (Yehoshua 5:3), he circumcised the children of Yisrael. The form that is done to a man: וּבַיּוֹם הַשְּׁמִינִי יִמּוֹל בְּשַׂר עָרְלָתֽוֹ (Vayikra 12:3), on the eighth day the flesh of his foreskin shall be circumcised.

עַל־כָּל־ מוּל בְּעָרְלָֽה (Yirmiyahu 9:24) he reads as two things at once: upon everyone circumcised and upon everyone who is in his foreskin, that is, upon Yisrael who are circumcised and upon those who are not.

יְמוֹלֵל וְיָבֵֽשׁ (Tehillim 90:6), it is cut down and dries up, he takes either as a verb that stands on its own or as one whose subject is left unsaid, the wind, as at רוּחַ עָֽבְרָה־בּוֹ וְאֵינֶנּוּ (Tehillim 103:16), the wind passes over it and it is gone. He says of the whole group that it is the sense of cutting.

A separate word means over against: מוּל הָֽאֱלֹהִים (Shemos 18:19), which he glosses as facing Hashem, and וַיִּסֹּב מֵֽאֶצְלוֹ אֶל־ מוּל אַחֵר (Shmuel I 17:30), he turned away from him toward another, which he reads as toward another place. It appears with a cholam, מוֹל סוּף (Devarim 1:1), and with a quiescent alef after the vav, הַֽהוֹלֶכֶת לְמוֹאל (Nechemiah 12:38).

רפא.sense: To heal and to be healed; by extension to mend what is broken, and to forgive. Separately רְפָאִים, the giant warriors, and רְפָאִים, the dead.

more.t: רְפֻאוֹת תְּעָלָה אֵין לָֽךְ (Yirmiyahu 30:13), you have no healing medicines; רִפְאוּת תְּהִי לְשָׁרֶּךָ (Mishlei 3:8), it will be a healing to your body; and מַרְפֵּא, a cure, לְאֵין מַרְפֵּֽא (Divrei HaYamim II 36:16), past all cure.

וְרַפֹּא יְרַפֵּֽא (Shemos 21:19) he takes as reaching past the one healed to a third: the man who struck hires the doctor for him. The Targum has וְאֲגַר אָסְיָא יְשַׁלֵּם, he shall pay the doctor's fee. And the Chachamim taught (Bava Kama 88a) that if the one who struck is himself a doctor and wants to do the healing, he is not listened to, since the injured man may tell him that he is as a lion lying in wait for him.

The word is used of repair: וַיְרַפֵּא אֶת־מִזְבַּח (Melachim I 18:30), of the broken down mizbe'ach, and כַּֽאֲשֶׁר יִשְׁבֹּר אֶת־כְּלִי הַיּוֹצֵר אֲשֶׁר לֹֽא־יוּכַל לְהֵֽרָפֵה עוֹד (Yirmiyahu 19:11), as one breaks a potter's vessel that can never be mended again. And of forgiveness: רְפָאָה נַפְשִׁי כִּי־חָטָאתִי לָֽךְ (Tehillim 41:5), heal my soul, for I have sinned against You.

נִשְׁאַר מִיֶּתֶר הָֽרְפָאִים (Devarim 3:11), left of the remnant of the Refaim, which he glosses as the mighty men among the giants. The singular is נוֹלַד לְהָֽרָפָֽא (Divrei HaYamim I 20:6), born to the Rafa, where the heh is the definite article kept after the lamed of service. The two places in Divrei HaYamim are written with an alef; in Shmuel the same word is written with a heh standing in the alef's place.

אִם־ רְפָאִים יָקוּמוּ (Tehillim 88:11), shall the dead rise, and כִּֽי־ רְפָאִים שָׁם (Mishlei 9:18), the dead are there. Some read הָֽרְפָאִים יְחוֹלָלוּ (Iyov 26:5) as a hint to the grains of seed under the ground, dead as they lie there and afterwards alive and brought forth, and take מִתַּחַת מַיִם of the waters beneath, which are the cause of the moisture of the earth that the seeds grow from.

אבן.sense: A stone; and from it the weight in a scale, the builder's plummet, the potter's wheel, and הָאָבְנָיִם, which he reads as the womb itself.

more.t: מִשָּׁם רֹעֶה אֶבֶן יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (Bereishis 49:24) he takes as all of Yisrael: a stone is one body, so Yisrael spoken of as one is called a stone, or else, since Yisrael are the foundation of the world's building, they are called a stone as a figure. Rabbi Yonah read it as the head of Yisrael, and he answers that we do not find a head called אֶבֶן unless the pasuk explains itself afterwards, as at אֶבֶן בֹּחַן פִּנַּת יִקְרַת מוּסָד (Yeshayahu 28:16), a tried stone, a precious cornerstone of a foundation.

תִּשְׁתַּפֵּכְנָה אַבְנֵי ־קֹדֶשׁ (Eichah 4:1), the holy stones are poured out, he reads of the princes and the great men. בְּתוֹךְ אַבְנֵי ־אֵשׁ הִתְהַלָּֽכְתָּ (Yechezkel 28:14), you walked among stones of fire, is as though among the angels; his father takes it of carbuncles, shining gems like lamps, and the man walked at night among them. Targum Yonasan rendered בְעַמָא קַדִישָׁא סְבַרְתָּא לְמִשְׁלַט, among the holy people you thought to rule, and that reading seems right to him, since the stones of fire of the pasuk after it are Yisrael, called so because they are holy.

וְכָֽבְשׁוּ אַבְנֵי ־קֶלַע (Zechariah 9:15), they tread down sling stones, are the officers of Greece: since the kings of the house of the Chashmonaim were likened to crown stones for their greatness, the officers of Greece are likened to sling stones for their lowness.

Weights are made of stone, so a weight is called אבן: לֹא־יִֽהְיֶה לְךָ בְּכִֽיסְךָ אֶבֶן וָאָבֶן (Devarim 25:13), you shall not have in your bag two sorts of weight. So too the builder's plumb, וְנָטָה עָלֶיהָ קַו־תֹהוּ וְאַבְנֵי ־בֹֽהוּ (Yeshayahu 34:11), and even when the thing is of tin or of lead it is still called a stone, אֶת־ הָאֶבֶן הַבְּדִיל (Zechariah 4:10) and אֶבֶן הָֽעוֹפֶרֶת (Zechariah 5:8).

עֹשֶׂה מְלָאכָה עַל־ הָֽאָבְנָֽיִם (Yirmiyahu 18:3), doing work on the אבנים, is the potter's implement on which he makes his earthenware, well known to the men of that trade and called in laaz סיל"א. They said it is like a pair of millstones, and that is why the name is put as two; but in these lands, he says, it is not so, only one round piece of wood shaped like a millstone. Rabbi Yonah wrote that the two-piece kind is the tool of the potters of the east. His father holds the alef here is added and the word belongs to building.

Rabbi Yonah takes וּרְאִיתֶן עַל־ הָֽאָבְנָיִם (Shemos 1:16) as the place where the child falls from its mother's womb, which is called מַשְׁבֵּר, and derives the word from בן and בנים with an added alef. He himself holds it is the womb itself, named for the בנים: were it the place the child falls after coming out, why does the pasuk say you shall see on the אבנים, when before the child is wholly out one can already see whether it is male or female (Sotah 11b), and why would a place of falling be called מַשְׁבֵּר? He answers from הַֽאֲנִי אַשְׁבִּיר וְלֹא אוֹלִיד (Yeshayahu 66:9) that the מַשְׁבֵּר comes before the birth. It is named as two for the צִירִים, which are like the two hinges of a door, and the Chachamim taught (Bechoros 45a) in the name of Rabbi Eliezer that as a house has hinges so has a woman, from כִּֽי־נֶֽהֶפְכוּ עָלֶיהָ צִרֶֽיהָ (Shmuel I 4:19), her pangs turned upon her.

צור.sense: To lay siege, and to be in straits; and separately צוּר, a rock, the sharpness of a flint, the shaping of a form, and the צַוָּאר, the neck.

more.t: וְצַרְתָּ עָלֶֽיהָ (Devarim 20:12), you shall besiege it, and the noun וּבָנִיתָ מָצוֹר (Devarim 20:20), you shall build a siege work. A walled city is itself called מָצוֹר, he says, because no man takes it by force but only by building a siege against it and standing about it until it falls from hunger and thirst: וַתִּבֶן צֹר מָצוֹר לָהּ (Zechariah 9:3).

more.h: Straits, the enemy, the rival wife
more.t: A second sense near it is pressure: צַר ־לִי הַמָּקוֹם (Yeshayahu 49:20), the place is too narrow for me, with the noun צָרָה, trouble. The enemy is called צַר, אִישׁ צַר וְאוֹיֵב (Esther 7:6), a man who is an adversary and an enemy, because an enemy pains and presses. And since two wives of one man hate and envy each other and their place is narrow for them, each is called her fellow's צָרָה, וְכִֽעֲסַתָּה צָֽרָתָהּ (Shmuel I 1:6), her rival provoked her. He holds this whole sense is close to the first, one shut inside a siege being in straits, and says it may all belong to the root צָרַר.

צִירִים אֲחָזוּנִי כְּצִירֵי יֽוֹלֵדָה (Yeshayahu 21:3), pangs took hold of me like the pangs of a woman giving birth; idols are called by the same word, חָֽרָשֵׁי צִירִֽים (Yeshayahu 45:15 in his edition). A ציר is also one sent, צִיר נֶאֱמָן לְשֹֽׁלְחָיו (Mishlei 25:13), a faithful messenger to those who send him. And it is the pivot of a door, הַדֶּלֶת תִּסּוֹב עַל־ צִירָהּ (Mishlei 26:14), the door turns upon its hinge, which he says is the door's foot that it turns on. Some say it is the hollow in the threshold that the door's foot enters; he holds they are wrong, that hollow being called צנור.

וְצַרְתָּ הַכֶּסֶף (Devarim 14:25), you shall bind up the money, and וְצַרְתָּ אוֹתָם בִּכְנָפֶֽיךָ (Yechezkel 5:3), bind them in your skirts: the putting away of money or of anything else in a purse and the like, with the tying of it. He calls this near the sense before it, since one who ties a thing up presses it.

וְצוּר יֶעְתַּק מִמְּקֹמֽוֹ (Iyov 14:18), a rock is moved from its place, and עַל־ הַצּוּר (Shemos 17:6): a crag. Because rocks are strong, חֶלְקַת הַצֻּרִים (Shmuel II 2:16) he glosses as the portion of the strong ones, those young men being strong as the rocks, standing against each other and neither side winning but all falling together. Because of that strength Hashem is called צוּר, by way of transfer, since He may be likened to nothing but His own works: הַצּוּר תָּמִים פָּֽעֳלוֹ (Devarim 32:4), the Rock, His work is perfect, and צוּר עֽוֹלָמִֽים (Yeshayahu 26:4), the everlasting Rock. Rabbi Yonah takes וַתִּבֶן צֹר מָצוֹר לָהּ and its like in the sense of strength, and so Targum Yonasan rendered.

אַף־תָּשִׁיב צוּר חַרְבּוֹ (Tehillim 89:44) he glosses as the sharpness of his sword, and חַֽרְבוֹת צֻרִים (Yehoshua 5:2) as swords that have an edge, or else צוּר is an adjective and the words mean his sharp sword. Another sense is the shaping of a form: וַיָּצַר אֹתוֹ בַּחֶרֶט (Shemos 32:4), he formed it with a graving tool, and צוּרַת הַבַּיִת (Yechezkel 43:11), the form of the house; he reads וַיָּצֻרוּ וַיִּמְנוּ (Melachim II 12:11) of making the silver into coin, as the Chachamim said of וְצַרְתָּ הַכֶּסֶף (Devarim 14:25) that it is a thing that has a form (Berachos 46b). From this root too the neck: וַיָּשֶׂם רְבִד הַזָּהָב עַל־ צַוָּארֽוֹ (Bereishis 41:42), he put the gold chain upon his neck, spoken of at times as two, for its right side and its left.

חלמשׁ.sense: Flint: the hardest and strongest kind of rock. The word is said of nothing but a צוּר.

more.t: מִצּוּר הַֽחַלָּמִֽישׁ (Devarim 8:15) he glosses as from the hard and mighty rock, and מֵֽחַלְמִישׁ צֽוּר (Devarim 32:13), where the word leans on צור, as the hardness of the rocks, the noun taking its own adjective after it as in תּוֹלַעַת שָׁנִי (Shemos 28:6) and וּשְׁנִי תוֹלַעַת (Vayikra 14:4).

Since the word falls on nothing but a rock, the pasuk can use it with no rock named beside it: בַּֽחַלָּמִישׁ שָׁלַח יָדוֹ (Iyov 28:9), he puts his hand to the flint, and שַׂמְתִּי פָנַי כַּֽחַלָּמִישׁ (Yeshayahu 50:7), I have set my face like flint.

פשֹע.sense: To stride, to take a step; and the noun פֶּשַׂע, a pace, and so a very small distance.

more.t: אֶפְשֳׂעָה בָהּ (Yeshayahu 27:4) he glosses as I will stride in it, and כִּי כְפֶשַׂע בֵּינִי וּבֵין הַמָּֽוֶת (Shmuel I 20:3), there is but a step between me and death, he takes as a pace, meaning a very little thing. The Chachamim use the word this way (Shabbos 113b and Taanis 10b) when they say that a wide stride takes away a five hundredth of a man's eyesight.

עַד־ הַמִּפְשָׂעָה (Divrei HaYamim I 19:4) he takes as the word standing for the private parts, the way the pesukim put רגלים for the same thing: וְלֹֽא־עָשָׂה רַגְלָיו (Shmuel II 24:25 in his edition), he had not dressed his feet, and אַךְ מֵסִיךְ הוּא אֶת־רַגְלָיו (Shoftim 3:24).

פשׁע.sense: Rebellion: breaking out from under the hand of a master, or of whoever gave the command.

more.t: מֶלֶךְ מוֹאָב פָּשַׁע בִּי (Melachim II 3:7), the king of Moav has rebelled against me, and אָז תִּפְשַׁע לִבְנָה בָּעֵת הַהִֽיא (Melachim II 8:22), then Livnah rebelled at that time; so too וְהֵם פָּשְׁעוּ בִֽי (Yeshayahu 1:2), and they have rebelled against Me. He reads אָח נִפְשָׁע מִקִּרְיַת־עֹז (Mishlei 18:19) as a brother who is harder to win than a strong city.

The Chachamim taught (Yoma 36b) that עֲוֹנוֹת are the wilful sins, from הִכָּרֵת תִּכָּרֵת הַנֶּפֶשׁ הַהִוא עֲוֹנָה בָֽהּ (Bamidbar 15:31), that soul shall be cut off, its iniquity upon it; that פשעים are the rebellions, from מֶלֶךְ מוֹאָב פָּשַׁע בִּי; and that חטאים are the sins done unknowing, from נֶפֶשׁ כִּי־תֶֽחֱטָא בִשְׁגָגָה (Vayikra 4:2), a soul that sins in error.

more.h: The bailee who is called a rebel
more.t: עַֽל־כָּל־דְּבַר־ פֶּשַׁע (Shemos 22:8), for every matter of trespass, he takes of a man careless with a deposit who did not guard it as guardians guard. There is no rebellion here and he does not destroy it with his own hands, and still he is called a פושע: once he does not put his eyes and his heart and his watching upon what was left with him, it is as though he rebels against the man who deposited it and goes out from under the hand of the charge he took upon himself.

Rabbi Yonah holds the word in כְּהָתֵם הַפּֽשְׁעִים (Daniel 8:23) is a noun, the punishments that had passed over them. Ibn Ezra reads it plainly, of those who do the deed, and holds the sense is that because the rebels of Yisrael were many they were sold into the hand of the Greeks.

חטא.sense: To sin, and to miss the mark; and from it the חַטָּאת, the offering that takes a man's sin away.

more.t: אֶל־הַֽשַּׂעֲרָה וְלֹא יַחֲטִֽא (Shoftim 20:16), at a hair and not miss, which he glosses as not missing with the stone.

וְֽחֹֽטְאִי חֹמֵס נַפְשׁוֹ (Mishlei 8:36) he explains as one who sins against me. שְׁאוֹל חָטָֽאוּ (Iyov 24:19) he reads as sinning as far as the grave, that is, until they die. And וְהָיִיתִי אֲנִי וּבְנִי שְׁלֹמֹה חַטָּאִֽים (Melachim I 1:21), I and my son Shlomo will be counted offenders, he takes as meaning that we shall seem guilty before you, having no part in the kingship; some read it as a respectful turn of speech, the sin being David's.

פֶּן־ יַֽחֲטִיאוּ אֹֽתְךָ לִי (Shemos 23:33), lest they make you sin against Me, and אֲשֶׁר־ הֶֽחֱטִיא אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵל (Melachim II 3:3), who made Yisrael sin. In another form, אָֽנֹכִי אֲחַטֶּנָּה (Bereishis 31:39), which he glosses as the loss falling on me, and I pay you its worth.

וְחִטְּאוּ אֶת־הַמִּזְבֵּחַ (Yechezkel 43:22) he glosses as removing a man's sin through the service of the mizbe'ach, and הַכֹּהֵן הַֽמְחַטֵּא אֹתָהּ (Vayikra 6:19) is the kohen who does its service, the offering being made by his hand and a man's sin removed by it. So too הוּא יִתְחַטָּא ־בוֹ (Bamidbar 19:12), which he reads as removing what is on him by the sprinkling.

more.h: Where the word is the punishment
more.t: זֹאת תִּֽהְיֶה חַטַּאת מִצְרָיִם (Zechariah 14:19) he glosses as the punishment of the sin they sinned, and in the same way כִּי לֹֽא־שָׁלֵם עֲוֹן הָֽאֱמֹרִי עַד־הֵֽנָּה (Bereishis 15:16), the punishment of the iniquity.

עוה.sense: To be twisted or bent out of true, and so to do wrong; from it עָוֹן, iniquity, and at times the punishment for it.

more.t: He glosses the whole group as twisting: נַֽעֲוֵיתִי שַׁחֹתִי עַד־מְאֹד (Tehillim 38:7), I am bent and bowed very low, and וְנַֽעֲוֵה לב (Mishlei 12:8), one of twisted heart; וְעִוָּה פָנֶיהָ (Yeshayahu 24:1), He turns its face about. From this root and this sense also רוּחַ עִוְעִים (Yeshayahu 19:14), a spirit of distortion, with its first letter doubled.

more.h: Which root Vashti's word belongs to
more.t: עָוְתָה וַשְׁתִּי הַמַּלְכָּה (Esther 1:16), Vashti the queen has done wrong, many put under this root; his own view is that it belongs to עות. His father wrote it under עָוַת, together with נַֽעֲוַת הַמַּרְדּוּת (Shmuel I 20:30) and מְעֻוָּת לֹֽא־יוּכַל לִתְקֹן (Koheles 1:15), what is twisted cannot be made straight.

more.h: Whether that word is male or female
more.t: He holds נַֽעֲוַת המרדות may belong here as a feminine form whose heh turned into a tav because it leans on the word after it, and what pushed him to that is that בן there is pointed with a segol, as words that lean are. His father read it from the root עָוַת and called it a masculine form, and he suggests his father may have found בן pointed with a tzere.

The noun עָוֹן stands to the verb as גָּאוֹן does to גָּאָה. Sometimes it is not the sin but the punishment of it: גָּדוֹל עֲוֹנִי מִנְּשֽׂוֹא (Bereishis 4:13), my punishment is greater than I can bear it and carry it, and כִּי לֹֽא־שָׁלֵם עֲוֹן הָֽאֱמֹרִי עַד־הֵֽנָּה (Bereishis 15:16), meaning that the time of the Emori's punishment, to drive them out of their land, had not come until the four hundred years were done. The Emori is named, he says, because he is the greatest of the seven nations. So too תְּֽנָה־ עָוֹן עַל־ עֲוֹנָם (Tehillim 69:28), lay punishment upon their iniquity.

לחץ.sense: To press, and so to oppress; he glosses the whole root as pressure.

more.t: וְהוּא לָחַץ אֶת־בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּחָזְקָה (Shoftim 4:3), he oppressed the children of Yisrael harshly, and וְגֵר לֹא תִלְחָץ (Shemos 23:9), you shall not oppress a stranger. The oppressors themselves are the לֹֽחֲצֵיהֶם (Shoftim 2:18).

וּלְחַצְתֶּם אֹתוֹ בַּדֶּלֶת (Melachim II 6:32), press him back with the door, and וַתִּלְחַץ אֶת־רֶגֶל בִּלְעָם (Bamidbar 22:25), she pressed Bilaam's foot, where the same pasuk has her וַתִּלָּחֵץ אֶל־הַקִּיר, pressed herself against the wall.
הַלַּחַץ (Shemos 3:9), the oppression, and לֶחֶם צָר וּמַיִם לָחַץ (Yeshayahu 30:20), the bread of straits and the water of oppression.

דחק.sense: To press or crowd; the word the Targum uses to render לָחַץ.

more.t: One line, on וְאִישׁ אָחִיו לֹא יִדְחָקוּן (Yoel 2:8), they do not press one another, and מִפְּנֵי לֹֽחֲצֵיהֶם וְדֹֽחֲקֵיהֶֽם (Shoftim 2:18), before their oppressors and those who pressed them; he adds that the Targum renders לָחַץ (Melachim II 13:4) with דוֹחֲקָא.

אלץ.sense: To press hard, to urge; he glosses it by לחץ, pressing.

more.t: One line, on כָּל־הַיָּמִים וַתְּאַֽלֲצֵהוּ (Shoftim 16:16), all the days, and she pressed him, which he glosses ותלחצהו, she pressed him, with a remark on the root's lamed and its dagesh.

נקף.sense: To strike off, to break and to cut: the beating down of olives, and the cutting off of a head.

more.t: חַגִּים יִנְקֹֽפוּ (Yeshayahu 29:1) he glosses as their head being cut off. The Targum renders וַֽעֲרַפְתּוֹ (Shemos 13:13) with וּתְנַקְפֵיהּ and הָֽעֲרוּפָה (Devarim 21:6) with דִנְקִיפָא.

וְנִקַּף סִֽבְכֵי הַיַּעַר בַּבַּרְזֶל (Yeshayahu 10:34), the thickets of the forest are cut down with iron, and וְאַחַר עוֹרִֽי נִקְּפוּ ־זֹאת (Iyov 19:26), which he glosses as the worms having broken and pecked at this, the word this standing for the bone. He says the whole group is breaking and cutting.

more.h: In the words of the Chachamim
more.t: They speak of one who beats down the top of an olive tree, and they said (Chullin 7b) that a man does not so much as bruise his finger below unless it has been declared of him above, and that the blood of such a bruise is accepted like the blood of an olah.

כחשׁ.sense: To deny and to lie; and in a second sense, of flesh, to grow lean.

more.t: וְכִחֵשׁ בַּעֲמִיתוֹ (Vayikra 5:21), he deals falsely with his fellow; וַתְּכַחֵשׁ שָׂרָה (Bereishis 18:15), and Sarah denied it; אָלֹה וְכַחֵשׁ (Hoshea 4:2), swearing and lying. The adjective is בָּנִים כֶּחָשִׁים (Yeshayahu 30:9), sons who deal falsely, and the noun is in סְבָבֻנִי בְכַחַשׁ (Hoshea 12:1), they have ringed me round with falsehood, and וּבְכַחֲשֵׁיהֶם שָׂרִים (Hoshea 7:3), and the princes with their lies. He gathers them all as denial and lying.

כִּחֵשׁ מַעֲשֵׂה־זַיִת (Chavakuk 3:17), the olive crop fails, he takes as a borrowed use: the tree lies to the hope of those who wait on it. So too וְתִירוֹשׁ יְכַחֶשׁ בָּהּ (Hoshea 9:2), the new wine fails her, that is, it belies their hope. The last word is one of two where בָּם is what the eye expects and the Mesorah has it read בָּהּ.

In another sense the word is thinness: וּבְשָׂרִי כָּחַשׁ מִשָּׁמֶן (Tehillim 109:24), my flesh has grown lean and lost its fat, and Chazal speak of a בהמה כחושה, a lean animal. So וְיִכָּחֲשׁוּ אֹיְבֶיךָ לָךְ (Devarim 33:29), your enemies will be lean and poor and cowed before you, and the noun וַיָּקָם בִּי כַחֲשִׁי (Iyov 16:8), my leanness rises up against me.

more.h: Strangers who cringe, or who deny
more.t: בְּנֵי נֵכָר יִתְכַּחֲשׁוּ־לִי (Shmuel II 22:45) he leaves open between the two senses. It may belong with the lean and the cowed, strangers who go under before me; or with the first sense, that out of great dread they will deny what they did and say they never did it.

נקב.sense: To bore through, to pierce a hole; and in a second sense to name a thing in so many words, and so to curse by spelling out the Name.

more.t: וּבָא בְכַפּוֹ וּנְקָבָהּ (Yeshayahu 36:6), the reed enters a man's palm and pierces it; אֶל־צְרוֹר נָקוּב (Chaggai 1:6), into a bag with a hole in it; וַיִּקֹּב חֹר (Melachim II 12:10), he bored a hole; בְּמוֹקְשִׁים יִנְקָב־אָף (Iyov 40:24), with snares his nose is pierced.

וְאֶל־מַקֶּבֶת בּוֹר (Yeshayahu 51:1) is the hollowed pit you were quarried from. The tool with which stones are dressed and pierced carries the same name: a hammer with one end pointed for boring and cutting and the other for striking, used in work of iron and copper and the like. וַתָּשֶׂם אֶת־הַמַּקֶּבֶת בְּיָדָהּ (Shoftim 4:21), she put the hammer in her hand; וּמַקָּבוֹת וְהַגַּרְזֶן (Melachim I 6:7), hammers and the axe; וּבְמַקָּבוֹת יְחַזְּקוּם (Yirmiyahu 10:4), with hammers they make it fast.
From this sense of piercing he derives זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה (Bereishis 1:27), male and female.

The second sense is to set out in so many words: נָקְבָה שְׂכָרְךָ עָלַי (Bereishis 30:28), name me your wage; נְקֻבֵי רֵאשִׁית הַגּוֹיִם (Amos 6:1), the men marked out as the first of the nations. וַיִּקֹּב בֶּן־הָאִשָּׁה הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִית (Vayikra 24:11) is that he spelled the Name out in its letters and cursed; and וְנֹקֵב שֵׁם (Vayikra 24:16) is to spell out and to curse, for a man is not liable until he does both. So יִקְּבֻהוּ אֹרְרֵי־יוֹם (Iyov 3:8), let those who curse the day curse it, and יִקְּבֻהוּ לְאוֹם (Mishlei 11:26), the people curse him.

פטשׁ.sense: A hammer, and the large kind of it.

more.t: וּכְפַטִּישׁ יְפֹצֵץ סָלַע (Yirmiyahu 23:29), and like a hammer that shatters rock. He glosses the word in a line: it is the large מקבת, the big hammer.

ארג.sense: To weave; and the noun אֶרֶג, the weaver's implement.

more.t: אִם־תַּאַרְגִי אֶת־שֶׁבַע מַחְלְפוֹת רֹאשִׁי (Shoftim 16:13), if you weave the seven locks of my head, and מַעֲשֵׂה אֹרֵג (Shemos 28:32), the work of a weaver. The sense, he says, is known.

אֶת־הַיְתַד הָאֶרֶג (Shoftim 16:14) names the implement on which the weaver folds the cloth before him as he works. The two words stand as a construct with the governing noun left out, the pin, the pin of the loom; or else as a construct that keeps the definite article, as in הַלִּשְׁכוֹת הַקֹּדֶשׁ (Yechezkel 46:19), the chambers of the holy. Yonasan renders it the weavers' implement, and renders כִּמְנוֹר אֹרְגִים (Shmuel II 21:19), like a weavers' beam, with the same word.

יָמַי קַלּוּ מִנִּי־אָרֶג (Iyov 7:6), my days are swifter than the אָרֶג. That is the implement that carries the weft thread, and the comparison holds because the weaver drives it at a run from one edge of the cloth to the other.

סגל.sense: A treasure set apart: silver, gold and precious stones laid up in a treasury.

more.t: וִהְיִיתֶם לִי סְגֻלָּה (Shemos 19:5), you shall be My treasure, and וּסְגֻלַּת מְלָכִים (Koheles 2:8), the treasure of kings. He glosses the word as the setting apart of silver and gold and precious stones in a treasury.

ים.sense: The sea; and so the west, the side the Great Sea lies on; and the יֵמִם, which he takes for mules.

more.t: כַּמַּיִם לַיָּם מְכַסִּים (Yeshayahu 11:9), as the waters cover the sea, with the plural יַמִּים, seas (Bereishis 1:10). Because the Great Sea lies to the west of Eretz Yisrael, the west itself is called by the word: יָם וְדָרוֹם יְרָשָׁה (Devarim 33:23), possess the west and the south.

The word is sometimes referred to in the feminine: וְאֶת־הַיָּם הוֹרִד מֵעַל הַבָּקָר הַנְּחֹשֶׁת אֲשֶׁר תַּחְתֶּיהָ (Melachim II 16:17), he took the sea down off the brazen oxen that were beneath it, where the word for beneath it is a feminine one.

He weighs two answers and settles neither. The root may be יָמַם, and the doubled letter in the plural and in the suffixed forms is the proof of it. Or the root is יוֹם, the doubling standing in place of the quiescent letter, and the proof there is the kamatz, since every one of them is kamatz save יַם סוּף.

more.h: The mules found in the wilderness
more.t: אֲשֶׁר מָצָא אֶת־הַיֵּמִם בַּמִּדְבָּר (Bereishis 36:24), who found the יֵמִם in the wilderness: these are mules, bred of two kinds, the horse and the donkey. מָצָא is that he found it while at pasture; he was herding the donkeys, and it came into his mind to breed the horse on the she-donkey, and he brought this kind into the world. Chazal (Pesachim 54a) say Anah was himself of invalid birth and brought invalid creatures into the world, being the son of his brother Tzivon, who came upon his own mother and fathered him.

דרם.sense: The south, the same quarter that also goes by the names תֵימָן and נֶגֶב.

more.t: וְדָרוֹם יְרָשָׁה (Devarim 33:23), possess the south. He glosses it in a line: דרום is the same as תֵימָן and the same as נֶגֶב, one side of the world called by all three.

ימן.sense: The right hand and the right side; and so the south, which lies on a man's right when he faces east.

more.t: אִם־הַשְּׂמֹאל וְאֵימִנָה (Bereishis 13:9), if you go left I will go to the right side. The adjective names the right of a thing: וּפְנֵי אַרְיֵה אֶל־הַיָּמִין (Yechezkel 1:10), the lion's face to the right; יַד־יְמִינוֹ (Bereishis 48:17), the hand of his right side; עַל יֶרֶךְ יְמִינוֹ (Shoftim 3:16), on the thigh of his right side; and the hand is spoken of in the masculine.

Since a man's strength is in his right side, the word stands for strength: וִימִינָם יְמִין שָׁקֶר (Tehillim 144:11), their strength and their might is a lie. Rabbi Adonim took it for an oath instead, from the Arabic, since the pasuk has already said אשר פיהם דבר שוא, whose mouth speaks falsehood, so that the second half runs: and their oath is a false oath.

אֶת־אֶצְבָּעוֹ הַיְמָנִית (Vayikra 14:16), his right finger, and וְעַל־בֹּהֶן יָדוֹ הַיְמָנִית (Vayikra 14:14), on the thumb of his right hand, come with kamatz under the mem. Rabbi Yonah wrote that the kamatz keeps the word apart from the one that belongs to the tribe of Binyamin, אִישׁ יְמִינִי (Esther 2:5), a Binyaminite. Rabbi Yehudah wrote the same, and both matched it to שמאלי, kamatz as well because the one stands opposite the other, though there no such parting is needed. Radak says they wrote well.

He finds the same use of a vowel to part two meanings in Mishnah Parah. Rabbi Yehoshua said he had heard only שלשית and could not say what the word meant. Ben Azzai explained: say שלישית and it is third to the others in a count; say שלשית and it is three years old. So with כרם רבעי: רביעי is fourth in a count, רבעי is of four years.

וְאָבִיו קָרָא־לוֹ בִנְיָמִין (Bereishis 35:18) he reads as בן ימין, son of the right. The right is the honoured and beloved side, and the youngest of the sons is the dearest, so the name says: my son who is dear and honoured to me. His tribesmen are called after him with the full form, בֶּן־יְמִינִי (Shmuel I 9:21), and with the bare word, אִישׁ יְמִינִי (Shmuel I 9:2).

The south quarter is called יָמִין because it is on a man's right when his face is to the east, the east being called פנים as the west is called אחור: צָפוֹן וְיָמִין אַתָּה בְרָאתָם (Tehillim 89:13), north and south You created. With a tav added it is תֵימָן: אֱלוֹהַּ מִתֵּימָן יָבוֹא (Chavakuk 3:3), God will come from the south. It is also called נֶגֶב, and the two are set side by side in נֶגְבָּה תֵימָנָה (Shemos 26:18), southward; the two words are one thing, as in אַדְמַת־עָפָר (Daniel 12:2), earth of dust, or else the second is there for plainness, תֵימָנָה being the clearer of the two.

דגן.sense: Grain: the wheat, the barley, or another of the five kinds, once the heap has been finished off.

more.h: The word and its two pesukim
more.t: דָּגָן תִּירוֹשׁ וְיִצְהָר (Devarim 28:51), grain, wine and oil, and וְאָסַפְתָּ דְגָנֶךָ (Devarim 11:14), you shall gather in your grain. He glosses it as the name of the wheat or the barley or one of the other five kinds, after the heap has been smoothed off.

זון.sense: To feed and to sustain; זַן, a kind of food that nourishes, and מָזוֹן, provision.

more.h: The kinds that feed a man
more.t: מְפִיקִים מִזַּן אֶל־זַן (Tehillim 144:13), yielding from kind to kind. זַן describes the kinds that nourish, the wheat and the barley and the sorts of pulse and the like, which feed a man. The Mishnah uses the verb the same way, of one who marries a woman and undertakes to feed her daughter three years, and he says the verb is much used besides. The noun is בָּר וָלֶחֶם וּמָזוֹן (Bereishis 45:23), corn and bread and provision.

רָחָב הַזּוֹנָה (Yehoshua 6:25) he takes as an adjective on the pattern of טוֹבָה, and its sense is one who sells food; Targum Yonasan renders it with the word for an innkeeper. Rabbi Yonah read וַיִּתְּנוּ הַיֶּלֶד בַּזּוֹנָה (Yoel 4:3) the same way, though it may belong to זנה, harlotry.

Rabbi Yonah read מזן אל זן as from one kind to another, taking it from the Targum of לְמִינוֹ (Bereishis 1:11), which is לִזְנֵיהּ, after its kind. He reads בְּשָׂמִים וּזְנִים מְרֻקָּחִים (Divrei HaYamim II 16:14), spices of kinds compounded, along with it; but the sounder grammar, he holds, makes וזנים there a word of another root, on the pattern of מְתִים.

more.h: A different word, and a form
more.t: וְיָתֵד תִּהְיֶה לְךָ עַל־אֲזֵנֶךָ (Devarim 23:14), you shall have a peg upon your gear: the alef is added, and the word is the sort of weapon Chazal call כלי זין. Of וְהַזֹּנוֹת רָחָצוּ (Melachim I 22:38), where the זֹנוֹת washed, he says only that the form goes on the pattern of קוֹמָה and קוֹמוֹת.

נוב.sense: To bear fruit and to thrive; and so of wealth increasing, and of speech, which is the fruit of the tongue.

more.t: חַיִל כִּי יָנוּב (Tehillim 62:11), when wealth increases, and עוֹד יְנוּבוּן (Tehillim 92:15), they will still bear fruit in old age. The noun is מִתְּנוּבֹת שָׂדָי (Eichah 4:9), the yield of the field, and the sense of them all is fruit and herbage coming out and growing. He puts the increase of wealth and ease and good under the same figure, a thing that grows as a plant grows, going on and growing.

פִּי־צַדִּיק יָנוּב חָכְמָה (Mishlei 10:31), the mouth of a tzaddik brings forth wisdom: speech too is called by this word, being the fruit of the tongue. Hence the noun in ניב שפתים (Yeshayahu 57:19), the speech of the lips, and וְנִיבוֹ נִבְזֶה אָכְלוֹ (Malachi 1:12), its speech, its food, is despised.

more.h: What the new wine does to the young
more.t: וְתִירוֹשׁ יְנוֹבֵב בְּתֻלוֹת (Zechariah 9:17) he reads twice over. In one reading the verb carries over to a third party: the grain and the wine gladden the young men and the maidens and set them breaking into song, that they will eat and drink and rejoice on the day of that deliverance. His father reads the surrounding words, כִּי מַה־טּוּבוֹ וּמַה־יָפְיוֹ, how great is its goodness and its beauty, of the grain and the wine that raise up those young men and those maidens when they ask rain of Hashem and He gives grass in the field to every man (Zechariah 10:1); so from Hashem's help and from the plenty of grain and wine the young men and maidens are fair and strong.

זוז.sense: The doorpost of a gate: מְזוּזָה, the jamb at its side.

more.t: In מְזוּזָה the mem is an addition and the final heh is the feminine ending: וּמְזוּזָתָם אֵצֶל מְזוּזָתִי (Yechezkel 43:8), their doorpost beside My doorpost, and in the plural וּכְתַבְתָּם עַל־מְזֻזוֹת בֵּיתֶךָ (Devarim 6:9), you shall write them on the doorposts of your house. They are the cheeks of the gateway.

more.h: At the post, or on the sill
more.t: וְעָמַד עַל־מְזוּזַת הַשַּׁעַר (Yechezkel 46:2) he reads as standing next to the doorpost of the gate, not upon it. Targum Yonasan takes the word here as a threshold, and renders that he stood on the sill of the gate. So too עַל־מְזוּזַת הֵיכַל (Shmuel I 1:9), which he reads as next to the doorpost, while Targum Yonasan renders it at the side of the threshold of the Heichal.

כסף.sense: To long for, to yearn; and the noun כֶּסֶף, silver.

more.t: כְּאַרְיֵה יִכְסוֹף לִטְרוֹף (Tehillim 17:12), like a lion longing to tear, and לְמַעֲשֵׂה יָדֶיךָ תִכְסֹף (Iyov 14:15), You will long for the work of Your hands. So נִכְסְפָה וְגַם־כָּלְתָה נַפְשִׁי (Tehillim 84:3), my soul longed and pined, and כִּי־נִכְסֹף נִכְסַפְתָּה לְבֵית אָבִיךָ (Bereishis 31:30), you longed sorely for your father's house. He gathers them all as desire and yearning.

more.h: The nation that feels no shame
more.t: הַגּוֹי לֹא נִכְסָף (Tzefaniah 2:1) he puts with the rest, a nation that does not long. His father reads it otherwise, a nation that has no shame in it, from the word the Gemara uses (Bava Basra 111a) for a man ashamed.

זָהָב וָכֶסֶף (Shemos 25:3), gold and silver, and the plural כספים in וּלְהָשִׁיב כַּסְפֵּיהֶם אִישׁ אֶל־שַׂקּוֹ (Bereishis 42:25), to put back each man's money into his sack. The sense, he says, is known.

מכר.sense: To sell; and the nouns מֶכֶר and מִמְכָּר, the thing sold.

more.t: כִּי־מָכְרוּ מִצְרַיִם (Bereishis 47:20), for the Egyptians sold; וְכִי־יִמְכֹּר אִישׁ (Shemos 21:7), if a man sells; מִכְרָה כַיּוֹם (Bereishis 25:31), sell me it this day. Of being sold: הֵן בַּעֲוֹנֹתֵיכֶם נִמְכַּרְתֶּם (Yeshayahu 50:1), you were sold for your sins, and כִּי נִמְכַּרְנוּ אֲנִי וְעַמִּי (Esther 7:4), we are sold, I and my people. Being handed over is the same word: וַיִּמְכְּרֵם בְּיַד כּוּשַׁן רִשְׁעָתַיִם (Shoftim 3:8), He sold them into the hand of Kushan Rishasayim.

אֲשֶׁר הִתְמַכֵּר לַעֲשׂוֹת הָרַע (Melachim I 21:25) and הִתְמַכֶּרְךָ לַעֲשׂוֹת הָרַע (Melachim I 21:20) are still selling: from the force of his labour at the sins it is as though he had sold himself to that work. So also וְהִתְמַכַּרְתֶּם שָׁם לְאֹיְבֶיךָ (Devarim 28:68), and there you will put yourselves up for sale to your enemies.

לְבַד מִמְכָּרָיו עַל־הָאָבוֹת (Devarim 18:8) he reads as: apart from what the fathers sold one to another in the days of David and Shmuel, when the watches were fixed and they traded among themselves, you take your week and I will take mine.

כְּלֵי חָמָס מְכֵרֹתֵיהֶם (Bereishis 49:5) some have explained as their dwellings, the word being like מְכֹרֹתַיִךְ וּמֹלְדֹתַיִךְ (Yechezkel 16:3), your origin and your birth, and like בְּאֶרֶץ מְכֻרוֹתַיִךְ (Yechezkel 21:35), in the land of your origin. The Targum goes that way, that in the land of your sojourning He will call you to account. Yelamdenu says instead that the word is Greek, for they call swords מכיר"י.

רוח.sense: Relief, the opposite of distress; and רוּחַ, which is wind, air, breath, a quarter of the sky, will, spirit and soul.

more.t: וְרָוַח לְשָׁאוּל (Shmuel I 16:23), Shaul had relief, and אֲדַבְּרָה וְיִרְוַח־לִי (Iyov 32:20), let me speak and find relief. The noun is רֶוַח וְהַצָּלָה (Esther 4:14), relief and rescue, and וְרֶוַח תָּשִׂימוּ (Bereishis 32:17), you shall put a space between; another form is כִּי הָיְתָה הָרְוָחָה (Shemos 8:11), when there was respite. The sense, he says, is known, and it is the opposite of straits.

Rabbi Yonah put לְרוּחַ הַיּוֹם (Bereishis 3:8) here, at the hour of the day's ease, when its air turns cool. He himself allows the plain sense of a wind that blows, the turn of the day when the wind comes up; and then מתהלך in the pasuk goes back to the wind or to the voice, as in קוֹלָהּ כַּנָּחָשׁ יֵלֵךְ (Yirmiyahu 46:22), her voice goes like a serpent's.

more.h: Wind, and what is winnowed by it
more.t: וְרוּחַ גְּדוֹלָה וְחָזָק (Melachim I 19:11), a great strong wind, and רוּחַ־קָדִים (Shemos 10:13), an east wind. From this comes אֲשֶׁר־זֹרֶה בָרַחַת (Yeshayahu 30:24), winnowed with the רַחַת, the implement grain is winnowed with, so called because they toss it into the wind. Rabbi Yaakov ben Elazar put וְהוֹרַדְתִּי בָרִיחִים כֻּלָּם (Koheles 43:14 in his edition) here too: they are ships, named so because they go by the wind; Targum Yonasan renders that He brought them all down with oars.

more.h: The four winds and the four sides
more.t: וְהֵבֵאתִי אֶל עֵילָם אַרְבַּע רוּחוֹת (Yirmiyahu 49:36), I will bring four winds upon Eilam, he reads as four kingdoms, likened to wind because a strong wind wrecks and breaks the high cedars; and the number is truly four, since evil will come on them from every side and corner. From this a quarter of the sky is itself called רוּחַ, there being four winds to the four sides: מָדַד רוּחַ הַצָּפוֹן (Yechezkel 42:17), he measured the north side, and לְאַרְבַּע רוּחוֹת מְדָדוֹ (Yechezkel 42:20), he measured it to the four sides. Some put here also סוֹבֵב סֹבֵב הוֹלֵךְ הָרוּחַ (Koheles 1:6), round and round it goes, saying it is said of the sun going round the quarters.

The word is also the spirit that speaks in a navi: כֹּל אֲשֶׁר הָיָה בָרוּחַ עִמּוֹ (Divrei HaYamim I 28:12), all that was with him in spirit, and וְרוּחֲךָ הַטּוֹבָה נָתַתָּ לְהַשְׂכִּילָם (Nechemiah 9:20), You gave Your good spirit to teach them. וַיֵּצֵא הָרוּחַ וַיַּעֲמֹד לִפְנֵי (Melachim I 22:21), the spirit came out and stood before Him, is the spirit of prophecy or else an angel; and וְסוּסֵיהֶם בָּשָׂר וְלֹא־רוּחַ (Yeshayahu 31:3), their horses are flesh and not spirit, means not an angel, an angel being a thing of spirit.

It is a man's will: עֵקֶב הָיְתָה רוּחַ אַחֶרֶת עִמּוֹ (Bamidbar 14:24), because another spirit was with him, and כָּל־רוּחוֹ יוֹצִיא כְסִיל (Mishlei 29:11), a fool lets out all his will. It is the soul: וְהָרוּחַ תָּשׁוּב אֶל־הָאֱלֹהִים אֲשֶׁר נְתָנָהּ (Koheles 12:7), and the spirit returns to Hashem who gave it, sometimes any of the three souls and sometimes the highest alone; or the one seated in the heart, where anger lives, so אַל־תְּבַהֵל בְּרוּחֲךָ לִכְעוֹס (Koheles 7:9), do not be hasty in your spirit to be angry. And it is the breath: רוּחִי זָרָה לְאִשְׁתִּי (Iyov 19:17), my breath is strange to my wife, and וּבְרוּחַ שְׂפָתָיו יָמִית רָשָׁע (Yeshayahu 11:4), by the breath of his lips he will slay the wicked, which he reads as the speech of the lips, since speech leaves the mouth on the breath. His father reads וַהֲרִיחוֹ בְּיִרְאַת (Yeshayahu 11:3) here as well, that his speech will be in the fear of Hashem.

לקק.sense: To lap, as a dog laps water with its tongue; he glosses it as licking and says the word is plainly known.

more.t: Beside the dogs stands הַמֲלַקְקִים בְּיָדָם אֶל־פִּיהֶם (Shoftim 7:6), the men who lapped by bringing the hand to the mouth.

רעל.sense: רַעַל, the thing that makes a man reel; the authorities differ whether that is bewilderment, trembling, or deadly poison.

more.h: What it does to a man
more.t: Rabbi Yonah takes the whole of it as bewilderment and tumult. His father reads תַּרְעֵלָה, the cup of reeling, and הָרְעָלוּ as trembling. He adds that it is the way among us to explain it as deadly poison.

A second sense in וְהַשֵּׁירוֹת וְהָרְעָלוֹת (Yeshayahu 3:19). Some read it by a la'az word; some from the Mishnah's ערביות יוצאות רעולות, Arab women go out veiled, which the Geonim explained as a scarf set over the head covering the whole face, so that nothing shows but the eyes, and tied below.
On הָרְעָלוּ he renders that the chiefs of their camps are wrapped in coloured stuff; on וְהָרְעָלוֹת he gives חֲנִיסְנְסַיָא, the word he uses for וְהָחַמָּנִים (Yeshayahu 17:8).

עכס.sense: The anklet, an ornament women wear on the foot that rattles as they walk; and the fetter, called by the same word because it rattles too.

more.t: אֵת תִּפְאֶרֶת הָעֲכָסִים (Yeshayahu 3:18) are the anklets, and וּבְרַגְלֵיהֶם תְּעַכַּסְנָה (Yeshayahu 3:16) is that they set them rattling on their feet.
Because it rattles in the same way, the shackle is called עכס: וּכְעֶכֶס אֶל־מוּסַר אֱוִיל (Mishlei 7:22), like a fetter to the chastening of a fool.

כהן.sense: To serve as a kohen; the כֹּהֵן is one who serves in eminence, and the word reaches to servants of avodah zarah, to counsellors and to chief men.

more.t: הַכֹּהֲנִים הַנִּגָּשִׁים (Shemos 19:22), the kohanim who draw near, he reads of the firstborn, since the service then was with the firstborn of Israel; anyone who serves is called a kohen.

One who serves avodah zarah carries the same word: כֹהֵן מִדְיָן (Shemos 18:1), the priest of Midyan, and רַק אַדְמַת הַכֹּהֲנִים לֹא קָנָה (Bereishis 47:22), only the land of the priests he did not buy.

הָיָה כֹהֵן לְדָוִד (Shmuel II 20:25) is his servant and counsellor, heeded before all the rest, for a trusted friend serves the one he loves by sound counsel. So too אַתָּה כֹהֵן לְעוֹלָם (Tehillim 110:4), a servant of Hashem and head of Israel, because you are a king of righteousness, as the kohen is head of the people.

In several places it is simply the chief men: וּמְיֻדָּעָיו וְכֹהֲנָיו (Melachim II 10:11), his intimates and his chiefs, מוֹלִיךְ כֹּהֲנִים שׁוֹלָל (Iyov 12:19), leading chiefs away stripped, and חֶבֶר כֹּהֲנִים (Hoshea 6:9), a band of chiefs. Apart from these, יְכַהֵן פְּאֵר (Yeshayahu 61:10) is that he makes his splendour great with fine garments.

וּבְנֵי דָוִד כֹּהֲנִים הָיוּ (Shmuel II 8:18): Divrei HaYamim in its place has וּבְנֵי דָוִיד הָרִאשֹׁנִים לְיַד הַמֶּלֶךְ (Divrei HaYamim 18:17, as his edition prints it), the first at the king's hand, and Yonasan renders רַבְרְבִין הֲווֹ, they were chiefs. He allows also that they were servants of Hashem and fearers of Him, but holds the first reading the true one because of what Divrei HaYamim says.

כמר.sense: To be stirred and to grow hot, as a man's mercy is stirred; the כְּמָרִים, black-robed servants of avodah zarah, are named from it; and a second sense, the hunter's net.

more.t: כִּי נִכְמְרוּ רַחֲמָיו אֶל־אָחִיו (Bereishis 43:30), his mercies were stirred toward his brother, and יַחַד נִכְמְרוּ נִחוּמָי (Hoshea 11:8). They were rolled over and moved, as the Targum has it, or else they grew hot; and close to that is עוֹרֵנוּ כְּתַנּוּר נִכְמָרוּ (Eichah 5:10), our skin was blackened like an oven.

Named from that blackening are the כְּמָרִים, וְהִשְׁבִּית אֶת־הַכְּמָרִים (Melachim II 23:5), servants of avodah zarah who dress in black. In אֶת־שֵׁם הַכְּמָרִים עִם־הַכֹּהֲנִים (Tzefaniah 1:4) the second word is the rest of the servants of avodah zarah, those not dressed in black.

A second sense: כְּתוֹא מִכְמָר (Yeshayahu 51:20), like a wild ox in a net, with וּפֹרְשֵׂי מִכְמֹרֶת (Yeshayahu 19:8), those who spread a net, and וְיַאַסְפֵהוּ בְּמִכְמַרְתּוֹ (Chavakuk 1:15), he gathers him in his net. They are the nets men hunt with.

צבר.sense: To heap up, to pile in heaps; and the noun צִבּוּר, a heap, which he glosses as a gathering.

more.t: וַיִּצְבֹּר עָפָר וַיִּלְכְּדָהּ (Chavakuk 1:10) is the pouring out of a siege ramp, as at the root סָלַל; or else that he heaped up a people like dust and took the city.
שִׂימוּ אֹתָם שְׁנֵי צִבֻּרִים (Melachim II 10:8), set them in two heaps.

פרס.sense: To break bread with the hands and hand it out; a second sense, the פַּרְסָה, the cloven hoof; and the פֶּרֶס, a large bird of the wilderness.

more.t: פֹּרֵשׂ אֵין לָהֶם (Eichah 4:4), none breaks bread for them, and וּפָרְשֲׂו כַּאֲשֶׁר בַּסִּיר (Michah 3:3) are written with a sin, yet they are the same breaking with the hands; so is הנותן פרוסה לעני in the words of Chazal, one who gives a piece of bread to a poor man. The Mesorah counts every such word with a sin but for two written with a samech, הֲלוֹא פָרֹס לָרָעֵב לַחְמֶךָ, is it not to break your bread for the hungry, and וְלֹא יִפְרְסוּ לָהֶם.

The word is used too of the hands and the body flung about in mourning out of great grief: תִּתְיַפֵּחַ תְּפָרֵשׂ כַּפֶּיהָ (Yirmiyahu 4:31), she gasps and spreads her hands, and פֵּרְשָׂה צִיּוֹן בְּיָדֶיהָ (Eichah 1:17), Tzion spread out her hands.

more.h: No one breaks bread for the mourner
more.t: וְלֹא יִפְרְסוּ לָהֶם עַל־אֵבֶל (Yirmiyahu 16:7) he reads as that none will come to comfort him for the dead, none lamenting the dead and none comforting the living. The commentators read it of the mourner's meal, where bread is broken and cut for him. His father reads פֵּרְשָׂה צִיּוֹן the same way: comforters break bread for a mourner, and she broke it with her own hands, having no comforter.

כֹּל מַפְרֶסֶת פַּרְסָה (Vayikra 11:3) is that it has two hooves, and וְשֹׁסַעַת שֶׁסַע that they are split below as they are above; for there is an animal whose hooves are split above and joined below, like the camel, the bear, the dog and the cat. The noun comes also in the masculine, וּפַרְסֵיהֶן יְפָרֵק (Zecharyah 11:16), he will tear off their hooves.

וְאֶת־הַפֶּרֶס (Vayikra 11:13) is a large bird that dwells in the wilderness, since Chazal say that the peres and the ozniah are not commonly found in settled places. Rabbi Yonah wrote that the Arabic name for it is עקא"ב.

רגם.sense: To stone, to pelt with stones; the מַרְגֵּמָה is a gathering of stones, and רִגְמָה a gathered company.

more.t: וְרָגְמוּ אֹתוֹ כָּל־הָעֵדָה (Vayikra 24:14), the whole congregation shall stone him, and יִרְגְּמֻהוּ בָאָבֶן (Vayikra 20:2), they shall stone him with the stone.

כִּצְרוֹר אֶבֶן בְּמַרְגֵּמָה (Mishlei 26:8) he takes as stones gathered together, with אבן there a precious stone. His father reads בְּמַרְגֵּמָה as אַרְגָּמָן, purple: binding a common street stone into purple cloth is what giving honour to a fool is like.

שָׂרֵי יְהוּדָה רִגְמָתָם (Tehillim 68:28) he glosses as their company, and some explain it as princes. At וְרֶגֶם מֶלֶךְ וַאֲנָשָׁיו Yonasan gives no rendering of ורגם מלך, and perhaps, he says, these were two men so named, which Radak takes to be the right reading.

סקל.sense: To stone; and turned about, to clear a place of its stones.

more.t: סַקְּלוּ מֵאֶבֶן (Yeshayahu 62:10), clear it of stone, turns the sense about, he says, because the word is joined to a mem; and וַיְעַזְּקֵהוּ וַיְסַקְּלֵהוּ (Yeshayahu 5:2), which has no such word attached, is that he cleared the vineyard of its stones.

more.h: His father makes it one sense
more.t: His father holds them all one sense: ויסקלהו is that he built it a wall of stones after digging the trench round it, which is ויעזקהו, as Chazal use עוזק; and סַקְּלוּ מֵאֶבֶן is to make a highway raised up out of great stones.

יסר.sense: To chasten and correct, whether by words or by blows; and a second family of nouns, bonds, which he sets down as binding.

more.t: מוּסַר שְׁלוֹמֵנוּ עָלָיו (Yeshayahu 53:5), the chastening of our peace was upon him, and מוּסַר הֲבָלִים עֵץ הוּא (Yirmiyahu 10:8), the chastening of vanities is wood.
מוסר, he says, is sometimes in words and sometimes in blows. So וְיִסְּרוֹ לַמִּשְׁפָּט (Yeshayahu 28:26) is the striking of the plough's fists as the manner of sowing requires.

הֲרֹב עִם־שַׁדַּי יִסּוֹר (Iyov 40:2) he takes as an infinitive, chastening. His father takes יִסּוֹר for a noun like מוּסַר, and reads the pasuk as asking whether it is the way of מוסר that a man should quarrel with Shaddai.

מוּסַר מְלָכִים פִּתֵּחַ (Iyov 12:18), He loosens the bond of kings, מוֹסְרֵי צַוָּארֵךְ (Yeshayahu 52:2), the bands of your neck, and נִתְּקוּ מוֹסֵרוֹת (Yirmiyahu 5:5), the bonds are snapped. He sets them all down as binding.

יכח.sense: To reprove, and to argue a case out with another, claim against claim; and in two places, to appoint.

more.t: הֲמִיִּרְאָתְךָ יֹכִיחֶךָ (Iyov 22:4) is that He will argue with you, that is, plead with you; and he sets the whole family down as words set one against another in claims, with judgments made known.

וְאֶת־כֹּל וְנֹכָחַת (Bereishis 20:16) he reads as Moshe's own words: with all that befell her through saying he is my brother, with Pharaoh and with Avimelech, Sarah was reproved and chastened out of ever saying it again.

טוֹבָה תּוֹכַחַת מְגֻלָּה (Mishlei 27:5) he reads as love made plain in reproof, as in הוֹכַח לְחָכָם וְיֶאֱהָבֶךָּ (Mishlei 9:8), reprove a wise man and he will love you: such love is better than a love kept hidden in the heart, never revealed and never reproving a fellow when reproof is called for. His father reads it otherwise: reproof is good in any case, even in the open, but where it comes of love it is hidden, the lover reproving the one he loves in private so as not to shame him.

Close to this sense, he says, are אֲשֶׁר הֹכִיחַ (Bereishis 24:44) and אֹתָהּ הֹכַחְתָּ לְעַבְדְּךָ לְיִצְחָק (Bereishis 24:14), which he glosses זִמֵּן, appointed, and זִמַּנְתָּ, You have appointed.

שׁכם.sense: To rise early and set out at dawn; and שְׁכֶם, the shoulder at the neck, which stretches to mean a side, a quarter, a portion.

more.t: וְהִשְׁכַּמְתֶּם וַהֲלַכְתֶּם לְדַרְכְּכֶם (Bereishis 19:2), you will rise early and go your way, and מַשְׁכִּימֵי קוּם (Tehillim 127:2), those who rise early. וְכַטַּל מַשְׁכִּים הֹלֵךְ (Hoshea 6:4) is dew that goes off early in the morning, and of the horses מַשְׁכִּים הָיוּ (Yirmiyahu 5:8) is that they were so every morning; he notes he has given another explanation of that one at the root מָשַׁך.

עַל־שְׁכֶם שְׁנֵיהֶם (Bereishis 9:23) and וַיֵּט שִׁכְמוֹ (Bereishis 49:15): what lies on the כָּתֵף against the neck is what is called שכם, as in כְּתֵפִי מִשִּׁכְמָה תִפּוֹל (Iyov 31:22), let my shoulder fall from the place at the neck.

Because the shoulder is a side, כִּי תְּשִׁיתֵמוֹ שֶׁכֶם (Tehillim 21:13) is to one side and one quarter; לְעָבְדוֹ שְׁכֶם אֶחָד (Tzefaniah 3:9) is with one heart and one mind; וַאֲנִי נָתַתִּי לְךָ שְׁכֶם אַחַד (Bereishis 48:22) is one portion. All of it one sense, and the side itself is called כָּתֵף, as in וְלַכָּתֵף הַשֵּׁנִית (Shemos 27:15), for the second side.

כתף.sense: The shoulder that carries a load; and from it a side or a flank, of a building or of a land.

more.t: כְתֵפֹת חֹבְרֹת (Shemos 28:7), joined shoulder pieces, are so called because they sat on the shoulders.

וְלַכָּתֵף הַשֵּׁנִית (Shemos 27:15), for the second side, and וְכִתְפוֹת הַפֶּתַח (Yechezkel 41:2), the sides of the doorway, are a side and a flank; so אֶל־כֶּתֶף הַבַּיִת (Melachim I 6:8), at the side of the house.

וְעָפוּ בְכָתֵף פְּלִשְׁתִּים (Yeshayahu 11:14) he takes as the Pelishtim being weary and weak in their shoulder, that is, in their land; or from the first sense, that Israel will be weary of shoulder from striking the Pelishtim so much. Targum Yonasan renders that they will join as one shoulder to strike the Pelishtim.

שׁיר.sense: שֵׁירוֹת, bracelets worn as ornaments; he fixes the sense from the way the Targum renders them.

more.t: At הַנְּטִיפוֹת וְהַשֵּׁירוֹת (Yeshayahu 3:19) it gives עַנְקַיָא וְשֵׁירֵי, neck chains and bracelets; at הַפְּאֵרִים וְהַצְּעָדוֹת (Yeshayahu 3:20) it gives כְּלִילַיָא וְשֵׁירֵי רְגִלַיָא, garlands and bands of the legs; and at חַחִים בִּלְחָיֶיךָ (Yechezkel 29:4) it gives וְאֶתֵּן שִׁירִין בְּלִיסָתָךְ, I will set rings in your jaws.

זמר.sense: To sing praise, with the songs and the instruments of it; a second sense, to prune the vine, with the branch and the pruning knife; and the name of an animal.

more.t: וְזִמְרָת there lacks the yud of the speaker, its proper form being וְזִמְרָתי, my song. The proof is the kamatz under the resh, since a construct word would be shorter, as וְזִמְרַת נְבָלֶיךָ (Amos 5:23), the music of your harps; and a greater proof than the vowel is the sense, since it stands beside עָזִּי, my strength.

מִזְמוֹר (Tehillim 3:1), זְמִרוֹת הָיוּ־לִי חֻקֶּיךָ (Tehillim 119:54), Your statutes were songs to me, and מְזַמְּרוֹת מִזְרָקוֹת חֲצֹצְרוֹת (Melachim II 12:14), which he says are the instruments they make music on.

וְהִנָּם שֹׁלְחִים אֶת־הַזְּמוֹרָה אֶל־אַפָּם (Yechezkel 8:17) he reads of the foul smell. קְחוּ מִזִּמְרַת הָאָרֶץ (Bereishis 43:11) is the choicest of the fruits of the land, which he holds near the first sense, since the best and most praised part of a song is called זָמִיר.

more.h: The vine branch and its cutting
more.t: הַזְּמוֹרָה אֲשֶׁר הָיָה בַּעֲצֵי הַיָּעַר (Yechezkel 15:2) and וּזְמֹרַת זָר תִּזְרָעֶנּוּ (Yeshayahu 17:10) are a vine or a single plant, and mostly the vine. The verb is וְכַרְמְךָ לֹא תִזְמֹר (Vayikra 25:4), you shall not prune your vineyard, and the tool is in וְכָרַת הַזַּלְזַלִּים בַּמַּזְמֵרוֹת (Yeshayahu 18:5), he cuts the shoots with pruning knives.

Rabbi Yonah explained זְמִיר עָרִיצִים יַעֲנֶה (Yeshayahu 25:5) from the cutting sense, taking יַעֲנֶה as he will call, that Hashem will call for the cutting down of the tyrants. He holds the right reading to be that יענה is he will subdue, the cutting that comes from Hashem subduing the tyrants, with זמיר not in construct. He allows too that it may be of the first sense, the song and delight the tyrants take pleasure in subduing them.
וּתְאוֹ וָזָמֶר (Devarim 14:5) is the name of an animal; Rabbi Yonah wrote that the Arabic name for it is זוֹרָאפַ"ה.

תעה.sense: To stray, to wander off the way, of a man lost in a field, of a heart, and of one gone astray in drink; and to lead another astray.

more.t: תָּעָה לְבָבִי (Yeshayahu 21:4), my heart wanders, תָּעִיתִי כְּשֶׂה אֹבֵד (Tehillim 119:176), I have strayed like a lost sheep, וּבַשֵּׁכָר תָּעוּ (Yeshayahu 28:7), through strong drink they went astray, and וְהִנֵּה תֹעֶה בַּשָּׂדֶה (Bereishis 37:15), wandering in the field.

more.h: A form taken apart two ways
more.t: וְשִׁנֵּי כְפִירִים נִתָּעוּ (Iyov 4:10), of the teeth of the young lions, carries a form the authorities take apart differently. Rabbi Yonah holds it a word compounded within this one pattern out of past and future. His brother Rabbi Moshe wrote that it is compounded of two patterns, its proper form being נִתְתָּעוּ, like וְנִכַּפֵּר לָהֶם הַדָּם (Devarim 21:8); and he notes he has written of it at the root לתע.

כִּי רוּחַ זְנוּנִים הִתְעָה (Hoshea 4:12), a spirit of harlotry has led astray, and עַמִּי מְאַשְּׁרֶיךָ מַתְעִים (Yeshayahu 3:12), those who guide you lead you astray. At וְעוֹזֵב תּוֹכַחַת מַתְעֶה (Mishlei 10:17) he says the verb stands on its own, like תּוֹעֶה, one straying, or else that he leads his own soul astray.

חוג.sense: To go round, to draw a circle; and the noun חוּג, the circle that goes round the earth or the heavens.

more.t: חֹק חָג עַל־פְּנֵי־מָיִם (Iyov 26:10), He inscribed a circle upon the face of the waters. The word means to go round.

הַיּשֵׁב עַל־ חוּג הָאָרֶץ (Yeshayahu 40:22), He who sits upon the circle of the earth, is the sphere that turns about the earth. So too וְחוּג שָׁמַיִם יִתְהַלָּֽךְ (Iyov 22:14), He walks the circle of the heavens, and בְּחוּקוֹ חוּג (Mishlei 8:27), when He inscribed a circle.
מְחוּגָה is the instrument with which a circle is drawn and set true: וּבַמְּחוּגָה יְתָֽאֳרֵהוּ (Yeshayahu 44:13), he marks it out with the compass. He gives its name in the vernacular.

נבא.sense: A prophet, and the verb: to receive prophecy from Hashem and speak it. נְבִיאָה is a prophetess.

more.t: יִהְיֶה נְבִיאֶֽךָ (Shemos 7:1), he shall be your prophet, answers to יִֽהְיֶה־לְּךָ לְפֶה (Shemos 4:16), he shall be a mouth for you: as the prophet speaks to the people on the mission of Hashem, so Aharon speaks on Moshe's mission whatever Moshe tells him.
וָֽאֶקְרַב אֶל־ הַנְּבִיאָה (Yeshayahu 8:6), and I drew near to the prophetess: she is called a prophetess because she was the prophet's wife.

וְגַם לְנֽוֹעַדְיָה הַנְּבִיאָה (Nechemiah 6:14), and also to Noadiah the prophetess. Rabbi Yonah wrote that the word stands for הַנָבִיא, the prophet, Noadiah being no woman, and that he is Shemayah ben Delayah, called Noadiah for his saying נִוָּעֵד אֶל־בֵּית הָֽאֱלֹהִים (Nechemiah 6:10), let us meet in the house of Hashem. He rejects this: the language does not make a feminine into a masculine and a masculine into a feminine, and he has written of the like, with his view on them, in the grammar. Noadiah was a woman, a false prophetess whom Sanvalat and Toviah hired to frighten Nechemiah, as they hired the other prophets who were making him afraid.

more.h: Why the word comes as a passive
more.t: Its sense is the receiving of prophecy from Hashem and the speaking of it to the one he is sent to, a single man or many. So אֲשֶׁר נִבֵּאתָ (Yirmiyahu 28:6), which you prophesied; וְנִבֵּאתִי כַּֽאֲשֶׁר צֻוֵּיתִי (Yechezkel 37:7), and I prophesied as I was commanded; and הִנָּבֵא בֶן־אָדָם (Yechezkel 38:14), prophesy, son of man. מַדּוּעַ נִבֵּיתָ (Yirmiyahu 26:9), why did you prophesy, is written with a yud.

הֵמָּה מִֽתְנַבְּאִים (Yirmiyahu 14:14), they prophesy; וַיִּֽתְנַבְּאוּ עַד לַֽעֲלוֹת הַמִּנְחָה (Melachim I 18:29), and they prophesied until the offering went up; הִנַּבְּאוּ בַבַּעַל (Yirmiyahu 23:13), they prophesied by the Baal, whose rule is הִתְנַּבְּאוּ. At וַיִּתְנַבֵּא בְתוֹךְ־הַבַּיִת (Shmuel I 18:10), and he prophesied inside the house, the Targum has וְאִישְׁתַּטִי בְּגוֹ בֵיתָא, he played the madman in the house.

חזה.sense: To see, and often the seeing of prophecy: the חֹזֶה, seer, and the חָזוֹן, vision. Separately חָזֶה, the breast of an offering.

more.t: יִשְׂמַח צַדִּיק כִּי־ חָזָה נָקָם (Tehillim 58:11), the righteous man rejoices when he sees vengeance; וְזֶֽה־ חָזִיתִי וַֽאֲסַפֵּֽרָה (Iyov 15:17), this I have seen and will tell; וְתַחַז בְּצִיּוֹן עֵינֵֽינוּ (Michah 4:11), let our eyes gaze upon Tzion. The Targum of רָאָה (Bereishis 29:10) is חֲזָא, and of these some are plain seeing and some the sight of prophecy.

מַשָּׂא גֵּיא חִזָּיוֹן (Yeshayahu 22:1), the burden of the valley of vision; כְּחֶזְיוֹן לָֽיְלָה (Iyov 20:8), like a night vision, and in the plural מֵֽחֶזְיוֹנוֹת לָיְלָה (Iyov 4:13), out of night visions; חָזוֹן נִרְאָה אֵלַי (Daniel 8:1), a vision appeared to me, without the yud; בַּֽמַּֽחֲזֶה לֵאמֹר (Bereishis 15:1), in a vision, saying; and חָזוּת קשׁה (Yeshayahu 21:2), a hard vision.
וּמֶחֱזָה אֶל־ מֶחֱזָה (Melachim I 7:4), window opposite window, is the feminine form, and Targum Yonasan renders it וּזְוִי לָקֳבֵיל זְוִי, an opening facing an opening.

more.h: What was made with the grave
more.t: וְעִם־שְׁאוֹל עָשִׂינוּ חֹזֶה (Yeshayahu 28:15), and with the grave we have made a חֹזֶה. Rabbi Yonah read it: we have set a watchman with the grave who will tell us when it comes, and when its time draws near we will push it off. He himself holds it may be the seer of כָל־ חֹזֶה לֵאמֹר (Melachim II 17:13), every seer, saying: a seeing we have made with the grave, and a covenant we have cut with it that it not take us. עַל דִּבְרֵי חוֹזָֽי (Divrei HaYamim II 33:19), the words of the seers, stands for חוזים, and he points to the like at Yeshayahu 19:9.

בֵּית אֲבָנִים יֶחֱזֶֽה (Iyov 8:17), he looks upon a house of stones, is a different matter: it means יסתבך, he is entwined, and he links it to קֶרֶן חָזוּת (Daniel 8:5), a horn of vision. Rabbi Yehudah put וְעִם־שְׁאוֹל עָשִׂינוּ חֹזֶה into this same sense, and he says he does not know what Rabbi Yehudah held in either of them.

וַיִּקַּח מֹשֶׁה אֶת־ הֶחָזֶה (Vayikra 8:29), and Moshe took the breast; חֲזֵה הַתְּנוּפָה (Vayikra 7:34), the breast of the waving; in the plural עַל־ הֶֽחָזוֹת (Vayikra 9:20), upon the breasts. He says the word is well known and explains no further.

שׁקר.sense: To deal falsely, to break faith; the noun שֶׁקֶר, a falsehood, which in some pesukim means without cause.

more.t: אִם־ תִּשְׁקֹר לִי וּלְנִינִי (Bereishis 21:23), that you will not deal falsely with me or with my offspring; וְלֹֽא־ שִׁקַּרְנוּ בִּבְרִיתֶֽךָ (Tehillim 44:18), and we did not break faith with Your covenant; וְלֹֽא־תְכַֽחֲשׁוּ וְלֹֽא־ תְשַׁקְּרוּ (Vayikra 19:11), you shall not deny and you shall not deal falsely. The sense is lying and betrayal, and the Targum of מַדּוּעַ נִבְגַּד אִישׁ בְּאָחִיו (Malachi 2:10), why do we betray one another, uses this very verb.
