מִדְּבַר־ שֶׁקֶר תִּרְחָק (Shemos 23:7), keep far from a false word; דֹּבֵר שְׁקָרִים (Tehillim 101:7), a speaker of lies; בְּשִׁקְרֵיהֶם וּבְפַֽחֲזוּתָם (Yirmiyahu 23:32), by their lies and their recklessness.

Some of them carry the sense of חִנָּם, for nothing: אֹיְבַי שֶׁקֶר (Tehillim 35:19), my enemies without cause; שֶׁקֶר רְדָפוּנִי (Tehillim 119:86), they pursued me without cause; לַשֶּׁקֶר שָׁמַרְתִּי (Shmuel I 25:21), for nothing I kept guard; הִנֵּה לַשֶּׁקֶר עָשָׂה עֵט שֶׁקֶר סֹֽפְרִֽים (Yirmiyahu 8:8), the pen of the scribes has worked for nothing. The word שָׁוְא goes the same way.

שֹקר.sense: Of the eyes: to ogle, sharpening them and signalling with them.

more.t: וּֽמְשַׂקְּרוֹת עֵינָיִם (Yeshayahu 3:16), and ogling with the eyes: they sharpen their eyes and hint with them. He gives the vernacular word for it.

The Targum of עַיִן שְׁזָפַתּוּ (Iyov 20:9), an eye glimpsed him, is עֵינָא סְקַרְתֵּיהּ. Chazal use the same root in Bereishis Rabbah: were she created from the eye she would be a gazer, and Chava stood and was a gazer, as it says ותרא האשה, and the woman saw.

כזב.sense: To lie, and to be proved false; the noun כָּזָב, a lie; and of water, to fail.

more.t: כָּל־הָאָדָם כֹּזֵֽב (Tehillim 116:11), every man is a liar. He reads the pasuk as a declaration of great faith: even when the speaker was fleeing in his poverty and in his haste, he would still say that every man who says the kingship will not be his is a liar, and that saying is the great faith itself.

יוֹכִיחַ בְּךָ וְנִכְזָֽבְתָּ (Mishlei 30:6), He will rebuke you and you will be shown a liar; הֵן־תֹּחַלְתּוֹ נִכְזָבָה (Iyov 41:1), his hope is proved false. עֵד אֱמוּנִים לֹא יְכַזֵּב (Mishlei 14:5), a faithful witness does not lie, he takes even of matters that are not testimony, even of idle talk. וְאִם־לֹא אֵפוֹ מִי יַכְזִיבֵנִי (Iyov 24:25), and if not, who will prove me a liar, means who will make my words out to be a lie.

אֲשֶׁר לֹֽא־ יְכַזְּבוּ מֵימָֽיו (Yeshayahu 58:11), whose waters do not fail, he takes the way of וְתִירוֹשׁ יְכַחֶשׁ בָּֽהּ (Hoshea 9:2), the wine fails her, and כִּחֵשׁ מַֽעֲשֵׂה־זַיִת (Chavakuk 3:17), the olive crop fails.

תִֽהְיֶה לִי כְּמוֹ אַכְזָב (Yirmiyahu 15:18), will You be to me like a thing that fails: the prophet was complaining before Hashem, who had promised him נְתַתִּיךָ הַיּוֹם לְעִיר מִבְצָר (Yirmiyahu 1:18), I have made you today a fortified city, while they were cursing him and striking him. אַכְזָב is the same word as כזב, and its use here is elegance, since Achziv is the name of a town: בתי אַכְזִיב לְאַכְזָב (Michah 1:14), the houses of Achziv shall be a failing thing, and וּקְעִילָה וְאַכְזִיב וּמָֽרֵאשָׁה (Yehoshua 15:44), and Keilah and Achziv and Mareishah.

חכם.sense: To be wise, to grow wise; the noun חָכְמָה, wisdom, and the wise man, חָכָם.

more.t: בְּנִי אִם־ חָכַם לִבֶּךָ (Mishlei 23:16), my son, if your heart is wise; אִם־ חָכַמְתָּ חָכַמְתָּ לָּךְ (Mishlei 9:12), if you have grown wise, you have grown wise for yourself; שִׁמְעוּ מוּסָר וַֽחֲכָמוּ (Mishlei 8:33), hear discipline and grow wise; וַיֶּחְכַּם מִכָּל־הָֽאָדָם (Melachim I 5:11), and he was wiser than any man.

חָכְמוֹת בַּחוּץ תָּרֹנָּה (Mishlei 1:20), wisdom cries aloud in the street, and חָכְמוֹת בָּֽנְתָה בֵיתָהּ (Mishlei 9:1), wisdom has built her house: the plural means every wisdom there is. חַכְמוֹת נָשִׁים בָּֽנְתָה (Mishlei 14:1), the wise among women has built her house, is pointed with a patach and means each one of the women who are wise.

וּזְקֵנָיו יְחַכֵּֽם (Tehillim 105:22), and he makes his elders wise; וּמֵעוֹף הַשָּׁמַיִם יְחַכְּמֵֽנוּ (Iyov 35:11), and from the birds of the heavens He makes us wise; מֵאֹֽיְבַי תְּחַכְּמֵנִי מִצְוֹתֶךָ (Tehillim 119:98), Your commandments make me wiser than my enemies.
הָבָה נִּֽתְחַכְּמָה לוֹ (Shemos 1:10), come, let us deal shrewdly with him; וְאַל־ תִּתְחַכַּם יוֹתֵר (Koheles 7:16), and do not be wise overmuch.

בין.sense: To understand, to discern; תְּבוּנָה and בִּינָה, understanding. The same letters carry בֵּין, between.

more.t: בַּנְתָּה לְרֵעִי מֵרָחֽוֹק (Tehillim 139:2), You understand my thought from afar; עַם־חָכָם וְנָבוֹן (Devarim 4:6), a wise and understanding people; בִּינֹתִי בַּסְּפָרִים מִסְפַּר הַשָּׁנִים (Daniel 9:2), I understood from the books the number of the years. He suggests that אָבְדָה עֵצָה מִבָּנִים (Yirmiyahu 49:7), counsel is lost from the sons, may belong here as well, meaning from the understanding ones.

וְהַלְוִיִּם מְבִינִים אֶת־הָעָם לַתּוֹרָה (Nechemiah 8:7), and the Levi'im giving the people understanding in the Torah; מֵבִין פְּתָיִֽים (Tehillim 119:130), giving understanding to the simple; הָבֵן לְהַלָּז אֶת־הַמַּרְאֶֽה (Daniel 8:15), make this man understand the vision. Ibn Ezra reads אִם־ יָבִין מִפְרְשֵׂי־עָב (Iyov 36:29), can one understand the spreadings of cloud, in this way: as though understanding were set into the spreadings of cloud.

בְּטֶרֶם יָבִינוּ סִּֽירֹתֵיכֶם אָטָד (Tehillim 58:10), before your pots feel the thorn, is said by way of borrowing: before they feel the heat of the burning thorn beneath them. So too וּבִתְבוּנוֹת כַּפָּיו יַנְחֵֽם (Tehillim 78:72), and with the understanding of his palms he led them: understanding sits in the heart, but it is ascribed to the palms, since a shepherd leads his flock gently with the staff in his palm along a straight way so that they do not stumble.

לִתְבוּנָתוֹ אֵין מִסְפָּֽר (Tehillim 147:5), His understanding is without number, means that the things He has understanding in are without number, for understanding itself is not counted but searched out, as אֵין חֵקֶר לִתְבוּנָתֽוֹ (Yeshayahu 40:28), His understanding is past searching.

וַיַּרְא־אָוֶן וְלֹא יִתְבּוֹנָֽן (Iyov 11:11), and He sees iniquity and does not consider: he reads it of the man, that Hashem sees a man of iniquity, and the man does not consider that the Holy One sees him.

The same letters carry בֵּין: בֵּין הָאוֹר וּבֵין הַחֹֽשֶׁךְ (Bereishis 1:4), between the light and the darkness; בֵּין קֹדֶשׁ לְחֹל (Yechezkel 44:23), between holy and profane. From this comes אִישׁ־ הַבֵּנַיִם (Shmuel I 17:4), the man of the space between, the one standing between the two battle lines.

אתן.sense: אָתוֹן, the she-donkey. His entry under these letters holds that animal and nothing else.

more.t: וַתִּרְאַנִי הָֽאָתוֹן (Bamidbar 22:33), the she-donkey saw me, and אֲתֹנוֹת צְחֹרוֹת (Shoftim 5:10), white she-donkeys. He gives nothing beyond the two pesukim, and the entry breaks off as it turns to the words of four letters.

פרא.sense: פֶּרֶא, the wild donkey of the desert, and of a man, one as wild as that animal.

more.t: פֶּרֶא אָדָם (Bereishis 16:12), a wild donkey of a man, means a man of the wilderness like the wild donkey. It is written with a heh at פֶּרֶה לִמֻּד מִדְבָּר (Yirmiyahu 2:24), a wild donkey used to the wilderness, and the plural is הֵן פְּרָאִים בַּֽמִּדְבָּר (Iyov 24:5), wild donkeys in the desert. The animal is the wild ass.
כִּי הוּא בֵּן אַחִים יַפְרִיא (Hoshea 13:15), though he be fruitful among brothers, he takes as multiplying and bearing fruit. Rabbi Yonah read it instead as the word פֶּרֶא, the wild donkey.

פרד.sense: To be parted, to separate, and to part others; the noun פֶּרֶד, the mule.

more.h: Why the mule is so named
more.t: וַיָּבֹא הַפֶּרֶד (Shmuel II 18:9), and the mule came; עַל־ הַפִּרְדָּה אֲשֶֽׁר־לִי (Melachim I 1:33), upon my own she-mule; וּבַצַּבִּים וּבַפְּרָדִים (Yeshayahu 66:20), in wagons and on mules. Rav Hai Gaon wrote that it is called פֶּרֶד because it does not breed and stands apart.

הִפָּרֶד נָא מֵֽעָלָי (Bereishis 13:9), part from me, please; מִמֵּעַיִךְ יִפָּרֵדוּ (Bereishis 25:23), from your womb they shall be parted; יַפְרִיד בֵּינִי וּבֵינֵֽךְ (Rus 1:17), it should part me from you; וְהִתְפָּֽרְדוּ כָּל־עַצְמוֹתָי (Tehillim 22:9), and all my bones came apart. וְכַנְפֵיהֶם פְּרֻדוֹת (Yechezkel 1:11), their wings parted, means spread out, and עָֽבְשׁוּ פְרֻדוֹת תַּחַת מֶגְרְפֹתֵיהֶם (Yoel 1:17) is the grains of seed lying separated and scattered under the earth.

לְֽתַֽאֲוָה יְבַקֵּשׁ נִפְרָד (Mishlei 18:1), the one who keeps himself apart seeks his desire: he reads it of a man apart in his opinion and his counsel, who will not trust the counsel of his fellows, and בְּכָל־תּֽוּשִׁיָּה יִתְגַּלָּֽע, he breaks out against all sound wisdom, means he shows himself mixing into every wisdom while he only follows the desires of his heart. Rav Saadiah Gaon read the נִפְרָד as the traitor who separates from the body of the people and abandons their faith, who quarrels with every argument brought to him, which is why the next words are that the fool takes no delight in understanding.

כִּי־הֵם עִם־הַזֹּנוֹת יְפָרֵדוּ (Hoshea 4:14), for they part off with the harlots: he takes it as their parting the women from their husbands to sin with them. His father takes it from the mule, that they are as steeped in lewdness as the mule, no beast being so steeped in it. Others read that they do with the harlots what the mule does, which bears no fruit, lying with them in a way that begets nothing.

שׁמט.sense: To let go, to release, to let a thing drop; and of the oxen at the aron, to slip out from under it.

more.t: כִּי שָֽׁמְטוּ הַבָּקָֽר (Shmuel II 6:6), for the oxen slipped: they slipped out from under the aron. The Targum holds the verb takes an object, and it renders וְנִדְּחָה יָדוֹ (Devarim 19:5), and his hand slips, with the same Aramaic word. Rabbi Yonah read that the oxen's joints and limbs came apart before the greatness of the aron and its purity, and his father wrote the same.

תִּשְׁמְטֶנָּה וּנְטַשְׁתָּהּ (Shemos 23:11), you shall release the land and leave it; שָׁמוֹט כָּל־בַּעַל מַשֵּׁה יָדוֹ (Devarim 15:2), every creditor shall release what his hand holds; תַּשְׁמֵט יָדֶֽךָ (Devarim 15:3), your hand shall release. All of them mean leaving a thing and abandoning it, and the noun is שְׁנַת הַשְּׁמִטָּה, the year of release. Rabbi Yonah, he notes, let this last form drop and did not record it.

וְשָׁמַטְתָּה וּבְךָ מִנַּֽחֲלָֽתְךָ (Yirmiyahu 17:4), and you shall let go, and in you, from your inheritance: the release will fall upon you, that you be released from your inheritance, since you did not release it while you were in it.
וַיִּשְׁמְטוּהָ (Melachim II 9:33), and they let her drop; נִשְׁמְטוּ בִֽידֵי־סֶלַע שֹׁפְטֵיהֶם (Tehillim 141:6), their judges were let drop by the sides of the rock.

שׁלף.sense: To draw out: a sword from its sheath, a shoe from the foot; and of a shoot, to come up.

more.t: וְלֹֽא־ שָׁלַף הַנַּעַר חַרְבּוֹ (Shoftim 8:20), and the lad did not draw his sword; כִּי לֹא שָׁלַף הַחֶרֶב מִבִּטְנוֹ (Shoftim 3:22), for he did not draw the sword out of his belly; שֹׁלֵֽף חָרֶב (Shoftim 20:15), a drawer of the sword. They mean bringing the sword out of its sheath.

שָׁלַף אִישׁ נַֽעֲלוֹ (Rus 4:7), a man drew off his shoe, is like חלץ, to take off, and the Targum Yerushalmi renders וְחָֽלְצָה נַֽעֲלוֹ (Devarim 25:9), and she shall draw off his shoe, with this same word.

Where the verb stands without an object: שָׁלַף וַיֵּצֵא מִגֵּוָה (Iyov 20:25), he drew it out and it came from his body; שֶׁקַּדְמַת שָׁלַף יָבֵֽשׁ (Tehillim 129:6), which withers before it is drawn out, that is, before it comes out and shows itself it is already dry.

נשׁל.sense: To slip off and drop away; and of a person taking a thing off: the shoe from the foot, nations from their land.

more.t: וְנָשַׁל הַבַּרְזֶל מִן־הָעֵץ (Devarim 19:5), and the iron slips off the wood; כִּי יִשַּׁל זֵיתֶֽךָ (Devarim 28:40), for your olive tree will drop its fruit.

וְנָשַׁל גּֽוֹיִם־רַבִּים מִפָּנֶיךָ (Devarim 7:1), and He will cast out many nations before you; שַֽׁל ־נְעָלֶיךָ (Shemos 3:5), take your shoes off; וַיְנַשֵּׁל אֶת־הַיְהוּדִים מֵֽאֵילוֹת (Melachim II 16:6), and he drove the Yehudim out of Eilos. Their sense is removing a thing and drawing it away.

כִּי יֵשֶׁל אֱלוֹהַּ נַפְשֽׁוֹ (Iyov 27:8), when Hashem takes away his soul: the form should be יָשֵּׁל with a dagesh, and the quiescent letter came in its place, as at וַיָּזֶד יַֽעֲקֹב נָזִיד (Bereishis 25:29), and Yaakov cooked a stew. He says he will write more of it under the root שָׁלָה.

חשׁה.sense: To be silent, to hold one's peace; and of the waves of the sea, to be stilled.

more.h: Silence and the breaking of it
more.t: לְמַעַן צִיּוֹן לֹא אֶחֱשֶׁה (Yeshayahu 62:1), for the sake of Tzion I will not be silent; פֶּן־ תֶּֽחֱשֶׁה מִמֶּנִּי (Tehillim 28:1), lest You be silent toward me; וַיֶּחֱשׁוּ גַּלֵּיהֶֽם (Tehillim 107:29), and their waves were stilled; עֵת לַֽחֲשׁוֹת (Koheles 3:7), a time to be silent; הֶחֱשֵׁיתִי מֵֽעוֹלָם אַֽחֲרִישׁ (Yeshayahu 42:14), I have long kept silent, I will hold my peace.

more.h: הֶחֱשׁוּ, a command or a past?
more.t: גַּם־אֲנִי יָדַעְתִּי הֶֽחֱשֽׁוּ (Melachim II 2:3), I too know, be silent. Some say the last word is a command, and on that reading it should have been pointed with a patach. The right view is that it is past, as its form requires: when he said to them that he too knew, they fell silent and spoke to him no more.

וְהַֽלְוִיִּם מַחְשִׁים לְכָל־הָעָם (Nechemiah 8:11), and the Levi'im quieting all the people, is the one place where the verb takes an object. And וְאַתֶּם מַחְשִׁים אַל־תֵּעָצְלוּ (Shoftim 15:9), and you are silent, do not be idle.

שׁתק.sense: To fall quiet, to be still: strife, the sea, and the men upon it.

more.t: יִשְׁתֹּק מָדֽוֹן (Mishlei 26:20), strife falls quiet; וְיִשְׁתֹּק הַיָּם מֵֽעָלֵינוּ (Yonah 1:11), that the sea may be still from upon us; וַיִּשְׂמְחוּ כִֽי־ יִשְׁתֹּקוּ (Tehillim 107:30), and they rejoiced when they grew quiet. He says the sense of silence is well known, and adds nothing further.

דום.sense: Silence: שָֽׁכְנָה דוּמָה נַפְשִֽׁי (Tehillim 94:17), my soul dwelt in silence; and דוּמָה is also the name of a nation.

more.t: שָֽׁכְנָה דוּמָה נַפְשִֽׁי (Tehillim 94:17), my soul dwelt in silence, and כְּדֻמָה בְּתוֹךְ הַיָּֽם (Yechezkel 27:32), like one silenced in the midst of the sea; he glosses both as silenced or cut off. The noun stands in שְׁבִי דוּמָם (Yeshayahu 47:5), sit silent, on the pattern of יוֹמָם, save that the one has a shuruk and the other a cholam; and it may come from the root דָּמַם, as לְאֶבֶן דּוּמָם (Chavakuk 2:19), to a dumb stone.

גַּם־מַדְמֵן תִּדֹּמִּי (Yirmiyahu 48:2), Madmen too shall be silenced, is a form built on the four letter root; Rabbi Yehudah reads it as though it were תִּתְדּוֹֽמְמִי, and its sense as you shall be struck silent. The four letter root on its own gives אִם־לֹא שִׁוִּיתִי וְדֽוֹמַמְתִּ י (Tehillim 131:2), if I have not stilled and quieted myself.

Rabbi Yonah reads these words as loss and darkness, and so reads מַשָּׂא דּוּמָה אֵלַי קֹרֵא מִשֵּׂעִיר (Yeshayahu 21:11) of the perishing nation, which is מלכות הרשעה, the wicked kingdom, taking מִשֵּׂעִיר as though it were לשעיר, on account of Seir. He answers that there is no need for all this forcing: Dumah is the nation of that name among Yishmael's sons, וּמִשְׁמָע וְדוּמָה וּמַשָּֽׂא (Bereishis 25:14), Mishma and Dumah and Massa. From Seir the destroyer will come upon them, and out of fear of Seir they set watchmen on their towers, and in their great fear they rise at night and ask the watchmen מה מלילה, what of the night. Yonasan holds the same, that Dumah is a nation's name, since he left the word untranslated.

כלב.sense: The dog; and כְּלוּב, which he glosses as a basket, and as the wicker cage birds are kept in.

more.t: הֲרֹאשׁ כֶּלֶב אָֽנֹכִי (Shmuel II 3:8), am I a dog's head, and לֹא יֶֽחֱרַץ־ כֶּלֶב לְשֹׁנוֹ (Shemos 11:7), no dog shall sharpen its tongue, both pointed with six dots; וְהַכְּלָבִים עַזֵּי־נֶפֶשׁ (Yeshayahu 56:11), the dogs are greedy of soul. The word he calls well known and glosses no further.
כְּלוּב קָֽיִץ (Amos 8:1) he glosses סל, a basket, and כִּכְלוּב מָלֵא עוֹף (Yirmiyahu 5:27), like a cage full of birds, is like it: a vessel made of rods, lattice work, in which birds are raised.
וְהוּא כָלִבִּֽו [ כָלִבִּֽי ] (Shmuel I 25:3) is a name attached to כָּלֵב, that is, the man was of Kalev's family. Targum Yonasan renders it וְהוּא מִדְבֵית כָּלֵב, he was of the house of Kalev.

כלכל.sense: וַיְכַלְכֵּל יוֹסֵף אֶת־אָבִיו (Bereishis 47:12), Yosef sustained his father; he glosses nothing here, having set the word down under the root כּוּל.

more.t: He brings וַיְכַלְכֵּל יוֹסֵף אֶת־אָבִיו (Bereishis 47:12), Yosef sustained his father, and יְכַלְכֵּל דְּבָרָיו בְּמִשְׁפָּֽט (Tehillim 112:5), he sustains his affairs with judgment, and explains neither: he says he has already set them down with the words like them under the root כּוּל.

כפף.sense: To bend or bow down; and from it כַּף, a thing named for being bent: a branch, the hollow of the hand, the sole of the foot, and a spoon.

more.t: כָּפַף נַפְשִׁי (Tehillim 57:7), he bowed down my soul, where the verb may stand on its own, נפש being spoken of as a masculine word as in כָּל־נֶפֶשׁ שִׁבְעָֽה (Bereishis 46:25), all the souls were seven; or the verb carries an object, and the sense is that each of them bowed down my soul. So too זֹקֵף כְּפוּפִים (Tehillim 146:8), He straightens the bent, and הֲלָכֹף כְּאַגְמֹן רֹאשׁוֹ (Yeshayahu 58:5), to bow his head like a bulrush. אִכַּף לֵֽאלֹהֵי מָרוֹם (Michah 6:6), shall I bow myself before the One on high, stands for אִכָּפֵף.

The noun for a branch is drawn from this: כִּפָּה וְאַגְמוֹן (Yeshayahu 9:13), branch and bulrush, וְכִפָּתוֹ לֹא רַֽעֲנָֽנָה (Iyov 15:32), his branch shall not be green, and כַּפֹּת תְּמָרִים (Vayikra 23:40), branches of palm trees, since the branch is bent. His father reads בְּעוֹדָהּ בְּכַפּוֹ יִבְלָעֶֽנָּה (Yeshayahu 28:4) the same way: while it is still on its branch, whoever sees it swallows it.

more.h: כַּף, the hollow of the hand
more.t: From this the inside of the hand is called כַּף, because it is bent: וַיְמַלֵּא כַפּוֹ מִמֶּנָּה (Vayikra 9:17), he filled his palm from it, עַל לֹא־חָמָס בְּכַפָּי (Iyov 16:17), though no violence is in my palms, וְכַפָּיו פְּרֻשׂוֹת הַשָּׁמָֽיִם (Melachim I 8:54), his palms spread out to heaven, and וְכַף יָשִׂימוּ לְפִיהֶֽם (Iyov 29:9), they laid a hand upon their mouth. וְאַכְפִּי עָלֶיךָ לֹֽא־יִכְבָּֽד (Iyov 33:7), my hand upon you shall not be heavy, is וכפי with an added alef, which he treats under the root אָכַף. The sole of the foot is כַּף as well: מִכַּף רַגְלוֹ (Iyov 2:7), from the sole of his foot, and מִכַּף רַגְלְךָ (Devarim 28:35), from the sole of your foot.

עַל־ כַּפַּיִם כִּסָּה־אוֹר (Iyov 36:32) he reads of clouds, since a cloud is at first like a palm, as it says עָב קְטַנָּה כְּכַף ־אִישׁ (Melachim I 18:44), a little cloud like a man's hand, and because the clouds are like a dome over men. So וְשַׂכֹּתִי כַפִּי (Shemos 33:22), meaning I will screen you with My clouds until I pass by; or it is a palm in its plain sense, said as a figure. נִשָּׂא לְבָבֵנוּ אֶל־כַּפָּיִם (Eichah 3:41) is the clouds too, or it is from כף: we lift our heart together with our palms, on the way of בְּנָשְׂאִי יָדַי אֶל־דְּבִיר קָדְשֶֽׁךָ (Tehillim 28:2), when I lift my hands toward Your holy sanctuary; or we set our heart in our palms and lift it as an offering on high, which is how Rav Saadiah Gaon read it. הֵן עַל־ כַּפַּיִם חַקֹּתִיךְ (Yeshayahu 49:16) he takes as clouds, and so his father writes; it may also be read plainly, as though you were engraved on palms, so that I see you always, and so Ibn Ezra read it.

more.h: The hip socket and the spoon
more.t: עַל־כַּף הַיָּרֵךְ (Bereishis 32:33), the hollow of the thigh, is so called because the bone the thigh bone enters is bent; and some explain that the flesh around the upper thigh bone is shaped like a spoon. The vessel is כַּף as well, כַּף אַחַת עֲשָׂרָה זָהָב (Bamidbar 7:14) and כַּפּוֹת זָהָב (Bamidbar 7:84), the golden spoons, since it too is bent; its name in la'az he gives as קוֹקְיַיארַא.

טלל.sense: To roof over, to set a covering above; and in another sense טַל, dew.

more.t: הוּא יִבְנֶנּוּ וִֽיטַלְלֶנּוּ (Nechemiah 3:15), he shall build it and roof it over: he glosses יסכהו, he shall cover it, that is, he shall set a roof above it. Chachamim say לסוכא מטללתא (Sukkah 28b), of a sukkah that has been roofed; the Targum renders בַּסֻּכֹּת (Vayikra 23:42), in booths, as בִּמְטַלַּיָּא, and בְּצֵל קֹֽרָתִֽי (Bereishis 19:8), in the shadow of my roof beam, as בִּטְלַל שֵׁרוּתִי.

In another sense the word is dew: נִמְלָא־ טָל (Shir HaShirim 5:2), filled with dew, and וְהַשָּׁמַיִם יִתְּנוּ טַלָּם (Zecharyah 8:12), the heavens shall give their dew; so too כִּי טַל אוֹרֹת טַלֶּךָ, for your dew is a dew of lights. The dagesh stands in place of the doubled letter that is missing, and the plural is טַלִים or טְלָלִים, on the pattern of צְלָלִים, shadows.

גלם.sense: To fold over and wrap up; the noun is a wrap a man covers himself in, and in another sense גולם, a thing not yet finished into its form.

more.t: אֶת־אַדַּרְתּוֹ וַיִּגְלֹם (Melachim II 2:8): he folded the mantle over and wound it up, and struck the water with it. So בִּגְלוֹמֵי תְּכֵלֶת וְרִקְמָה (Yechezkel 27:24) is a garment a man covers and wraps himself in, which he names in la'az קפ"א; and Chachamim say גלימא דמיכסא (Bava Metzia 65a), the cloak a man covers himself with. Some explain the word as bundles of garments, טרושל"ש in la'az.

In another sense, גָּלְמִי רָאוּ עֵינֶיךָ (Tehillim 139:16), Your eyes saw my unformed shape: he glosses גופי, my body, since a thing that does not yet have all its forms and is not finished into a vessel is called גולם. So גלמי כלי עץ, גלמי כלי מתכות (Chullin 25a), rough wooden vessels and rough metal vessels, are called so before their work is done. A man empty of wisdom is called גולם too, as in שבעה דברים בגולם ושבעה בחכם (Avos 5:10), seven things are said of a golem and seven of a wise man.

כרך.sense: To wind or wrap around; תַּכְרִיךְ is the cloak a man winds about himself, and in Chazal the shrouds of the dead.

more.t: וְתַכְרִיךְ בּוּץ וְאַרְגָּמָן (Esther 8:15), a wrap of fine linen and purple: a linen cloak, called תכריך because a man winds himself in it and covers himself with it. Chachamim speak of תכריכי המת (Kilayim 9:4), the shrouds of the dead.

They use the root in the plain verb, as אפילו נחש כרוך על עקבו לא יפסיק (Berachos 30b), even if a snake is wound around his heel he does not break off, and כרוכה ומנחת בקרן זויות (Kiddushin 66a), it lies wound up and set in a corner.

גלח.sense: To shave: the head, the beard, the scalp affliction. He says the sense of these is well known and glosses them no further.

more.t: וְגִלְּחָה אֶת־רֹאשָׁהּ (Devarim 21:12), she shall shave her head, וְאֶת־הַנֶּתֶק לֹא יְגַלֵּחַ (Vayikra 13:33), he shall not shave the netek, and יְגַלַּח ... בְּתַעַר הַשְּׂכִירָה (Yeshayahu 7:20), He shall shave with a hired razor. Where no doer is named: כַּאֲשֶׁר גֻּלָּֽח (Shoftim 16:22), after he had been shaved, and אִם־ גֻּלַּחְתִּי וְסָר מִמֶּנִּי כֹחִי (Shoftim 16:17), if I be shaved my strength will leave me. וְהִתְגַּלָּח (Vayikra 13:33) is to shave oneself.

מְגֻלְּחֵי זָקָן וּקְרֻעֵי בְגָדִים (Yirmiyahu 41:5), men shaven of beard and torn of garment, he sets beside כְּאֵלָה נֹבֶלֶת עָלֶהָ (Yeshayahu 1:30), like a terebinth withering of leaf, and says he will explain the turn under the root נבל.

גזז.sense: To shear or cut off: the wool of the flock, the hair of the head, the grass that is mown, and stone cut to shape.

more.t: לִגְזֹז אֶת־צֹאנוֹ (Bereishis 31:19), to shear his flock, וְעַתָּה שָׁמַעְתִּי כִּי גֹֽזְזִים לָךְ (Shmuel I 25:7), now I have heard that they are shearing for you, גָּזִּי נִזְרֵךְ (Yirmiyahu 6:29), cut off your hair, and וַיָּגָז אֶת־רֹאשׁוֹ (Iyov 1:20), he shaved his head. In וְכֵן נָגוֹזּוּ וְעָבָר (Nachum 1:12), so are they cut down and he passes away, he glosses נכרתו, they were cut off.

יֵרֵֽד כְּמָטָר עַל־ גֵּז (Tehillim 72:6), he shall come down like rain upon the mown grass: the grass that has been cut, whose roots are left and which will grow again with the rain. So אַחַר גִּזֵּי הַמֶּֽלֶךְ (Amos 7:1), after the king's mowings.

The wool shorn from the flock carries the same name: גֵּז צֹֽאנְךָ (Devarim 18:4), the shearing of your flock, וַיִּמֶץ טַל מִן־ הַגִּזָּה (Shoftim 6:38), he wrung dew out of the fleece, and אֶת־ גִּזַּת הַצֶּמֶר (Shoftim 6:36), the fleece of wool.

אַבְנֵי גָזִֽית (Melachim I 5:31), stones of hewn work, and לֹֽא־תִבְנֶה אֶתְהֶן גָּזִית (Shemos 20:22), you shall not build them of hewn stone, he glosses אבני כריתה, stones of cutting, that is, stones chiselled to shape. The form should have been גַּזִית with a dagesh, and the resting letter came in place of the dagesh, as the rule is.

גלב.sense: תַּעַר הַגַּלָּבִים (Yechezkel 5:1), the razor of the גלבים, whom he glosses as הסופרים, the men who cut hair.

more.t: תַּעַר הַגַּלָּבִים (Yechezkel 5:1) he glosses הם הסופרים, they are the men who cut hair. In Bereishis Rabbah, parsha 44, היה המלאך עומד ומגלב בידו, the angel stood with a מגלב in his hand. The Targum renders וְכָל־זָקָן גְּרֻעָה (Yirmiyahu 48:37), and every beard shorn, with גליבא, and חַֽרְבוֹת צֻרִים (Yehoshua 5:2), knives of flint, with גלבים דטור, where the same word stands for the blades.

נגף.sense: To strike or thrust. All of these, he says, carry the sense of thrusting and striking, some of them bringing death and some not.

more.t: וְנָגְפוּ אִשָּׁה הָרָה (Shemos 21:22), they strike a pregnant woman, וְכִֽי־ יִגֹּף שׁוֹר־אִישׁ (Shemos 21:35), if a man's ox strike another, נָגֹף וְרָפוֹא (Yeshayahu 19:22), smiting and healing, and לִנְגֹּף אֶת־מִצְרַיִם (Shemos 12:23), to smite Egypt: all of these, he says, take an object. Of אֶת־הַיֶּלֶד אֲשֶׁר יָֽלְדָה אֵֽשֶׁת־אֽוּרִיָּה לְדָוִד וַיֵּֽאָנַֽשׁ (Shmuel II 12:15), the child whom Uriyah's wife bore to David, and he fell sick, he glosses נגפו בחולי קשה, He struck him with a hard illness.

Standing on its own it is to knock against: פֶּן־ תִּגֹּף בָּאֶבן רַגְלֶֽךָ (Tehillim 91:12), lest you strike your foot against a stone, and וְרַגְלְךָ לֹא תִגּֽוֹף (Mishlei 3:23), your foot shall not stumble. So וּבְטֶרֶם יִתְנַגְּפוּ רַגְלֵיכֶם עַל־הָרֵי נָשֶׁף (Yirmiyahu 13:16), before your feet stumble on the mountains of dusk.

כִּי נִגַּף לִפְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל (Shmuel II 10:15), that they were beaten before Israel, he marks with a patach and reads as past. אַךְ נִגּוֹף נִגָּף הוּא (Shoftim 20:39), surely he is smitten, and the like of it at Devarim 28:25, he marks with a kamatz and reads as present. בְּֽהִנָּגֵף עַמְּךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל (Melachim I 8:33), when Your people Israel are beaten.

The noun stands in וְלֹא־יִֽהְיֶה בָכֶם נֶגֶף (Shemos 12:13), there shall be no plague among you, pointed with six dots; and on another pattern אַֽחֲרֵי הַמַּגֵּפָה (Bamidbar 26:1), after the plague, and אֶת־כָּל־ מַגֵּֽפֹתַי (Shemos 9:14), all My plagues.

צפרדע.sense: The frog. He says the word is well known, and that the singular הַצְּפַרְדֵּעַ may name the whole kind rather than one of them.

more.h: The singular for the whole kind
more.t: וַתַּעַל הַצְּפַרְדֵּעַ (Shemos 8:2), the frog came up, he calls well known; and it may be that הַצְּפַרְדֵּעַ there is the name of the whole kind and is not said of a single one, as also וַתְּהִי הַכִּנָּם, and the lice came. So וּצְפַרְדֵּעַ וַתַּשְׁחִיתֵֽם (Tehillim 78:45), and the frog, and it destroyed them, stands in the singular. The plural stands in וַיַּֽעֲלוּ אֶת־ הַֽצְפַרְדְּעִים, they brought up the frogs, and וְשָׁרַץ הַיְאֹר צְפַרְדְּעִים, the river shall swarm with frogs.

שׁחן.sense: שְׁחִין, the boil: an affliction, he says, that comes of heat other than fire.

more.t: שְׁחִין אֲבַעְבֻּעֹת (Shemos 9:10), a boil of blisters, and לִשְׁחִין פֹּרֵחַ (Shemos 9:9), a boil breaking out: he says it is an affliction that comes of heat other than fire. So Chachamim ask איזהו שחין, what is a shechin, and answer לקה בעץ או באבן או בזפת או במי טבריא (Negaim 9:1), one struck by wood or by stone or by pitch or by the waters of Teveriah; and they say there כל שאינו מחמת האש זהו שחין, whatever is not from fire is a shechin, הבא מחמת האש זה מכוה, and what comes of fire is a burn.

The Targum renders וַיִּקַּח מֵהֶם וַיָּחָם (Yeshayahu 44:15), he takes of them and warms himself, with וּנְסֵיב מִנְהוֹן וּשְׁחֵין; and the Kohen Gadol's tefillah (Yoma 53b) runs יהי רצון שתהא שנה זו שחונה וגשומה, may it be His will that this year be warm and rainy.

גרב.sense: וּבַגָּרָב וּבֶחָרֶס (Devarim 28:27), with the garav and with the cheres: he glosses גרב as one of the diseases of itching.

ילף.sense: יַלֶּפֶת, the affliction named at Vayikra 22:22; the Chachamim take it for the Egyptian lichen, which winds itself about a man until the day he dies.

more.t: One line, and no gloss of his own. The word stands at Vayikra 22:22, and what he gives in place of a gloss is the Chachamim's in Bechoros 41a: this is the Egyptian lichen, שמלפפתו עד יום המיתה, which winds itself about a man until the day of death. The edition prints a gap in the middle of their words.

חפשֹ.sense: To search, to look through; the noun חֵפֶשׂ, a search. In the reflexive it is to change one's clothing and go about disguised.

more.t: חֹפֵשׂ כָּל־חַדְרֵי־בָטֶן (Mishlei 20:27), searching all the chambers of the belly, and וְכַמַּטְמוֹנִים תַּחְפְּשֶׂנָּה (Mishlei 2:4), and you search her out as men search for hidden treasure. וַיְחַפֵּשׂ בַּגָּדוֹל הֵחֵל (Bereishis 44:12), he searched, beginning with the eldest, and וְחִפַּשְׂתִּי אֹתוֹ בְּכֹל אַלְפֵי יְהוּדָה (Shmuel I 23:23), and I will search him out among all the thousands of Yehudah. On עִם־לְבָבִי אָשִׂיחָה וַיְחַפֵּשׂ רוּחִי (Tehillim 77:7) he says: if I speak with my heart, he searches my spirit and knows what I think.

The passive is אֵיךְ נֶחְפְּשׂוּ עֵשָׂו, how Esav has been searched out, which he cites from Ovadiah without a chapter, and וּבְקוּם רְשָׁעִים יְחֻפַּשׂ אָדָם (Mishlei 28:12), when the wicked rise, a man is searched out. תַּמְנוּ חֵפֶשׂ מְחֻפָּשׂ (Tehillim 64:7), we have finished a search well searched, carries the noun, and the sense of it is inquiry.

The reflexive is of exchanging the veil or the garment for another: וַיִּתְחַפֵּשׂ בָּאֲפֵר (Melachim I 20:38), he disguised himself with a covering, וַיִּתְחַפֵּשׂ מֶלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל (Melachim I 22:30), the king of Yisrael disguised himself, and וַיִּתְחַפֵּשׂ שָׁאוּל וַיִּלְבַּשׁ בְּגָדִים אֲחֵרִים (Shmuel II 28:8 in his edition), Shaul disguised himself and put on other clothes. בְּרָב־כֹּחַ יִתְחַפֵּשׂ לְבוּשִׁי (Iyov 30:18), by great force my garment is changed about me.

more.h: The two kings going to battle
more.t: On הִתְחַפֵּשׂ וָבֹא בַמִּלְחָמָה (Melachim I 22:30) he reads הִתְחַפֵּשׂ as an infinitive: the king of Yisrael says of himself that he will disguise himself and come into the battle, as though he said, I will disguise myself and go into the war, and you wear your own garments, since you have no need to disguise. His father reads it as a command: the king of Yisrael told Yehoshafat to take off his royal clothes and enter the battle, meaning that both of them should go disguised. Yehoshafat answered, and you wear your garments, if I am to disguise, since one of the two of us should enter in the honour of kingship. The king of Yisrael did not accept it and disguised himself; Yehoshafat, seeing that, kept his royal clothes on, and it was for this that the officers of the chariots took him for the king of Yisrael, until he cried out and they knew his voice.

חפשׁ.sense: Free; חָפְשִׁי is a man free of his master, and the nouns are חֹפֶשׁ, freedom, and חֻפְשָׁה, release.

more.t: וְעֶבֶד חָפְשִׁי מֵאֲדֹנָיו (Iyov 3:19), and the slave is free of his master, and הָעִבְרִי וְהָעִבְרִיָּה חָפְשִׁים (Yirmiyahu 34:9), the Hebrew man and the Hebrew woman going free. בַּמֵּתִים חָפְשִׁי (Tehillim 88:6), free among the dead, he reads as free of the toil of this world, as the pasuk says, ושם ינוחו יגיעי כח, and there the weary of strength are at rest.

יֵצֵא לַחָפְשִׁי (Shemos 21:2), he goes out to freedom, he explains as going out to a place where he will be free, that is, out of his master's house to his own house. Some say the yud is added and the word stands for לחופש, and others that the lamed is added.

כִּי־לֹא חֻפָּשָׁה (Vayikra 19:20), because she was not set free, and the noun אוֹ חֻפְשָׁה לֹא נִתַּן־לָהּ (Vayikra 19:20), or freedom was not given her, on the pattern of טֻמְאָה, uncleanness. The heh may be the feminine ending, soft though it is written, and he says he has set out many like it in his grammar; or חֻפְשָׁה may be built from חֹפֶשׁ the way מְלֹא קֻמְצוֹ (Vayikra 5:12), the full of his fist, is built from קֹמֶץ, and כְּרֹב גֻּדְּלוֹ (Tehillim 150:2), according to his abundant greatness, from גֹּדֶל.

more.h: Clothes of freedom, house of freedom
more.t: בְבִגְדֵי־חֹפֶשׁ לְרִכְבָּה (Yechezkel 27:20), garments of freedom for riding, are costly clothes, the kind fit for a free man and a nobleman. בְּבֵית הַחָפְשִׁית (Melachim II 15:5), in the house of freedom, is so called because he kept apart there from people, as though free of their company. Rabbi Yonah reads it otherwise, a small house, from the Arabic, where a small house is called חפשי. The Yerushalmi in Kesubos says he made him a house in the graveyard, as you say בַּמֵּתִים חָפְשִׁי, free among the dead.

דרר.sense: דְּרוֹר, freedom; and the name of the bird that nests in men's houses without fear, as though free of them.

more.t: וּקְרָאתֶם דְּרוֹר (Vayikra 25:10), and you shall proclaim דרור: the word is freedom, and that one word is the whole of his gloss on it.
מָר־דְּרוֹר (Shemos 30:23) is the fine myrrh, the myrrh that is free of counterfeit and of anything mixed into it.

וּדְרוֹר קֵן לָהּ (Tehillim 84:4), the deror has a nest of her own, and כַּדְּרוֹר לָעוּף (Mishlei 26:2), like the deror in its flying. It is one of the unclean birds, the one called hirondelle in the vernacular, and it carries the name because it nests in houses without fear, as though free of men and safe from being caught.

חור.sense: White, and to turn white; in another sense a hole bored through; and חֹרִים, the nobles, which Rabbi Yonah also draws from whiteness.

more.t: חוּר כַּרְפַּס וּתְכֵלֶת (Esther 1:6) is white, and so תְּכֵלֶת וָחוּר (Esther 8:15), blue and white; the Chachamim (Megillah 12a) say a couch of white wool was spread for them. The verb shows its middle letter in וְלֹא עַתָּה פָּנָיו יֶחֱוָרוּ (Yeshayahu 29:22), his face shall not now turn white, and the Targum renders לָבָן (Bereishis 30:35), white, as חִוָּר.
He puts shame under this whiteness, since a man who feels shame goes white in the face; and so the Chachamim (Bava Metzia 58b) speak of one who whitens his fellow's face in public.

Rabbi Yonah reads וְאֹרְגִים חוֹרָי (Yeshayahu 19:9) from whiteness, as white cloth, and סַלֵּי חֹרִי (Bereishis 40:16) likewise, baskets of peeled rods, which are white once the bark is off. That reading he holds to be a far one.

From whiteness too Rabbi Yonah takes בֶּן־חוֹרִים (Koheles 10:17), son of nobles, כָּל־חֹרֵי יְהוּדָה וִירוּשָׁלָם (Yirmiyahu 27:20), all the nobles of Yehudah and Yerushalayim, וָאָרִיבָה אֶת־הַחֹרִים (Nechemiah 5:7), and I contended with the nobles, and חֹרֶיהָ וְאֵין־שָׁם מְלוּכָה (Yeshayahu 34:12), her nobles, and no kingship there. In the language of Yishmael, he says, the princes and the great men are called by a word for whiteness.

The other sense is a hole: וַיִּקֹּב חֹר בְּדַלְתּוֹ (Melachim II 12:10), he bored a hole in its door, וַיְמַלֵּא־טֶרֶף חֹרָיו (Nachum 2:13), he filled his holes with prey, חֹרֵי עָפָר וְכֵפִים (Iyov 30:6), holes of the dust and of the rocks, and מִן־הַחֹרִים אֲשֶׁר הִתְחַבְּאוּ־שָׁם (Shmuel I 14:11), out of the holes where they had hidden. With a shuruk it is עַל־חֻר פָּתֶן (Yeshayahu 11:8), over the hole of an asp, and again at Yeshayahu 42:22, which he says needs no explaining.

more.h: The woven work read as holes
more.t: The same two words he can take from the hole instead: וְאֹרְגִים חוֹרָי (Yeshayahu 19:9) would be cloth pierced with holes at the weaving, for ornament, or else the nets, which are holes upon holes, and the pasuk beside it is of spreading, וּפֹרְשֵׂי מִכְמֹרֶת עַל־פְּנֵי־מַיִם (Yeshayahu 19:8), they that spread nets upon the water. סַלֵּי חֹרִי (Bereishis 40:16) are then pierced baskets, for that is how they are made. He says he takes it further under the root חרר.

more.h: Words he keeps out of the root
more.t: Rabbi Yehudah and Rabbi Yonah put into this root וְחָרָה נְחֻשְׁתָּהּ (Yechezkel 24:11), her copper burning hot, וְעַצְמִי־חָרָה מִנִּי־חֹרֶב (Iyov 30:30), my bone burnt with heat, and חָרוּ יֹשְׁבֵי אֶרֶץ (Yeshayahu 24:6), the dwellers of the earth scorched. He holds the right and straight place for them is among the doubled verbs.

בצר.sense: To gather grapes, to pluck; in another sense to make strong, of a fortified city; and to be withheld, as in a year of drought. בָּצֶר is gold.

more.t: לֹא תִבְצֹר (Vayikra 25:5), you shall not gather, כִּי תִבְצֹר כַּרְמְךָ (Devarim 24:21), when you gather your vineyard, and כְּבוֹצֵר עַל־סַלְסִלּוֹת (Yirmiyahu 6:9), like a gatherer over the baskets. The noun is בָּצִיר, the vintage: וְהִשִּׂיג לָכֶם דַּיִשׁ אֶת־בָּצִיר (Vayikra 26:5), your threshing shall reach the vintage, and מִבְצִיר אֲבִיעֶזֶר (Shoftim 8:2), than the vintage of Aviezer, where the beis is soft though it ought to carry a dagesh. All of them are plucking.

כִּי יָרַד יַעַר הַבָּצוּר (Zechariah 11:2), the edition correcting the word to הַבָּצִיר, for the forest has come down. He can take it from the gathering, as a figure for the great men of Yisrael: he likens them to a forest because forest trees are tall and many, and joins them to the vintage because these give fruit, which forest trees do not. Later in the entry he says it can as well be taken from the strength.

וְהֶעָרִים בְּצֻרוֹת (Bamidbar 13:28), and the cities are fortified, לְחוֹמַת נְחֹשֶׁת בְּצוּרָה (Yirmiyahu 15:20), a fortified wall of copper, and וְאַגִּידָה לְּךָ גְּדֹלוֹת וּבְצֻרוֹת לֹא יְדַעְתָּם (Yirmiyahu 33:3), and I will tell you great things and fortified things you have not known. The verb makes strong: וַתִּתְצוּ הַבָּתִּים לְבַצֵּר הַחוֹמָה (Yeshayahu 22:10), you pulled the houses down to fortify the wall, and וְכִי תְבַצֵּר מְרוֹם עֻזָּהּ (Yirmiyahu 51:53), though she fortify the height of her strength. The nouns are שׁוּבוּ לְבִצָּרוֹן (Zechariah 9:12), return to the stronghold, which he reads as the cities of strength, עָרֵי הַמִּבְצָר (Yehoshua 10:20), the fortified cities, הַבְּמַחֲנִים אִם בְּמִבְצָרִים (Bamidbar 13:19), whether in open camps or in strongholds, and עִיר מִבְצָרוֹת (Daniel 11:15), a city of strongholds. All of them are strength.

יִבְצֹר רוּחַ נְגִידִים (Tehillim 76:13) he reads from the strength: He will raise it up and make it strong. It can also be read from the plucking: He will pluck and bring the spirit of princes low from its pride, which fits what comes after it, נוֹרָא לְמַלְכֵי־אָרֶץ, feared by the kings of the earth.

וְעַתָּה לֹא־יִבָּצֵר מֵהֶם (Bereishis 11:6), now nothing will be withheld from them, and וְלֹא־יִבָּצֵר מִמְּךָ מְזִמָּה (Iyov 42:2), no purpose is withheld from You: their sense is not being kept back. From the same, וּבִשְׁנַת בַּצֹּרֶת לֹא יִדְאָג (Yirmiyahu 17:8), in a year of drought he will not worry, and עַל־דִּבְרֵי הַבַּצָּרוֹת (Yirmiyahu 14:1), concerning the droughts, which is the withholding of the rains and their being held back. Some read לְעִתּוֹת בַּצָּרָה (Tehillim 9:10), in times of trouble, from this too, taking the beis as a root letter. He says the fortified city and this sense lie close together, since a thing great and strong is withheld from a man's reaching it.

וְשִׁית־עַל־עָפָר בָּצֶר (Iyov 22:24), and lay gold upon the dust, and the plural בצרים in וְהָיָה שַׁדַּי בְּצָרֶיךָ (Iyov 22:25), and the Almighty will be your gold. There are careful books with no yud, and then it is singular, the resh taking a segol for the esnachta; and it may still be plural even with the yud missing, since many like it are found.

זהב.sense: Gold; and because gold is clear and clean, a thing that is clear and clean is called זָהָב too.

more.t: זָהָב וָכֶסֶף (Shemos 25:3), gold and silver. The word itself he calls known and leaves without a gloss.

מִצָּפוֹן זָהָב יֶאֱתֶה (Iyov 37:22), gold comes out of the north, he takes of the clear clean wind. Ibn Ezra reads it of the brightness of the sky, which looks like gold, since it is from the northern side that it begins to clear. כּוֹס־זָהָב בָּבֶל (Yirmiyahu 51:7), Bavel a golden cup, is the clear clean wine, and הַמְרִיקִים מֵעֲלֵיהֶם הַזָּהָב (Zechariah 4:12), that empty the gold out of themselves, is the clear clean oil.

כתם.sense: כֶּתֶם, the fine gold; Rabbi Yonah takes it for pearls, but its being tied to Ophir and to פָּז tells for gold.

more.t: בְּכֶתֶם אוֹפִיר (Tehillim 45:10), in the fine gold of Ophir, וְלַכֶּתֶם אָמַרְתִּי מִבְטַחִי (Iyov 31:24), and I said to the fine gold, you are my trust, יִשְׁנֶא הַכֶּתֶם הַטּוֹב (Eichah 4:1), how the good gold is changed, and וַחֲלִי־כָתֶם (Mishlei 25:12), an ornament of fine gold: it is the good gold. Rabbi Yonah wrote that these are pearls, but from the word being tied to Ophir and to פָּז it looks like gold and not pearls.

כֶּתֶם פָּז (Shir HaShirim 5:11) he reads as כתם and פז with the vav dropped, as in שֶׁמֶשׁ יָרֵחַ (Chavakuk 3:11), sun and moon; or else as a construct, the כתם of the פז, attached to it for its worth, as in זָהָב מוּפָז (Melachim I 10:18), refined gold.

מִכְתָּם לְדָוִד (Tehillim 16:1) he takes from this, the mizmor being upon David like a כתם. נִכְתָּם עֲוֹנֵךְ (Yirmiyahu 2:22) is like נרשם, your sin is marked in, and the Chachamim use כתם for the marking of a thing.

חמץ.sense: To become leavened, of dough; the noun חֹמֶץ, vinegar; in another sense to oppress; and חֲמוּץ בְּגָדִים is red of garment.

more.t: כִּי לֹא חָמֵץ (Shemos 12:39), because it was not leavened, טֶרֶם יֶחְמָץ (Shemos 12:34), before it was leavened, and מִלּוּשׁ בָּצֵק עַד־חֻמְצָתוֹ (Hoshea 6:4 in his edition), from the kneading of the dough until it is leavened, which he marks as an infinitive on the pattern of לְחֻמְלָה עָלָיִךְ (Yechezkel 16:5), to have pity on you. חָמֵץ תֵּאָפֶינָה (Vayikra 23:17), they shall be baked leavened, is the adjective, and כָּל־מַחְמֶצֶת (Shemos 12:20), anything leavened, the noun, which he says may also be a word for the kneading trough. חֹמֶץ יַיִן וְחֹמֶץ שֵׁכָר (Bamidbar 6:3), vinegar of wine and vinegar of strong drink, belongs with them, since dough left to leaven too long tastes of vinegar.

more.h: The judge who leavens his ruling
more.t: The Chachamim take אַשְּׁרוּ חָמוֹץ (Yeshayahu 1:17) from here, of the judge who lets his ruling leaven, not judging at once but after much looking into it; and so they said in Sanhedrin 35a, fortunate is the judge who leavens his judgment.
כִּי יִתְחַמֵּץ לְבָבִי (Tehillim 73:21), when my heart was soured, he calls a borrowed use of the word, and it is anger.

בְּלִיל חָמִיץ יֹאכֵלוּ (Yeshayahu 30:24), the provender they eat: Rabbi Yonah explains חמיץ as clean and good, and likens it to the Arabic, where clean good fodder for a beast is called חמצ"ה with a dot on the tzadi. Targum Yonasan has בְּלִיל מְפַטֵּם, fattening provender.

אַשְּׁרוּ חָמוֹץ (Yeshayahu 1:17) he himself takes as a word for the man who is robbed, set the oppressed right, and מִכַּף מְעַוֵּל וְחוֹמֵץ (Tehillim 71:4), from the hand of the wrongdoer and the oppressor, is the man who robs; the word is חוֹמֵס with a samech, as הַשְּׁבִיסִים (Yeshayahu 3:18) with a samech goes with ושבצת with a tzadi. וְקַטֵּר מֵחָמֵץ תּוֹדָה (Amos 4:5) can be read from this, and Targum Yonasan has וּמַגְבַן מִן אוֹנֶס תּוֹדָתָא, an offering of thanks out of what was seized; on וְרֹעֶה זוֹלְלִים יַכְלִים אָבִיו (Mishlei 28:7), he who keeps company with gluttons shames his father, he has וּדְמִתְחַבֵּר לִזְלִילֵי מַחֲמֵץ אֲבוּי, whoever joins himself to gluttons does his father violence.
חֲמוּץ בְּגָדִים (Yeshayahu 63:1) is red, and he says so from the sense of the pasuk.

גנב.sense: To steal; and with the heart as its object, to steal a man's knowledge of what is being done to him.

more.t: לָמָּה גָנַבְתָּ אֶת־אֱלֹהָי (Bereishis 31:30), why did you steal my gods, is plain theft. וַיִּגְנֹב יַעֲקֹב אֶת־לֵב לָבָן הָאֲרַמִּי (Bereishis 31:20), and Yaakov stole the heart of Lavan the Arami, he reads as stealing his knowledge: Lavan thought he was still with his flock, and he had fled. וַתִּגְנֹב אֹתִי (Bereishis 31:27), and you stole me, is as though he had said, my knowledge; or אותי stands in place of מן, you stole your knowledge away from me, and so the Targum has וְכַסֵּיתָא מִנִּי, you hid it from me.

more.h: Stolen by day and by night
more.t: גְּנֻבְתִי יוֹם וּגְנֻבְתִי לָיְלָה (Bereishis 31:39), what was stolen by day and what was stolen by night. The yud in both is added, and the proper form is גְּנוּבַת יום וּגְנוּבַת לילה.

וְאִם־גָּנֹב יִגָּנֵב (Shemos 22:11), and if it be stolen, מְגַנְּבֵי דְבָרַי (Yirmiyahu 23:30), who steal My words, וַיְגַנֵּב אַבְשָׁלוֹם אֶת־לֵב אַנְשֵׁי יִשְׂרָאֵל (Shmuel II 15:6), and Avshalom stole the heart of the men of Yisrael, כִּי־גֻנֹּב גֻּנַּבְתִּי (Bereishis 40:15), for I was surely stolen away, וְאֵלַי דָּבָר יְגֻנָּב (Iyov 4:12), and a word was stolen to me, וְגֻנַּב מִבֵּית הָאִישׁ (Shemos 22:6), and it is stolen out of the man's house, and וַיִּתְגַּנֵּב הָעָם בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא (Shmuel II 19:4), and the people stole away that day.

The noun is גְּנֵבָה: אִם־הִמָּצֵא תִמָּצֵא בְיָדוֹ הַגְּנֵבָה (Shemos 22:3), if the theft is found in his hand, and וְנִמְכַּר בִּגְנֵבָתוֹ (Shemos 22:2), he is sold for his theft. The man is הַגַּנָּב: אִם־בַּמַּחְתֶּרֶת יִמָּצֵא הַגַּנָּב (Shemos 22:1), if the thief is found breaking in, גַּנָּבִים בָּאוּ לְךָ, thieves coming upon you, which he cites from Ovadiah without a chapter, and כְּבֹשֶׁת גַּנָּב כִּי יִמָּצֵא (Yirmiyahu 2:26), like the shame of a thief when he is found, on which Targum Yonasan has כְּבַהֲתַת גְבַר דְמִתְחַשֵׁיב מְהֵימָן וּמִשְׁתְּכַח גְנִיב, like the shame of a man held trustworthy who is found to be a thief.

חמס.sense: To take by force, and in particular to tear a thing from its place or strip off what covered it.

more.h: Taking a thing from its place
more.t: חָמְסוּ תוֹרָתִי (Yechezkel 22:26), they did violence to My Torah: since they do not keep it, it is as though they robbed it and moved it from its place. Rabbi Yonah wrote that חמס in Arabic is the removing of a thing from its place.

וּמְזִמּוֹת עָלַי תַּחְמֹסוּ (Iyov 21:27), the schemes you devise against me, he reads either as your thinking that the violence is with me, or as your schemes against me being themselves violence and sin. וְחֹטְאִי חֹמֵס נַפְשׁוֹ (Mishlei 8:36), and he who sins against me does violence to his own soul.

וַיַּחְמֹס כַּגַּן שֻׂכּוֹ (Eichah 2:6), and He tore away His booth as a garden. The right reading, he says, is כסכת גן, like a garden's booth: as a garden's booth is easily pulled down and taken away, so He did with His booth, which is Tzion.

יַחְמֹס כַּגֶּפֶן בִּסְרוֹ (Iyov 15:33), he will strip off his unripe grapes like a vine, is to take away and lay bare, and נֶחְמְסוּ עֲקֵבָיִךְ (Yirmiyahu 13:22), your heels were laid bare: they were uncovered and the covering upon them taken off.
וְאֶת־הַתַּחְמָס (Devarim 14:16) is one of the unclean birds, named so because it takes other birds by force and robs them; the Targum Yerushalmi has חטופיתא.

נהג.sense: To drive a flock or a beast along, to lead; and of a man, to conduct himself in a way.

more.t: אוֹתִי נָהַג וַיֹּלַךְ (Eichah 3:2), He drove me and made me walk, נֹהֵג כַּצֹּאן יוֹסֵף (Tehillim 80:2), who leads Yosef like a flock, וַיִּנְהַג אֶת־כָּל־מִקְנֵהוּ (Bereishis 31:18), and he drove all his cattle, and נְהַג וָלֵךְ (Melachim II 4:24), drive and go. So וְעֻזָּא וְאַחְיוֹ נֹהֲגִים בָּעֲגָלָה (Divrei HaYamim I 13:7), Uzza and Achyo driving the wagon, and וּמַלְכֵיהֶם נְהוּגִים (Yeshayahu 60:11), their kings led along.
וְלִבִּי נֹהֵג בַּחָכְמָה (Koheles 2:3), and my heart leading with wisdom, he reads as conducting himself with wisdom.

more.h: Driving hard, and the manner of it
more.t: כִּי בְשִׁגָּעוֹן יִנְהָג (Melachim II 9:20), for he drives with madness, means that he drives his camp so; and the noun is כְּמִנְהַג יֵהוּא בֶן־נִמְשִׁי (Melachim II 9:20), like the driving of Yehu son of Nimshi.

נָהֲגוּ לִפְנֵי הַמִּקְנֶה הַהוּא (Shmuel I 30:20), they drove on before that cattle. נהגו is said of the flock and the cattle just named: as David took everything, so they drove everything off and left nothing, having no fear; and some of them went ahead of the cattle saying, this is David's spoil.

נִהַג רוּחַ־קָדִים (Shemos 10:13), He drove an east wind, וַתְּנַהֵג אֶת־בְּנֹתַי (Bereishis 31:26), and you drove my daughters off, and מְנַהֲגוֹת כְּקוֹל יוֹנִים (Nachum 2:8), leading her with a sound like doves: he reads מנהגות as leading her, their voice being like the voice of doves. All of these take an object.

נחה.sense: To lead, to guide along a road. The entry is a list of the pesukim that use it, all of them in the sense of conducting and leading.

more.t: נָחִיתָ כַצֹּאן עַמֶּךָ (Tehillim 77:21), You led Your people like a flock, מִי נָחַנִי עַד־אֱדוֹם (Tehillim 60:11), who has led me to Edom, לֵךְ נְחֵה אֶת־הָעָם (Shemos 32:34), go, lead the people, and וּנְחֵנִי בְּאֹרַח מִישׁוֹר (Tehillim 27:11), lead me in a level path. He brings Yeshayahu 58:11 with them, that Hashem will lead you always.

תַּנְחֶה אֹתָךְ (Mishlei 6:22), it will lead you, לַנְחֹתָם הַדֶּרֶךְ (Shemos 13:21), to lead them the way, יַנְחֵנִי בְמַעְגְּלֵי־צֶדֶק (Tehillim 23:3), He leads me in paths of righteousness, וְלִפְנֵי גְדֹלִים יַנְחֶנּוּ (Mishlei 18:16), and it leads him before great men, וּבִתְבוּנוֹת כַּפָּיו יַנְחֵם (Tehillim 78:72), and with the skill of his hands he led them, וַיַּנְחֵם בַּחְלַח וּבְחָבוֹר (Melachim II 18:11), and he led them to Chalach and Chavor, שֹׁטֵחַ לַגּוֹיִם וַיַּנְחֵם (Iyov 12:23), He spreads the nations out and leads them, וְעַיִשׁ עַל־בָּנֶיהָ תַנְחֵם (Iyov 38:32), and Ayish with her sons, will you lead them, and וַיַּנְחֵם אֶת־פְּנֵי מֶלֶךְ מוֹאָב (Shmuel I 22:4), and he led them before the king of Moav. All of them are conducting and leading.
וַיָּכִינוּ אֶת־הַמִּנְחָה (Bereishis 43:25), and they made the gift ready, he does not treat here: he says he has explained that word under the root מָנַח.

נהל.sense: To lead along and bring on gently, a sense he groups with driving a flock; and to sustain, as Yosef sustained them with bread.

more.t: נֵהַלְתָּ בְעָזְּךָ (Shemos 15:13), You led them on in Your strength, וְעַל־מַבּוּעֵי מַיִם יְנַהֲלֵם (Yeshayahu 49:10), He will lead them by springs of water, and אֵין־מְנַהֵל לָהּ (Yeshayahu 51:18), she has none to lead her. אֶתְנַהֲלָה לְאִטִּי (Bereishis 33:14), let me go on at my own slow pace, is the reflexive. He says all of them carry the sense of driving a flock along.

וַיְנַהֲלֵם בַּלֶּחֶם (Bereishis 47:17), and he sustained them with bread, and וַיְנַהֲלֵם מִסָּבִיב (Divrei HaYamim II 32:22), and He led them about, which he reads as leading them in His kindness, so that they had no fear of any around them.

וּבְכֹל הַנַּהֲלֹלִים (Yeshayahu 7:19) he takes as a kind of low and poor tree. His father takes it from the root הָלַל with an added nun, and Targum Yonasan has וּבְכֹל בָּתֵּי תוּשְׁבְּחָתָא, and in all the houses of praise.

מזג.sense: מָזֶג, the mixture in the cup, wine with water mixed into it.

more.t: Two lines. אַל־יֶחְסַר הַמָּזֶג (Shir HaShirim 7:3), let the mixture not be wanting; and the word, he says, is familiar from the Chachamim, who speak of יין מזוג (Negaim 1:2), mixed wine, explained as wine they mix water into.

דמע.sense: To shed tears; דִּמְעָה, a tear; and דֶּמַע, the oil or the wine running down from the press, drop by drop.

more.t: וְדָמֹעַ תִּדְמַע וְתֵרַד עֵינִי דִּמְעָה (Yirmiyahu 13:17), my eye shall surely weep and run down with tears, וְדִמְעָתָהּ עַל לֶחֱיָהּ (Eichah 1:2), her tear upon her cheek, וְלוֹא תָבוֹא דִּמְעָתֶךָ (Yechezkel 24:16), and your tears shall not come, and in the plural כָּלוּ בַדְּמָעוֹת עֵינַי (Eichah 2:11), my eyes are spent with tears.
מְלֵאָתְךָ וְדִמְעֲךָ (Shemos 22:28), your fullness and your flow, is a word for the oil or the wine that comes down from the press, falling like a tear, drop by drop.

ערם.sense: Three senses under one set of letters: to be shrewd, to be naked, and a heap of piled grain.

more.t: עָרֹם יַעְרִם הוּא (Shmuel I 23:22), he is very crafty; וּפֶתִי יַעְרִם (Mishlei 19:25), the simple one will grow shrewd; עַל־עַמְּךָ יַעֲרִימוּ סוֹד (Tehillim 83:4), against Your people they plot in secret. The adjective is עָרוּם, as of the snake, וְהַנָּחָשׁ הָיָה עָרוּם (Bereishis 3:1), the snake was cunning. The noun is עָרְמָה, as at Yehoshua 9:4, where the Givonim acted בְּעָרְמָה, with guile. In לֹכֵד חֲכָמִים בְּעָרְמָם (Iyov 5:13), He catches the wise in their cunning, the right sense of the form is בערמתם, in their cunning, as כִּתְבוּנָם עֲצַבִּים (Hoshea 13:2) stands for בתבונתם, by their own understanding. The matter is stratagem and guile.

A second sense is the bare body: וְאַתְּ עֵרֹם וְעֶרְיָה (Yechezkel 16:7), and you were naked and bare, where masculine and feminine stand together because Scripture speaks of Knesses Yisrael in both. It is written with a yud after the ayin in כִּי־עֵירֹם אָנֹכִי (Bereishis 3:10), for I am naked, and כִּי עֵירֻמִּם הֵם (Bereishis 3:7), that they were naked. Another pattern is עָרוֹם וְיָחֵף (Yeshayahu 20:2), naked and barefoot, and the plural takes a dagesh, וַיִּהְיוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם עֲרוּמִּים (Bereishis 2:25), the two of them were naked. The Mesorah marks the shrewd ones soft and the naked ones hard, which is what keeps the two apart in the reading. The noun stands also in וּבְעֵירֹם וּבְחֹסֶר כֹּל (Devarim 28:48), in nakedness and in want of everything.

A third sense is grain piled up: בִּקְצֵה הָעֲרֵמָה (Rus 3:7), at the end of the heap, and עֲרֵמַת חִטִּים (Shir HaShirim 7:3), a heap of wheat. The plural runs both ways, עֲרֵמוֹת עֲרֵמוֹת (Divrei HaYamim II 31:6), heap upon heap, and סָלּוּהָ כְמוֹ־עֲרֵמִים (Yirmiyahu 50:26), pile her up like heaps. From it נֶעֶרְמוּ מַיִם (Shemos 15:8), the waters were heaped up, which he glosses as standing in heaps, as the pasuk goes on, נִצְּבוּ כְמוֹ־נֵד, they stood like a wall. Borrowed usage gives מֵעֲרֵמוֹת הֶעָפָר (Nechemiah 3:34), out of the heaps of dust.

The same letters give עַרְמוֹן, a tree: לַח וְלוּז וְעַרְמוֹן (Bereishis 30:37), fresh poplar and almond and plane, and וְעַרְמֹנִים לֹא־הָיוּ כְּפֹארֹתָיו (Yechezkel 31:8), the plane trees were not like its boughs. Chazal call it דופלי, and the Targum renders it וְדִדְלוּף. Some say it is the tree named in the vernacular קשטני"ר.

גדשׁ.sense: גָּדִישׁ, the crop heaped up in the threshing floor once it has been cut.

more.t: מִגָּדִישׁ וְעַד־קָמָה (Shoftim 15:5), from the stack to the standing grain, and וְנֶאֱכַל גָּדִישׁ (Shemos 22:5), and a stack was consumed. Grain that has been reaped and piled in the threshing floor is called גדיש.

From it Chazal use the word for a measure filled above its edge: כל חמדות שהיו במקדש היו נגדשות, every measure in the Mikdash was heaped up, and אין מוחקין במקום שגודשין, one does not level off a measure in a place where the custom is to heap it.

וְעַל־גָּדִישׁ יִשְׁקוֹד (Iyov 21:32) he glosses as hurrying to be gathered to the graves: as a stack is gathered in its season once the crop has ripened, so a man is gathered in his time. Rabbeinu Hai explained גָּדִישׁ as the domed mound built over a grave, after the custom of the land of Yishmael, and he approves that reading, since the pasuk just above says והוא לקברות יובל, and he is carried to the graves, and the dome is shaped like a stack.

עמר.sense: To use a man as merchandise; and, in a second sense, the עֹמֶר, both a measure and a sheaf of cut grain.

more.t: וְהִתְעַמֶּר־בּוֹ וּמְכָרוֹ (Devarim 24:7), and he deals with him as goods and sells him, and לֹא־תִתְעַמֵּר בָּהּ (Devarim 21:14), of the captive woman. The matter is trading in a person, as Chazal taught that one who steals a Jew is not liable until he brings him into his house and uses him and sells him. On the captive woman he gives לא תשתמש ותשתעבד בה, you shall not use her and make her serve you, once you have taken her.
עֹמֶר לַגֻּלְגֹּלֶת (Shemos 16:16), an omer a head, is a measure, as the pasuk says, וְהָעֹמֶר עֲשִׂרִית הָאֵיפָה הוּא (Shemos 16:36), the omer is a tenth of an eifah.

The same word is the cut sheaf: וְהֵנִיף אֶת־הָעֹמֶר (Vayikra 23:11), he shall wave the sheaf; וְשָׁכַחְתָּ עֹמֶר בַּשָּׂדֶה (Devarim 24:19), and you forget a sheaf in the field; וְאָסַפְתִּי בָעֳמָרִים (Rus 2:7), and I will gather among the sheaves. Another pattern is עָמִיר: וּכְעָמִיר מֵאַחֲרֵי הַקֹּצֵר (Yirmiyahu 9:21), like a swathe behind the reaper, and וּכְלַפִּיד אֵשׁ בְּעָמִיר (Zechariah 12:6), like a torch of fire among the cut stalks. These, he says, are the bound bundles of ears. The verb stands in וְחִצְנוֹ מְעַמֵּר (Tehillim 129:7), of the one who binds the sheaves and fills his bosom.

משׁה.sense: To draw out of the water; and the entry gives also מֶשִׁי, silk.

more.t: כִּי מִן־הַמַּיִם מְשִׁיתִהוּ (Shemos 2:10), because I drew him out of the water. Some read from it וַיִּזְכֹּר יְמֵי־עוֹלָם מֹשֶׁה עַמּוֹ (Yeshayahu 63:11), or it is plain as it sounds, Moshe and his people. So too יַמְשֵׁנִי מִמַּיִם רַבִּים (Tehillim 18:17), He drew me out of many waters. The matter of all of them is drawing and bringing out.
וָאֲכַסֵּךְ מֶשִׁי (Yechezkel 16:10), and I covered you with silk, which he glosses as garments of silk, a thing well known.

משׁך.sense: To draw or pull, as a bow is drawn or a yoke is pulled; and from there to draw a thing out in time.

more.t: וְאִישׁ מָשַׁךְ בַּקֶּשֶׁת לְתֻמּוֹ (Melachim I 22:34), a man drew the bow in his innocence; אֲשֶׁר לֹא־מָשְׁכָה בְּעֹל (Devarim 21:3), which has not pulled in a yoke; תִּמְשֹׁךְ לִוְיָתָן בְּחַכָּה (Iyov 40:25), can you draw out the livyasan with a hook. Of a scribe, מֹשְׁכִים בְּשֵׁבֶט סֹפֵר (Shoftim 5:14), because the scribe draws the pen across the page as he writes. And לִמְשׁוֹךְ בַּיַּיִן אֶת־בְּשָׂרִי (Koheles 2:3) is to lead the body and draw it along with wine.

עַל־כֵּן מְשַׁכְתִּיךְ חָסֶד (Yirmiyahu 31:3) he reads as I have drawn kindness toward you, and so מְשֹׁךְ חַסְדְּךָ לְיֹדְעֶיךָ (Tehillim 36:11), draw out Your kindness to those who know You, on the model of וַיֵּט אֵילָו חָסֶד (Bereishis 39:21), and He extended kindness to him.

לֵךְ וּמָשַׁכְתָּ בְּהַר תָּבוֹר (Shoftim 4:6), go and draw toward Har Tavor, he explains as draw the people to you there. The word of drawing is used because the sense is bring them out against their will and win them over with words until you bring them to the war, for they were afraid of Sisra's army. So too וּמָשַׁכְתִּי אֵלֶיךָ אֶל־נַחַל קִישׁוֹן (Shoftim 4:6), and I will draw Sisra to you at Nachal Kishon: it is said that his astrologers saw his downfall and held him back from going out, and the Holy One strengthened his heart and drew him to Nachal Kishon. In וַיִּמְשֹׁךְ הָאֹרֵב (Shoftim 20:37) he gives two readings, that he drew out a blast on the shofar or that he drew the people with him toward the city.

לֹא תִמָּשֵׁךְ עוֹד (Yechezkel 12:25), it shall no longer be drawn out; וְיָמֶיהָ לֹא יִמָּשֵׁכוּ (Yeshayahu 13:22), her days shall not be prolonged; and תּוֹחֶלֶת מְמֻשָּׁכָה (Mishlei 13:12), hope drawn out long.

כִּי־גַרְתִּי מֶשֶׁךְ (Tehillim 120:5) is not of this sense but the name of a nation named in the Torah, וּמֶשֶׁךְ וְתִירָס (Bereishis 10:2). Yosef ben Gorion says they are the men of Tuscany, and Ibn Ezra explained מַשְׁכִּים הָיוּ (Yirmiyahu 5:8) as belonging to Meshech, since the strong horses come from there.

וּמֶשֶׁךְ חָכְמָה מִפְּנִינִים (Iyov 28:18) he reads as the preciousness of wisdom, since the name of a precious thing is drawn out to a distance. So too מֶשֶׁךְ־הַזָּרַע (Tehillim 126:6), since the seed is precious to the one who sows it, all the more so in a parched land, and for that reason the one carrying seed to sow is called בְּמֹשֵׁךְ הַזָּרַע (Amos 9:13).

שׁאף.sense: To draw in air, to snuff or to gasp; from there to swallow up greedily, and to look eagerly toward a thing.

more.t: שָׁאֲפָה רוּחַ (Yirmiyahu 2:24), she snuffs the wind, and שָׁאֲפוּ רוּחַ כַּתַּנִּים (Yirmiyahu 14:6), they gasped for air like jackals: this is smelling and drawing the air into the nose. The same of drawing air into the mouth, פִּי־פָעַרְתִּי וָאֶשְׁאָפָה (Tehillim 119:131), I opened my mouth wide and panted.

Pressed further the word is devouring: וְשָׁאַף צַמִּים חֵילָם (Iyov 5:5), the thirsty swallow up their wealth; כִּי־שְׁאָפַנִי אֱנוֹשׁ (Tehillim 56:2), man would swallow me up; הַשֹּׁאֲפִים עַל־עֲפַר־אֶרֶץ (Amos 2:7), who pant after the dust of the earth; הַשֹּׁאֲפִים אֶבְיוֹן (Amos 8:4), who swallow up the needy; אֶשֹּׁם וְאֶשְׁאַף יָחַד (Yeshayahu 42:14), I will lay waste and swallow together. All of these he glosses as swallowing.

In the matter of looking and watching for a thing: כְּעֶבֶד יִשְׁאַף־צֵל (Iyov 7:2), like a servant who longs for the shade; אַל־תִּשְׁאַף הַלָּיְלָה (Iyov 36:20), do not long for the night; שׁוֹאֵף זוֹרֵחַ הוּא שָׁם (Koheles 1:5), it presses toward the place where it rises. He allows שָׁאֲפָה רוּחַ to belong here too, רוּחַ then meaning a direction or quarter. All the senses in this root, he says, stand close to looking at a thing and setting one's aim on it.

בית.sense: A house; and from there a household, a bird's nest, a grave, a prison, and the inside of a thing.

more.t: כִּי תִבְנֶה בַּיִת חָדָשׁ (Devarim 22:8), when you build a new house, and אֵין לְשִׁפְחָתְךָ כֹל בַּבַּיִת (Melachim II 4:2), your maidservant has nothing in the house, which he calls plain.

A bird's nest is called a house: גַּם־צִפּוֹר מָצְאָה בַיִת (Tehillim 84:4), even the bird has found a house, and חֲסִידָה בְּרוֹשִׁים בֵּיתָהּ (Tehillim 104:17), the stork has her house in the cypresses. So too the grave, שָׁכְבוּ בְכָבוֹד אִישׁ בְּבֵיתוֹ (Yeshayahu 14:17), they lie in honour, each in his house; and the prison, אֲסִירָיו לֹא־פָתַח בָּיְתָה (Yeshayahu 14:15), he did not open the house for his prisoners.

וְשָׂמַחְתָּ אַתָּה וּבֵיתֶךָ (Devarim 14:26) is you and the people of your house. וַיַּעַשׂ לָהֶם בָּתִּים (Shemos 1:21) he first gives as households, that they were fruitful and multiplied, as in מוֹשִׁיב יְחִידִים בַּיְתָה (Tehillim 68:7), He settles the solitary in a household. What seems right to him is that Hashem hid them from Pharaoh so that he did them no harm, in the way said of Yirmiyahu and Baruch, that they were hidden (Yirmiyahu 36:26).

מִבַּיִת וּמִחוּץ (Shemos 25:11), within and without; כְּמַרְאֵה־אֵשׁ בֵּית־לָהּ סָבִיב (Yechezkel 1:27), the look of fire inside it round about; אֲחֹרֵיהֶם בָּיְתָה (Melachim I 7:25), their backs turned inward.

בִּיתָן is the palace, so called because a palace is a large and honoured house: שָׁב מִגִּנַּת הַבִּיתָן (Esther 7:8), he came back from the palace garden. בָּתִּים לַבַּדִּים (Shemos 37:14) are the settings for the staves; בָּתִּים לָאֲשֵׁרָה (Melachim II 23:7) are the hangings the women wove; כְּבֵית סָאתַיִם (Melachim I 18:32) is ground sown with two se'ah; בֵּית אֲבָנִים יֶחֱזֶה (Iyov 8:17) is a place of stones; and וּבָתֵּי הַנֶּפֶשׁ (Yeshayahu 3:20) is an ornament the women hang over the heart.

Some say בית is used as a delicate way of speaking, on the strength of כִּי שָׁחָה אֶל־מָוֶת בֵּיתָהּ (Mishlei 2:18), for her house sinks down to death. He answers that שָׁחָה may be said of the harlot herself, who sinks toward death, which is her house. His father writes that שָׁחָה here is masculine, on the pattern of עָשָׂה and בָּנָה, even though the accent falls on the earlier syllable.

חנה.sense: To encamp, and to encamp against a city; the camp מַחֲנֶה is from it, and he raises the spear חֲנִית as well.

more.t: קִרְיַת חָנָה דָוִד (Yeshayahu 29:1), the city where David encamped; וַיִּחַן־שָׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל (Shemos 19:2), and Yisrael encamped there; וַחֲנֵה עַל־הָעִיר וְלָכְדָהּ (Shmuel II 12:28), encamp against the city and capture it. He counts these as verbs that take no object, so פִּזַּר עַצְמוֹת חֹנָךְ (Tehillim 53:6), He scattered the bones of the one who besieges you, means one encamping upon you, just as בָּנַי יְצָאֻנִי (Yirmiyahu 10:20), my sons have gone out from me, and לֹא יְגֻרְךָ רָע (Tehillim 5:5), evil shall not dwell with You.

וְחָנִיתִי כַדּוּר עָלָיִךְ (Yeshayahu 29:3) he reads as I will encamp with a siege ring against you, and וְחָנִיתִי לְבֵיתִי מִצָּבָה (Zechariah 4:8) as I will encamp for my house, so that they will not fear any garrison encamping over them. He allows that both may instead be verbs that take an object.

מַחֲנֶה is found masculine and feminine: וְהָיָה הַמַּחֲנֶה הַנִּשְׁאָר (Bereishis 32:9), the camp that is left, against אִם־תַּחֲנֶה עָלַי מַחֲנֶה (Tehillim 27:3), if a camp encamps against me, and הַמַּחֲנֶה הָאַחַת (Bereishis 32:9), the one camp. The plural runs both ways too, מַחֲנֵיהֶם (Shmuel I 17:53) and מַחֲנוֹת (Bereishis 32:11). מַחֲנָיִם (Bereishis 32:3) means two camps, named for his own camp that had been with Lavan and the camp of Hashem that he saw afterward.

From the same root and the same matter he takes אֶל־בֵּית הַבּוֹר וְאֶל־הַחֲנֻיוֹת (Yirmiyahu 37:16), to the dungeon house and to the cells. The word is well known in the words of Chazal for a shop, and it is called so because travellers lodge there.

He raises the possibility that חֲנִית, the spear, belongs to this root: וְלַהֶבֶת חֲנִיתוֹ (Shmuel I 17:7), the blade of his spear; וַתֵּצֵא הַחֲנִית מֵאַחֲרָיו (Shmuel II 2:23), and the spear came out behind him; נִשְׁעָן עַל־חֲנִיתוֹ (Shmuel II 1:6), leaning on his spear. The plural is found masculine, הַחֲנִיתִים וְאֶת־הַמָּגִנּוֹת (Divrei HaYamim II 23:9), the spears and the shields, and feminine, וַחֲנִיתוֹתֵיהֶם לְמַזְמֵרוֹת (Yeshayahu 2:4), their spears into pruning hooks.

שֹאר.sense: שְׂאֹר, the leaven, the sourdough with which the dough is leavened.

more.t: One line, on כִּי כָל־שְׂאֹר (Vayikra 2:11), for any leaven, and שְׂאֹר לֹא יִמָּצֵא בְּבָתֵּיכֶם (Shemos 12:19), no leaven shall be found in your houses. It is the starter with which the dough is leavened.

שׁאר.sense: To remain and be left over, and the remnant שְׁאֵרִית; in a second sense שְׁאֵר, flesh, and from it a near relative.

more.t: עוֹד שָׁאַר הַקָּטָן (Shmuel I 16:11), the youngest still remains; וְאִם־מְעַט נִשְׁאַר (Vayikra 25:52), and if little remains; וְהָעָם הַנִּשְׁאָר (Melachim II 25:22), the people who were left. Where the verb takes an object, לֹא הִשְׁאִיר שָׂרִיד (Yehoshua 10:28), he left no survivor, and תַּשְׁאִיר מֵאָה (Amos 5:3), it shall leave a hundred. The noun is שְׁאֵרִית יִשְׂרָאֵל (Tzefaniah 3:13), the remnant of Yisrael, written also without the alef, שֵׁרִית יִשְׂרָאֵל (Divrei HaYamim I 12:38).

In וְכָל־הַנִּשְׁאָר מִכָּל־הַמְּקֹמוֹת אֲשֶׁר הוּא גָר־שָׁם (Ezra 1:4), and everyone who is left, of all the places where he lives, he ties the mem of מִכָּל not to הַנִּשְׁאָר but to the words that follow, יְנַשְּׂאוּהוּ אַנְשֵׁי מְקֹמוֹ, the men of his place shall support him, since הנשאר joins only with a beis.

שֵׁרִיתִיךָ לְטוֹב (Yirmiyahu 15:11) he takes from this root, and the Targum renders it אם לָא סוֹפֵךְ יְהֵא לְטַב, if your end will not be for good. Dunash wrote it from the Aramaic וּמְשָׁרֵא קִטְרִין (Daniel 5:12), loosing knots, and its sense is then I have released you. He reads the pasuk as Hashem telling the navi that He will release him from his confinement and make the enemy entreat him in the time of Yisrael's trouble, which is what the chief of the guard said to Yirmiyahu, הִנֵּה פִתַּחְתִּיךָ הַיּוֹם מִן־הָאזִקִּים אֲשֶׁר עַל־יָדֶךָ (Yirmiyahu 40:4), see, I have freed you today from the chains on your hand.

שְׁאָר יָשׁוּב (Yeshayahu 10:21), a remnant shall return. He suggests that וּשְׁאָר רוּחַ לוֹ (Malachi 2:15) carries advantage and high standing, since יתר and שאר are one matter. He reads the pasuk of Avraham, who was one and a father in his faith to those who came after him, and did not chase after desire but sought seed of Hashem. His father reads ולא אחד עשה as the people's own words to the navi, put as a question: Avraham, who was one, did he not do as we do, when he left his wife and took Hagar her maidservant, and he with a remnant of spirit and a navi? And the navi answered them that the other one sought seed of Hashem, and did it by his wife's will and at her word, while you are to guard your spirit and let none of you betray his wife.

A second sense is flesh: אִם־יָכִין שְׁאֵר לְעַמּוֹ (Tehillim 78:20), can He prepare flesh for His people; וַיַּמְטֵר עֲלֵיהֶם כֶּעָפָר שְׁאֵר (Tehillim 78:27), He rained flesh upon them like dust; כָּלָה שְׁאֵרִי וּלְבָבִי (Tehillim 73:26), my flesh and my heart fail. From this a man's near relatives are called שְׁאֵר, אִישׁ אִישׁ אֶל־כָּל־שְׁאֵר בְּשָׂרוֹ (Vayikra 18:6), any man to any near of kin, and שַׁאֲרָה הֵנָּה (Vayikra 18:17), they are near kin, as though to say they are one flesh. A man's relative is like his own flesh, as it says אַךְ עַצְמִי וּבְשָׂרִי אָתָּה (Bereishis 29:14), you are my bone and my flesh.

The word is used of food at large, שְׁאֵרָהּ כְּסוּתָהּ וְעֹנָתָהּ (Shemos 21:10), her food, her covering and her conjugal right, which the Targum renders זִיּוּנַהּ, her provisioning. Another sense is משארת, בָּרוּךְ טַנְאֲךָ וּמִשְׁאַרְתֶּךָ (Devarim 28:5), blessed is your basket and your kneading trough, the trough in which the dough is kneaded; but מִשְׁאֲרֹתָם צְרֻרֹת בְּשִׂמְלֹתָם (Shemos 12:34), their kneading bowls bound up in their garments, is the dough itself. It may be called so for food, since bread is a man's chief food.

פדר.sense: הַפֶּדֶר, the fat of the korban.

more.t: Two pesukim, וְאֶת־הַפָּדֶר (Vayikra 1:8) and וְאֶת־רֹאשׁוֹ וְאֶת־פִּדְרוֹ (Vayikra 1:12), its head and its fat, which he glosses as fat; so the Targum renders וְיָת תַּרְבֵּיהּ, and its fat. Chazal taught that the fat was laid over the place of the slaughter and brought up so, out of respect for Heaven.

רבה.sense: To grow many or great; from it הַרְבֵּה for quantity, the rearing of a child, the archer, and the locust.

more.t: וְחָיִיתָ וְרָבִיתָ (Devarim 30:16), and you shall live and multiply; אֶסְפְּרֵם מֵחוֹל יִרְבּוּן (Tehillim 139:18), were I to count them they would be more than the sand; פְּרֵה וּרְבֵה (Bereishis 35:11), be fruitful and multiply. Where the verb takes an object, הִרְבָּה אַשְׁמָה (Divrei HaYamim II 33:23), he multiplied guilt, and וְלֹא יַרְבֶּה־לּוֹ נָשִׁים (Devarim 17:17), he shall not take many wives.

הַרְבֵּה stands for quantity: אֵשׁ וְעֵצִים הַרְבֵּה (Yeshayahu 30:33), much fire and wood; וְלִבִּי רָאָה הַרְבֵּה חָכְמָה וָדָעַת (Koheles 1:16), my heart has seen much wisdom and knowledge; וְהַרְבֵּה עִמּוֹ פְדוּת (Tehillim 130:7), and with Him is much redemption. Other patterns are לְמַרְבֵּה הַמִּשְׂרָה (Yeshayahu 9:6), which takes a tzeirei because it leans on the word after it, and כִּי מַרְבִּית הָעָם (Divrei HaYamim II 30:18), for the multitude of the people.

Rabbi Yehudah set וְלֹא־רִבִּיתָ בִּמְחִירֵיהֶם (Tehillim 44:13), and You did not raise their price, with וּבְמַרְבִּית לֹא־תִתֵּן אָכְלֶךָ (Vayikra 25:37), you shall not give your food at increase, and וְתַרְבִּית לֹא יִקָּח (Yechezkel 18:8), he takes no increase, in a sense of its own. He holds there is no need for that, and that they belong to this same sense, as they plainly sound.

A second sense, near the first, is bringing up: רִבְּתָה גוּרֶיהָ (Yechezkel 19:2), she reared her cubs, and אֲשֶׁר־טִפַּחְתִּי וְרִבִּיתִי (Eichah 2:22), those I nursed and reared. The nouns are תַּרְבּוּת אֲנָשִׁים חַטָּאִים (Bamidbar 32:14), a brood of sinful men, and וְכָל־מַרְבִּית בֵּיתְךָ (Shmuel I 2:33), all the increase of your house, which he glosses as the matter of growing up.

A third sense is רֹבֶה קַשָּׁת (Bereishis 21:20), one who shoots arrows with a bow. Some take it instead from the Targum of נַעַר (Bereishis 21:12), רַבְיָא, a lad. He also allows that אֶת־הָאַרְבֶּה לְמִינוֹ (Vayikra 11:22), the locust after its kind, is from this root, called so because it is a numerous kind.

ציץ.sense: To blossom and to show itself; the blossom צִיץ, the golden plate of the Kohen Gadol, and the fringe צִיצִת.

more.t: צָץ הַמַּטֶּה (Yechezkel 7:10), the staff has blossomed; וַיָּצֵץ צִיץ (Bamidbar 17:23), and it put forth a blossom; יָצִיץ וּפָרַח יִשְׂרָאֵל (Yeshayahu 27:6), Yisrael shall bud and blossom. וּפְטוּרֵי צִצִּים (Melachim I 6:18) are carvings shaped like flowers and buds, the yud swallowed in the dagesh. And וְהָיְתָה צִיצַת נֹבֵל (Yeshayahu 28:4), the fading blossom, takes the feminine ending though נֹבֵל is masculine. The matter of all of them is the flowers opening and coming into sight.

Close to it is מֵצִיץ מִן־הַחֲרַכִּים (Shir HaShirim 2:9), peering in through the lattices, which is to say showing himself and being seen and looking out through the windows. Some read from it וְעָלָיו יָצִיץ נִזְרוֹ (Tehillim 132:18), his crown shall shine upon him: in the place where He makes a horn sprout for David, there his crown will be seen. Or its sense is that the crown on his head will bud and blossom, meaning that his greatness and glory will grow day by day.
Another sense is a plate of gold: וְעָשִׂיתָ צִּיץ זָהָב (Shemos 28:36), and you shall make a plate of gold, and צִיץ נֵזֶר־הַקֹּדֶשׁ (Shemos 39:30), the plate of the holy crown.

Another sense is תְּנוּ־צִיץ לְמוֹאָב (Yirmiyahu 48:9), give a wing to Moav, a wing to fly with. The Targum of סְנַפִּיר (Vayikra 11:9) is צִיצִין, and Chazal speak of the fins as what the fish moves by.

וְעָשׂוּ לָהֶם צִיצִת (Bamidbar 15:38), and they shall make themselves fringes. The loose end of a garment, what is left over from the weave and hangs from it, is called ציצית, and so the threads that the Torah commands to be hung on the corner are called ציצית. Hanging locks of hair are the same, וַיִּקָּחֵנִי בְּצִיצִת רֹאשִׁי (Yechezkel 8:3), and he took me by a lock of my head, and some read מֵצִיץ מִן־הַחֲרַכִּים this way too, showing the locks of his head. Chazal said there is no ציצית but a loose end, and that a third is the twisted cord and two thirds the loose end.

גדל.sense: To be great, in honour, in years, in size or in number; and to make a thing grow or rear it up.

more.h: Great in honour, great in years
more.t: מַה־גָּדְלוּ מַעֲשֶׂיךָ (Tehillim 92:6), how great are Your works, and גִּדַּל הַמֶּלֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ (Esther 3:3), the king Achashverosh promoted him, are greatness in honour and standing. וַיִּגְדַּל הַיֶּלֶד (Bereishis 21:8), the child grew, and וַיִּגְדְּלוּ הַנְּעָרִים (Bereishis 25:26), the lads grew up, are the adding of years. So גָּדוֹל is read both ways: גַּם הָאִישׁ מֹשֶׁה גָּדוֹל מְאֹד (Shemos 11:3) in honour and standing, and אֲחִי יֶפֶת הַגָּדוֹל (Bereishis 10:21) in years, as Chazal explained that Yefes was the eldest of the brothers.

The word takes its measure from the thing it describes: אֶת־שְׁנֵי הַמְּאֹרֹת הַגְּדֹלִים (Bereishis 1:16) are great in light; אִשָּׁה גְדוֹלָה (Melachim II 4:8) is a woman of standing and honour; הַמַּסֹּת הַגְּדֹלֹת (Devarim 7:19) are great in wonder; חַיִל גָּדוֹל מְאֹד (Yechezkel 37:10) means a great number, and so זְבָחִים גְּדוֹלִים (Nechemiah 12:43), since the word serves for abundance both in quality and in quantity.

רַק הַכִּסֵּא אֶגְדַּל מִמֶּךָּ (Bereishis 41:40), only in the throne will I be greater than you, he explains as greater in the matter of the throne, since here too the verb takes no object, as Rabbi Yonah wrote.

עַל־פְּרִי־גֹדֶל (Yeshayahu 10:12), the fruit of pride; כְּגֹדֶל חַסְדֶּךָ (Bamidbar 14:19), according to the greatness of Your kindness; הַלְלוּהוּ כְּרֹב גֻּדְּלוֹ (Tehillim 150:2), praise Him for His abundant greatness. Another pattern is גדלה, as in וְלִגְדֻלָּתוֹ אֵין חֵקֶר (Tehillim 145:3), and His greatness is unsearchable; and another is בִּגְדֹל זְרוֹעֲךָ (Shemos 15:16), by the greatness of Your arm.

מִנְּעוּרַי גְּדֵלַנִי כְאָב (Iyov 31:18), from my youth he grew up with me as a father: he takes the verb as taking no object, גדל עמי, he grew with me, said of the orphan mentioned above, while Rabbi Yonah wrote that גְדֵלַנִי is a past tense. In the doubled form it is plainly making a thing grow: מַיִם גִּדְּלוּהוּ (Yechezkel 31:4), the waters made it grow, וְגֶשֶׁם יְגַדֵּל (Yeshayahu 44:14), and rain makes it grow, and גַּדֵּל פֶּרַע שְׂעַר רֹאשׁוֹ (Bamidbar 6:5), letting the hair of his head grow long.

מִגְדָּל is a tower, the tall and large building: וַיִּבֶן מִגְדָּל בְּתוֹכוֹ (Yeshayahu 5:2), and he built a tower in it, and אֶתֹּץ אֶת־הַמִּגְדָּל הַזֶּה (Shoftim 8:9), I will pull down this tower. The plural is בִּנְפֹל מִגְדָּלִים (Yeshayahu 30:25), when towers fall, and in the feminine וּמִגְדְּלֹתַיִךְ יִתֹּץ (Yechezkel 26:8), he will pull down your towers. מִגְדְּלוֹת מֶרְקָחִים (Shir HaShirim 5:13) he takes as the flowers that grow among the spices.

גְּדִלִים תַּעֲשֶׂה־לָּךְ (Devarim 22:12): the fringes hanging from a garment that are not woven are called גדילים, and גְּדִלִים מַעֲשֵׂה שַׁרְשְׁרוֹת (Melachim I 7:17) are cords worked like chains, which is how the Targum renders מַעֲשֵׂה עֲבֹת (Shemos 28:22). He asks why the Torah says גדיל here and ציצית elsewhere (Bamidbar 15:38), and answers that the mitzvah of tzitzis is that a third be the twisted cord and two thirds the loose end.

פתל.sense: Turning and twisting: crooked in conduct, a thread twisted double, and the פְּתִיל, a strip of cloth.

more.t: אֵין בָּהֶם נִפְתָּל וְעִקֵּשׁ (Mishlei 8:8), there is nothing twisted or crooked in them; וַעֲצַת נִפְתָּלִים נִמְהָרָה (Iyov 5:13), the counsel of the crooked is rushed; וְעִם־עִקֵּשׁ תִּתְפַּתָּל (Tehillim 18:27), with the crooked You deal in kind. The matter of all of them is turning about and distortion, and the adjective with the letters doubled is דּוֹר עִקֵּשׁ וּפְתַלְתֹּל (Devarim 32:5), a crooked and twisted generation.

נַפְתּוּלֵי אֱלֹהִים נִפְתַּלְתִּי (Bereishis 30:8) he reads as I turned about and strove with my sister to overcome her, and I have prevailed. נפתולי is joined to the name of Hashem to mark how great and how many the wrestlings were, on the model of שַׁלְהֶבֶתְיָה (Shir HaShirim 8:6) and עִיר־גְּדוֹלָה לֵאלֹהִים (Yonah 3:3), an exceedingly great city. Others read the phrase from the twisted thread: I grew strong against my sister, since a thread doubled and twisted is the stronger for it.

אֲשֶׁר אֵין־צָמִיד פָּתִיל (Bamidbar 19:9) he explains as a small piece of cloth, like פתילת הבגד in the words of the Mishnah, a wick made from a garment. To his mind חֹתָמְךָ וּפְתִילֶךָ (Bereishis 38:18), your seal and your cord, is the same, meaning Yehudah's cloak or the turban on his head; and that is how the Targum understood it, rendering שׁוֹשִׁפָּךְ, the same word it uses for וַיָּלֶט פָּנָיו בְּאַדַּרְתּוֹ (Melachim I 19:13), and he wrapped his face in his mantle. Some of the commentators read חותמך ופתילך as a thread, but he holds by what he has written.

פְּתִיל־הַנְּעֹרֶת (Shoftim 16:9), a thread of tow, and פְּתִיל תְּכֵלֶת (Shemos 39:31), a thread of techeiles, are a cord doubled and twisted, and Chazal said of it פתיל שיהיה טווי ושזור, that it be spun and twisted. Everything that falls under this root is one matter, distortion and turning about, since a thread doubled and twisted is turned about itself, and so is cloth made from twisted threads.
