more.t: הֲיִנְהַק פֶּרֶא עֲלֵי דֶשֶׁא (Iyov 6:5), does the wild donkey bray over grass, and בֵּין שִׂיחִים יִנְהָקוּ (Iyov 30:6), among the bushes they bray.

שׁען.sense: To lean on a thing, and so to rely on it; the nouns are the stay or support a man leans upon.

more.t: וְנִשְׁעַן לִגְבוּל מוֹאָב (Bamidbar 21:15), leaning up against the border of Moav; וְהוּא נִשְׁעָן עַל יָדִי (Melachim II 5:18), he leans on my hand; יִשָּׁעֵן עַל בֵּיתוֹ (Iyov 8:15), he leans on his house. The same word is relying on Hashem, at Yeshayahu 10:20 and Divrei HaYamim II 13:18, and it is set against לְהִשָּׁעֵן עַל מַכֵּהוּ (Yeshayahu 10:20), leaning on the one who strikes him.

מַשְׁעֵן וּמַשְׁעֵנָה (Yeshayahu 3:1), stay and support, and in construct in that same pasuk כֹּל מִשְׁעַן לֶחֶם וְכֹל מִשְׁעַן מָיִם, every stay of bread and every stay of water. In another form, לְמִשְׁעָן לִי (Tehillim 18:19), Hashem became a support to me; and he allows that כֹּל מִשְׁעַן לֶחֶם may belong to this second form.
עַל מִשְׁעֶנֶת הַקָּנֶה הָרָצוּץ (Yeshayahu 36:6), on the staff of that crushed reed, and עַל מִשְׁעַנְתּוֹ (Shemos 21:19), on his staff.

מַקֵּל שָׁקֵד (Yirmiyahu 1:12), a rod of almond; מַקֵּל תִּפְאָרָה (Yirmiyahu 48:17), a rod of beauty; וּבְמַקֵּל יָד (Yechezkel 39:9), a hand staff; מַקַּל לִבְנֶה (Bereishis 30:37), a rod of livneh; כִּי בְמַקְלִי עָבַרְתִּי (Bereishis 32:11), with my staff I crossed over; וּמַקְלוֹ יַגִּיד לוֹ (Hoshea 4:12), his stick tells him.

The first three carry a tzeirei and מַקַּל לִבְנֶה a patach; with a suffix and in the plural the strong point falls away, as at כִּי בְמַקְלִי עָבַרְתִּי and וַיַּצֵּג אֶת הַמַּקְלוֹת (Bereishis 30:38), he set up the rods. He allows that the word may belong with the roots whose first letter is a nun, the mem being added.

שׁרב.sense: The scorching heat; and in one pasuk the parched ground itself.

more.t: וְלֹא יַכֵּם שָׁרָב וָשָׁמֶשׁ (Yeshayahu 49:10), neither scorching heat nor sun shall strike them: he glosses it simply as the heat. At וְהָיָה הַשָּׁרָב לַאֲגָם (Yeshayahu 35:7), the sharav shall become a pool, he reads it as the place of desert and drought. The Targum renders אֲכָלַנִי חֹרֶב (Bereishis 31:40), drought consumed me, with this same word, אֲכַלְנִי שַׁרְבָא.

חטר.sense: A shoot or rod; the Targum uses the word for a staff.

more.t: וְיָצָא חֹטֶר מִגֶּזַע יִשָׁי (Yeshayahu 11:1), a shoot shall come out of the stock of Yishai. The Targum renders מַטֶּה (Shemos 4:2), a staff, as חוּטְרָא.

בְּפִי אֱוִיל חֹטֶר גַּאֲוָה (Mishlei 14:3) he reads as the rod of pride in the fool's mouth, since the fool speaks proud and lofty words against men. Rabbi Yonah takes it the other way about: on account of the words the fool speaks, a rod of pride comes upon him, meaning that he is struck great blows for what he said.

זקן.sense: To grow old, and the old man; and the same letters give the beard.

more.t: וַיְהִי כִּי זָקֵן יִצְחָק (Bereishis 27:1) is the past verb, Yitzchak grew old, while וְאַבְרָהָם זָקֵן (Bereishis 24:1) is the adjective, Avraham was old. So also זָקַנְתִּי וָשַׂבְתִּי (Shmuel I 12:2), I am old and grey, and in construct זְקַן בֵּיתוֹ (Bereishis 24:2), the elder of his house.

כִּי בֶן זְקֻנִים הוּא לוֹ (Bereishis 37:3), a son of his old age, and בֵּן לִזְקֻנָיו (Bereishis 21:2), a son to his old age: זְקֻנִים is a plural noun from which no singular comes, like נְעוּרִים, youth, and בְּתוּלִים, maidenhood. Other forms are מִזֹּקֶן (Bereishis 48:10), the eyes of Yisrael heavy with age, and זִקְנָה (Yeshayahu 46:4; Bereishis 24:36).
אִם יַזְקִין בָּאָרֶץ שָׁרְשׁוֹ (Iyov 14:8), though its root grow old in the ground, and גַּם כִּי יַזְקִין לֹא יָסוּר מִמֶּנָּה (Mishlei 22:6), even when he is old he will not turn from it.

וְגַם אֶת הַזָּקָן תִּסְפֶּה (Yeshayahu 7:20), the beard too shall be swept away, and in construct בִּזְקַן עֲמָשָׂא לִנְשָׁק לוֹ (Shmuel II 20:9), by Amasa's beard, to kiss him. The word comes as a masculine at עַד יְצַמַּח זְקַנְכֶם, until your beard grows, and as a feminine at וְכָל זָקָן גְּרֻעָה (Yirmiyahu 48:37), every beard shorn. For זְקַנְכֶם, and for וְהֶחֱזַקְתִּי בִּזְקָנוֹ, I took hold of his beard, his edition prints citations that break off unfinished and give no address.

ישׁשׁ.sense: The aged man, further on in years than the זָקֵן or the שָׂב.

more.t: זָקֵן וְיָשֵׁשׁ (Divrei HaYamim II 36:17), old and aged, with a tzeirei; and with a chirik גַּם שָׂב גַּם יָשִׁישׁ בָּנוּ (Iyov 15:10), among us are both the grey-haired and the aged, and בִּישִׁישִׁים חָכְמָה (Iyov 12:12), wisdom is with the aged. They are the elders, many of days, and he holds the yashish further on in years than the zakein and than the sav.
He holds it right that the word be of the sense of יֵשׁ, there is, and reckons יָשָׁה and יְשַׁשׁ one matter; the old man is called יָשִׁישׁ because being has stood in him many days.

קשׁשׁ.sense: To gather up small things, straw or thin sticks; and from that, to search out faults and collect them.

more.t: לְקֹשֵׁשׁ קַשׁ (Shemos 5:12), to gather straw, and מְקֹשֵׁשׁ עֵצִים (Bamidbar 15:32), gathering wood. The kash is the fine straw, or the thin sticks, and the verb is derived from it: the picking up of fine things, straw or wood, which he names in the vernacular.

The word serves also for hunting out a man's blemishes and gathering them well, since they are like fine things that need careful searching. הִתְקוֹשְׁשׁוּ וָקוֹשּׁוּ (Tzefaniah 2:1) he reads as search yourselves of your own evil blemishes and only then search others, as Chazal derived from this pasuk (Bava Basra 60b): correct yourself and afterwards correct others. They said likewise in the Yerushalmi, let us clear ourselves before we clear others.

וְלַמּוֹכִיחַ בַּשַּׁעַר יְקֹשׁוּן (Yeshayahu 29:21) belongs here as well, the quiescent letter standing in place of the doubling. It is of men who set themselves to reprove the reprovers, in the manner of what Chazal said (Bava Basra 15b) of a generation that judges its judges: one says to him, take the splinter from between your eyes, and he says back, take the beam from between your eyes.

שׁבט.sense: The tribe, which is larger than the family; and the rod, for striking or for chastening, and so the ruler's staff and the ruler himself.

more.t: לְשֵׁבֶט וּלְמִשְׁפָּחָה (Shoftim 18:19), for a tribe and for a family; שְׁבָטִים שִׁבְטֵי יָהּ (Tehillim 122:4), the tribes of Hashem; בְּכָל שִׁבְטֵי בִנְיָמִן (Shoftim 20:12), through all the tribes of Binyamin; and הִתְעוּ אֶת מִצְרַיִם פִּנַּת שְׁבָטֶיהָ (Yeshayahu 19:13), they led Mitzrayim astray, the cornerstone of her tribes, which he closes by saying that the sense of them all is family. The sense is family, but the shevet is the larger of the two: מִשְׁפְּחוֹת שִׁבְטֵי בִנְיָמִן (Shmuel I 9:21), the families of the tribes of Binyamin, and וַיַּקְרֵב אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל לִשְׁבָטָיו (Yehoshua 7:16), he brought Yisrael near by its tribes, and only then וַיַּקְרֵב אֶת מִשְׁפַּחַת יְהוּדָה, the family of Yehudah.

more.h: One word for all the tribes
more.t: וְיִשְׂרָאֵל שֵׁבֶט נַחֲלָתוֹ (Yirmiyahu 10:16), and Yisrael is the tribe of His inheritance, where the one word covers all the tribes together.

וְכִי יַכֶּה אִישׁ אֶת עַבְדּוֹ אוֹ אֶת אֲמָתוֹ בַּשֵּׁבֶט (Shemos 21:20), striking his servant with the rod; תְּרֹעֵם בְּשֵׁבֶט בַּרְזֶל (Tehillim 2:9), You shall break them with a rod of iron; וּפָקַדְתִּי בְשֵׁבֶט פִּשְׁעָם (Tehillim 89:33), I will visit their sin with a rod; שֵׁבֶט מוּסָר יַרְחִיקֶנָּה מִמֶּנּוּ (Mishlei 22:15), the rod of discipline drives it far from him. It is a מטה, a staff, and the family is called a מטה as well, as he writes at the root נָטָה, since the men of a family lean each one on his fellow.

more.h: Rain as rod or as kindness
more.t: אִם לְשֵׁבֶט אִם לְאַרְצוֹ (Iyov 37:13) he takes as the rod of chastening: sometimes the rain comes as a rod and a chastisement upon the world, sweeping away the seed and ruining everything, and sometimes לְאַרְצוֹ, for the world's need, because they do His will; and sometimes He brings it in kindness though the people of the world are guilty.

Since a ruler carries a rod in his hand, and the rod for chastening the people is in his hand, the head and the ruler are themselves called שֵׁבֶט: שֵׁבֶט מֹשְׁלִים (Yeshayahu 14:5), the rod of rulers; לֹא יָסוּר שֵׁבֶט מִיהוּדָה (Bereishis 49:10), the sceptre shall not depart from Yehudah; שֵׁבֶט מִישֹׁר שֵׁבֶט מַלְכוּתֶךָ (Tehillim 45:7), a sceptre of uprightness is the sceptre of your kingdom. A people with a scribe at its head is called so too: מֹשְׁכִים בְּשֵׁבֶט סֹפֵר (Shoftim 5:14), they that handle the scribe's rod.

הֲדָבָר דִּבַּרְתִּי אֶת אַחַד שִׁבְטֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל (Shmuel II 7:7), did I speak a word with one of the tribes of Yisrael, he reads as meaning with the heads and the kings; and the parallel pasuk has אֶת אַחַד שֹׁפְטֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל (Divrei HaYamim I 17:6), one of the judges of Yisrael.

פשׁת.sense: Flax, and the linen made of it; the word is feminine, yet its suffix and its plural both come in masculine form.

more.h: The two pesukim he opens with
more.t: וְהַפִּשְׁתָּה וְהַשְּׂעֹרָה נֻכָּתָה (Shemos 9:31), the flax and the barley were struck, and וּפִשְׁתָּה כֵהָה לֹא יְכַבֶּנָּה (Yeshayahu 42:3), a dim flax wick he will not put out.

more.h: Masculine forms on a feminine word
more.t: The suffix comes in the masculine although the thing is feminine, צַמְרִי וּפִשְׁתִּי (Hoshea 2:7), my wool and my flax; and so does the plural, כַּפִּשְׁתִּים אֲשֶׁר בָּעֲרוּ בָאֵשׁ (Shoftim 15:14), like flax burnt in fire, and בַּצֶּמֶר אוֹ בַפִּשְׁתִּים (Vayikra 13:52), in the wool or in the linen.

בְּפִשְׁתֵּי הָעֵץ (Yehoshua 2:6) he reads as the wood of the flax, since it was still in its stalk, and a stalk is called עֵץ. A construct of this kind turns about in Hebrew, the governing word becoming the governed and the governed the governing, as תּוֹלַעַת שָׁנִי, the scarlet worm, stands beside וְאֶת־שְׁנִי הַתּוֹלַעַת, the worm's scarlet. It holds only where each of the two can stand either way, and everything goes by the sense.

כתן.sense: A tunic, the garment worn on the body; the noun appears in several patterns, and at times it and the robe are named together.

more.t: פָּשַׁטְתִּי אֶת־כֻּתָּנְתִּי (Shir HaShirim 5:3), I have taken off my tunic, and of Yosef, וַיַּפְשִׁיטוּ אֶת־יוֹסֵף אֶת־כֻּתָּנְתּוֹ, they stripped Yosef of his tunic. The plural is כֻּתֳּנֹת (Shemos 40:14), you shall clothe them in tunics, and בְּכֻתֳּנֹתָם (Vayikra 10:5), they carried them in their tunics.
In those two plurals the tav carries a bare sheva, though by rule it should carry a kamatz katan; in another exact sefer he found it written with the kamatz katan.

הַכָּתְנֹת שֵׁשׁ (Shemos 39:26 in his edition), the linen tunics, and כָּתְנוֹת עוֹר (Bereishis 3:21), tunics of skin; then הַכֻּתֹּנֶת (Bereishis 37:31), the tunic they dipped in blood, and כְּתֹנֶת פַּסִּים (Bereishis 37:3), a striped tunic.

At times the tunic and the robe are spoken of as one, as though both were a single thing, from וְעָלֶיהָ כְּתֹנֶת פַּסִּים כִּי כֵן תִּלְבַּשְׁןָ בְּנוֹת־הַמֶּלֶךְ הַבְּתוּלֹת מְעִילִים (Shmuel II 13:18), she had on a striped tunic, for so the king's virgin daughters dressed, in robes. But the tunic written in the bigdei kehunah is not the robe, since each of them is a garment in its own right.

קטן.sense: To be small, and to count for little in someone's eyes; as a noun, the small one, whether in size, in age, or in what it is worth.

more.t: קָטֹנְתִּי מִכֹּל הַחֲסָדִים (Bereishis 32:11), I am too small for all the kindnesses, and וַתִּקְטַן עוֹד זֹאת בְּעֵינֶיךָ (Shmuel II 7:19), and this was still a small thing in your eyes.

הַמָּאוֹר הַקָּטֹן (Bereishis 1:16), the lesser light; קָטֹן וְגָדוֹל שָׁם הוּא (Iyov 3:19), small and great are there alike; and קָטָנִּי עָבָה (Melachim I 12:10), which he reads as my little finger. With a kamatz, וְדָוִד הוּא הַקָּטָן (Shmuel I 17:14), and David was the youngest.

הַקְּטַנִּים עִם־הַגְּדֹלִים (Tehillim 115:13), the small together with the great; קְטַנָּה אוֹ גְדוֹלָה (Bamidbar 22:18), a small thing or a great one; and כִּי מִי בַז לְיוֹם קְטַנּוֹת (Zecharyah 4:10), who has despised a day of small things. To make small is לְהַקְטִין אֵיפָה (Amos 8:5), to shrink the eifah.
The grammar of קָטָנִּי עָבָה he says he has set out in the section on grammar that he put before the book, in the gate of nouns.

כיל.sense: The miser, the man who lays out everything by a set measure and nothing beyond it; he stands opposite the open-handed man.

more.t: וּלְכִילַי לֹא יֵאָמֵר שׁוֹעַ (Yeshayahu 32:5), the miser will not be called open-handed, with a chirik; and with a tzeirei, וְכֵלַי כֵּלָיו רָעִים (Yeshayahu 32:7), the miser, his measures are bad. The yud is the yud of relation, as in מוֹכִיחַ אָדָם אַחֲרַי (Mishlei 28:23), one who reproves a man after me, and הוּא הַהֵיכָל לִפְנָי (Melachim I 6:17), that was the Heichal before me.

more.h: Where he takes the word from
more.t: In his own view the word is cut from the sense of וְכָל בַּשָּׁלִשׁ (Yeshayahu 40:12), he measured out by a measure, and from that root: the man is called a miser because he conducts his affairs and lays out his expenses by a fixed measure, so that nothing is left over.

כֵּלָיו is the noun of miserliness, one of them כֵּל on the pattern of גֵּר and כֵּן, the plural כֵּלִים; it means that his measures are bad. A fixed and even measure is good in most things, but the miser's measures are bad in all of them, since he adds nothing to the set measure, not in his household outlay and not in giving to the poor, and his eye is grudging over everything he spends.
He says he explains the word there too, from כְּלִי and כֵּלִים, vessels, and gives a foreign word for it.

כול.sense: To measure, and so to hold or contain; from there to bear and endure, and in the doubled form to sustain a man with food.

more.t: וְכָל בַּשָּׁלִשׁ (Yeshayahu 40:12) he glosses as: and he measured. Of vessels, אַלְפַּיִם בַּת יָכִיל (Melachim I 7:26), it held two thousand bath, that was its measure; קָטֹן מֵהָכִיל אֶת־הָעֹלָה (Melachim I 8:64), too small to hold the olah, its measure not large enough for all the olos and shelamim; and אֲשֶׁר לֹא־יָכִלוּ הַמָּיִם (Yirmiyahu 2:13), broken cisterns that do not hold the water but let it out.

more.h: The large cup, and the sword
more.t: מִרְבָּה לְהָכִיל (Yechezkel 23:32) is the cup that is large enough to hold much, as the pasuk there calls it deep and wide. Of the sword he says לְהָכִיל, that it was whetted to hold and bear the killing, and to make its flash the greater, to put fear in the nations; his father reads that לְהָכִיל as לְהַאֲכִיל, to feed, which he has written at the root אכל.

וּמִי יְכִילֶנּוּ (Yoel 2:11), who can bear him. In the doubled form, לֹא יְכַלְכְּלוּךָ (Melachim I 8:27), the heavens and the heaven of heavens cannot contain you or bear you; וְנִלְאֵיתִי כַּלְכֵל (Yirmiyahu 20:9), I am worn out holding it in; וּמִי מְכַלְכֵּל אֶת־יוֹם בּוֹאוֹ (Malachi 3:2), who can bear the day of his coming; and הַנִּצָּבָה לֹא יְכַלְכֵּל (Zecharyah 11:16), the sick one left standing he will neither bear up nor strengthen.

more.h: The body's illness and the soul's
more.t: רוּחַ אִישׁ יְכַלְכֵּל מַחֲלֵהוּ וְרוּחַ נְכֵאָה מִי יִשָּׂאֶנָּה (Mishlei 18:14), a man's spirit bears up his illness, but a broken spirit who can carry: it is lighter to bear the sickness of the body than the sickness of the soul.

וְכִלְכַּלְתִּי אֹתְךָ שָׁם (Bereishis 45:11), I will provide for you there; וַיְכַלְכֵּל יוֹסֵף אֶת־אָבִיו וְאֶת־אֶחָיו (Bereishis 47:12), Yosef provided for his father and his brothers; and וְכִלְכְּלָם לֶחֶם וָמָיִם (Melachim I 18:4), he sustained them with bread and water. This is food supplied to each one's need by his own measure, and it does not leave the first sense but is taken in by it.

יְכַלְכֵּל דְּבָרָיו בְּמִשְׁפָּט (Tehillim 112:5), that he brings his words out with justice and uprightness and measure and does not multiply words; or דְּבָרָיו is his affairs, that he orders his outlays and his gifts by measure and by justice. From this root and this sense he takes וּלְכִילַי לֹא יֵאָמֵר שׁוֹעַ (Yeshayahu 32:5), the miser, as well.

נכל.sense: Cunning: the evil thought hidden away in the heart, and the deed done by guile that comes out of it.

more.t: וְאָרוּר נוֹכֵל (Malachi 1:14), cursed be the deceiver; the noun בְּנִכְלֵיהֶם (Bamidbar 25:18), by their wiles; וַיִּתְנַכְּלוּ אֹתוֹ לַהֲמִיתוֹ (Bereishis 37:18), they plotted against him to kill him; and לְהִתְנַכֵּל בַּעֲבָדָיו (Tehillim 105:25), to deal craftily with his servants.
The Targum of לְהָרְגוֹ בְעָרְמָה (Shemos 21:14), to kill him by guile, is לְמִקְטְלֵיהּ בִּנְכִילוּ, which puts this very root where the Hebrew has cunning.

קמץ.sense: To close the hand on something: to gather the fingers in to the palm and take a fistful, and so to gather in and heap up.

more.t: וְקָמַץ מִשָּׁם מְלֹא קֻמְצוֹ (Vayikra 2:2), he shall take from there his fistful. The sense is gathering and collecting, and מְלֹא קֻמְצוֹ is a full fist, the fingers gathered in to the palm of the hand.
Chazal describe it (Menachos 11a): he stretches three fingers over the flat of his hand, and wipes off with his thumb above and with his little finger below.

וַתַּעַשׂ הָאָרֶץ בְּשֶׁבַע שְׁנֵי הַשָּׂבָע לִקְמָצִים (Bereishis 41:47) means that the people of the land gathered the grain into heaps, so much produce did they gather in; or the earth itself is the one doing, that it put out much produce, handfuls from a single prutah.

גוי.sense: A nation; and in the way Chazal speak, a man who is not of Israel, where it is not known which nation he comes from.

more.h: A yud dropped from the writing
more.t: וְיֶתֶר גּוֹיִ יִנְחָלוּם (Tzefaniah 2:9), the remnant of my nation will inherit them, where the yud of the suffix is missing from the writing and stays in the speaking. So too גּוֹיֶךָ (Tehillim 106:5), your nation, גּוֹיַיִךְ (Yechezkel 36:13) and (Yechezkel 36:14), your nations, and גּוֹיֵי הָאֲרָצוֹת (Divrei HaYamim II 32:17), the nations of the lands.
He brings כִּי־גוֹי עָלָה עַל־אַרְצִי (Yoel 1:6), for a nation has come up against my land, said of a gathering of locusts.

more.h: Why a non-Jew is called a goy
more.t: Chazal were accustomed in their speech to call a man who is not of Israel a goy. The usage came about because whenever they wished to say of a man that he was not of Israel but of some other nation, and it was not settled with them which nation he came from, whether Edomite or Ishmaelite or one of the rest, they said goy, meaning that he is of another nation and not of Israel.

more.h: Whether one man is called a goy
more.t: Rabbi Yonah said that גּוֹי falls on a single man, from הֲגוֹי גַּם־צַדִּיק תַּהֲרֹג (Bereishis 20:4), will you kill a nation though it be righteous. Radak holds instead that Avimelech said it on account of his people, since the anger was on him and on his people, as he said כִּי־הֵבֵאתָ עָלַי וְעַל־מַמְלַכְתִּי חֲטָאָה גְדֹלָה (Bereishis 20:9), you have brought on me and on my kingdom a great sin; and at Bereishis 20:17 Avimelech, his wife and his maidservants were healed and bore children, which makes it plain that he was not stricken alone.

עמם.sense: To cover over and hide; and the noun עַם, a people, which is said of locusts, ants and other creatures that come in numbers.

more.t: אֲרָזִים לֹא־עֲמָמֻהוּ (Yechezkel 31:8), the tall cedars did not cover him or hide him, for he rose above them all; כָּל־סָתוּם לֹא עֲמָמוּךָ (Yechezkel 28:3), no hidden thing was covered or concealed from you; and אֵיכָה יוּעַם זָהָב (Eichah 4:1), how the gold is dimmed. His father reads עֲמָמוּךָ from עִם: the matters were not closed off with you.

more.h: A people, and the gender of the word
more.t: עַם רַב וְעָצוּם (Yoel 2:2), a great and mighty people. The word is mostly masculine and at times feminine: מַדּוּעַ שׁוֹבְבָה הָעָם הַזֶּה, why has this people turned away; וְחָטָאת עַמֶּךָ (Shemos 5:16), and your people has sinned; and הָעָם אֲשֶׁר־בְּקִרְבָּהּ יוֹשֶׁבֶת־לָבֶטַח (Shoftim 18:7), the people in her midst dwelling secure. He adds חֲבִי כִמְעַט־רֶגַע (Yeshayahu 26:20), hide yourself a moment, for whoever reads that as a command.

עַמִּים הַר־יִקְרָאוּ (Devarim 33:19), peoples will call to the mountain; in the fuller form בַּעֲמָמֶיךָ (Shoftim 5:14), among your peoples, and עַמְמֵי הָאָרֶץ (Nechemiah 9:24), the peoples of the land.

As עַם is said of a gathering and assembly of men, so it is said of other things: of the locust, עַם רַב וְעָצוּם כָּמֹהוּ לֹא נִהְיָה מִן־הָעוֹלָם (Yoel 2:2), a people great and mighty whose like has never been; of the ants, עַם לֹא־עָז (Mishlei 30:25), a people not strong; and of the shefanim, עַם לֹא־עָצוּם (Mishlei 30:26), a people not mighty. His father reads עַם־זוּ יָצַרְתִּי לִי תְּהִלָּתִי יְסַפֵּרוּ (Yeshayahu 43:21), this people I formed for myself, they will tell my praise, the same way, of the beasts, since the pasuk before it says that the beast of the field will honour him.

לאם.sense: A people, one body of men set beside another.

more.t: וּלְאֹם מִלְאֹם יֶאֱמָץ (Bereishis 25:23), one people will be stronger than the other, and וּשְׁנֵי לְאֻמִּים in the same pasuk, two peoples; תּוֹכֵחֹת בַּל־אֻמִּים (Tehillim 149:7), rebukes upon the peoples; and וּלְאוּמִּי אֵלַי הַאֲזִינוּ (Yeshayahu 51:4), my people, give ear to me, in which the quiescent letter, the vav, is written and carries the dagesh besides. He says he has set out the like of it in the section on grammar, and that these are as אוּמִים.

אם.sense: Mostly the particle אִם, if; on the same letters אֵם, a mother, אוּמָּה, a family or a nation, and אַמָּה, a cubit.

more.t: In most places it sets a condition, as וְאִם־עֵז קָרְבָּנוֹ (Vayikra 3:12), and if his offering is a goat. It also asks a question: הֲיִנְהַק־פֶּרֶא עֲלֵי־דֶשֶׁא אִם יִגְעֶה־שּׁוֹר (Iyov 6:5), does the wild donkey bray over grass, or the ox low over its fodder; and the heh of asking can come on it as well, הַאִם תַּמְנוּ לִגְוֹעַ (Bamidbar 17:28), have we done with dying?

וְהָיָה אִם־בָּא אֶל־אֵשֶׁת אָחִיו (Bereishis 38:9) is: when he came to his brother's wife. So too אִם־כֶּסֶף תַּלְוֶה אֶת־עַמִּי (Shemos 22:24), when you lend money to my people, since lending is an obligation, as it says וְהַעֲבֵט תַּעֲבִיטֶנּוּ (Devarim 15:8), you shall surely lend to him.

כִּי אִם־תַּם הַכֶּסֶף (Bereishis 47:18), truly the money is gone, and אִם־לַלֵּצִים הוּא יָלִיץ (Mishlei 3:34), truly he scoffs at the scoffers. Every אִם of this kind is to be read as truly, and he holds these are short of the nun of אָמֵן, as אֱמֶת is short a nun, its proper form being אֱמֶנֶת, which the dagesh in אֲמִתּוֹ proves.

אָב וָאֵם (Esther 2:6 in his edition), father and mother, is plain enough. A family is called אוּם or אוּמָּה, the plural רֹאשׁ אֻמּוֹת (Bamidbar 25:15), head of families, and שְׁנֵים־עָשָׂר נְשִׂיאִם לְאֻמֹּתָם (Bereishis 25:16), twelve princes for their families; and a whole nation is called אוּם, כָּל־הָאֻמִּים (Tehillim 117:1), all the nations. His father writes that the root of אוּם is אָמַם, on the evidence of the Arabic.

more.h: A mother of roads, a mother city
more.t: The middle of the road, where the roads turn to it from this side and that, is called אֵם הַדֶּרֶךְ (Yechezkel 21:26), the mother of the road, since it is like a mother to the roads that turn in to it; and the great city is עִיר וְאֵם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל (Shmuel II 20:19), a city and a mother in Israel, since it is like a mother to the smaller places, which are themselves called daughters.

וְהָאַמָּה מִזֶּה וְהָאַמָּה מִזֶּה (Shemos 26:13) is the cubit, and so בְּאַמַּת־אִישׁ (Devarim 3:11), by the cubit of a man. אַמַּת בִּצְעֵךְ (Yirmiyahu 51:13) is the arm of your gain, or the measure of your gain, the measure you measured out. In וַיָּנֻעוּ אַמּוֹת הַסִּפִּים (Yeshayahu 6:4) the doorposts are called אַמּוֹת, and Targum Yonasan renders them so; the Targum seems to take them as the corners standing on the doorposts on either side, on which the lintel rests. Others explain that the thresholds moved two or three cubits from their place.

מוט.sense: To totter, tilt and slip; and the noun מוֹט, the pole a load is carried on, with מוֹטָה the yoke or the strap it is tied with.

more.t: וּמָטָה יָדוֹ עִמָּךְ (Vayikra 25:35), his hand falters beside you; צַדִּיק מָט לִפְנֵי־רָשָׁע (Mishlei 25:26), a righteous man tottering before a wicked one; וּמָטִים לַהֶרֶג (Mishlei 24:11), those stumbling to the slaughter; and וְהַגְּבָעוֹת תְּמוּטֶינָה (Yeshayahu 54:10), the hills will give way. The sense of them all is tilting and losing one's footing.

לֹא־יִתֵּן לְעוֹלָם מוֹט לַצַּדִּיק (Tehillim 55:23), he will never let the righteous be shaken; אַל־יִתֵּן לַמּוֹט רַגְלֶךָ (Tehillim 121:3), he will not let your foot slip; and וַיְחַזְּקֵהוּ בְמַסְמְרִים לֹא יִמּוֹט (Yeshayahu 41:7), fastened with nails so that it will not totter.

Near this sense: וַיִּשָּׂאֻהוּ בַמּוֹט (Bamidbar 13:23), they carried it on a pole; וְנָתְנוּ עַל־הַמּוֹט (Bamidbar 4:10), they put it on the pole; and אֶשְׁבֹּר מֹטֵהוּ (Nachum 1:13), I will break his bar. The plural is בִּכְתֵפָם בַּמֹּטוֹת (Divrei HaYamim I 15:15), on their shoulder with the poles, and מוֹטֹת עֵץ שָׁבָרְתָּ (Yirmiyahu 28:13), bars of wood you have broken.

more.h: The yoke, and a masculine verb
more.t: וַיִּקַּח חֲנַנְיָה הַנָּבִיא אֶת־הַמּוֹטָה מֵעַל צַוַּאר יִרְמְיָה הַנָּבִיא וַיִּשְׁבְּרֵהוּ (Yirmiyahu 28:12 in his edition), Chananyah the navi took the bar off the neck of Yirmiyahu the navi and broke it. Though מוֹטָה is feminine the pasuk says וַיִּשְׁבְּרֵהוּ in the masculine, against the עֹל, the yoke, for the מוֹטָה is the yoke; or else the מוֹטָה is the strap by which the yoke is tied on.

מֻטּוֹת כְּנָפָיו (Yeshayahu 8:8) he keeps here, the quiescent letter swallowed in a dagesh and the cholam turned into a shuruk, its sense being bonds or staves of wood. His father puts the phrase at the root נטה, the dagesh standing for a swallowed nun, and reads it as the spreading of his camp, which will fill the breadth of your land. The Midrash of Rabbi Tanchuma asks how great the מֻטּוֹת of a rooster's wings are, and answers a sixtieth of its wings, a sixtieth of Sancheriv's hosts, the full breadth of the land of Yehudah.

בדד.sense: Alone, by itself; a noun of solitariness rather than an adjective, and it carries with it the sense of dwelling secure.

more.h: Not an adjective but a noun
more.t: בָּדָד יֵשֵׁב (Vayikra 13:46), he shall dwell alone, on his own. The word serves the feminine and the plural too, אֵיכָה יָשְׁבָה בָדָד (Eichah 1:1), how she sat alone, and בָּדָד יִשְׁכֹּנוּ (Yirmiyahu 49:31), they dwell alone; and it takes a serving lamed in the way of a noun, שֹׁכְנִי לְבָדָד (Michah 7:14), dwelling alone. For that reason he says it is not an adjective but the noun of being alone.

It comes in the sense of בֶּטַח, security, since one who dwells secure sits alone and has no need of many men about him to help: וַיִּשְׁכֹּן יִשְׂרָאֵל בֶּטַח בָּדָד (Devarim 33:28), Israel dwelt secure and alone, and בָּדָד יַנְחֶנּוּ (Devarim 32:12), Hashem alone led him.

בַּד בְּבַד (Shemos 30:34) he reads as one by one, that each of the spices be ground by itself. Some explain it as weight by weight, and so Onkelos rendered it: each weighed on its own for exactness, or that the weight of one be like the weight of another, since among them were spices of equal weight, the ones named in the Torah. Chazal too say (Kereisos 6a) that the tzori and the tziporen, the levonah and the chelbenah, are seventy manah in weight each.

Most who use the noun use it with a lamed: מִשְׁפַּחַת בֵּית־דָּוִיד לְבָד וּנְשֵׁיהֶם לְבָד (Zecharyah 12:12), the family of Beis David apart and their wives apart, pointed with a kamatz, and in construct with a patach, לְבַד מִשָּׂרֵי הַנִּצָּבִים (Melachim I 5:30), apart from the appointed officers. A mem is added on top of that, מִלְּבַד נְשֵׁי בְנֵי־יַעֲקֹב (Bereishis 46:26), apart from the wives of Yaakov's sons; and with suffixes the letter doubles, וַיִּוָּתֵר יַעֲקֹב לְבַדּוֹ (Bereishis 32:24), Yaakov was left alone, and אֵין עוֹד מִלְּבַדּוֹ (Devarim 4:35), there is none besides him.

The verb from it is וְאֵין בּוֹדֵד בְּמוֹעָדָיו (Yeshayahu 14:31), no man keeping to himself at the appointed times: at the times set for the army to muster, not one of them holds apart or stays back, for all come out together. Targum Yonasan renders it that none delays at his times.

He weighs three readings of that pasuk. It may be Nevuchadnetzar, since the smoke comes from the north, and Bavel lies north of Pelishtim as it does of Eretz Yisrael, and in that destruction Israel was saved from the Pelishtim who pressed them. It may be Pharaoh, who struck the Pelishtim, as it says בְּטֶרֶם יַכֶּה פַרְעֹה אֶת־עַזָּה (Yirmiyahu 47:1), before Pharaoh struck Gaza. But for the parsha as a whole he holds it better read of Chizkiyahu, who struck the Pelishtim as far as Gaza (Melachim II 18:8): the rod that was broken is Uziyahu, who had struck the Pelishtim (Divrei HaYamim II 26:6), and from his seed came the one who would strike them now.
פֶּרֶא בּוֹדֵד לוֹ (Hoshea 8:9), a wild donkey off by itself, and כְּצִפּוֹר בּוֹדֵד עַל־גָּג (Tehillim 102:8), like a lone bird on a roof, both of them meaning solitary.

נסס.sense: The נֵס, the banner carried high for a whole army to see and follow; the root's core is height and being raised, and a sail is a נֵס too.

more.t: וְנָשָׂא־נֵס לַגּוֹיִם (Yeshayahu 5:27 in his edition), he will raise a banner to the nations, and Hashem is called נִסִּי (Shemos 17:15). The root is height and being lifted up, since the man bearing the banner carries it high, so that it is seen over the whole army and they march after it.

כִּמְסֹס נֹסֵס (Yeshayahu 10:18) he reads as: when the bearer of the banner melts away, the whole army melts and flees. Rabbi Yehudah wrote that the phrase has another sense, and Rabbi Yonah put it under another root and another sense.

נֹסְסָה בוֹ (Yeshayahu 59:19), that the spirit of Hashem was raised against him to drive him back; נָתַתָּה לִּירֵאֶיךָ נֵּס לְהִתְנוֹסֵס (Tehillim 60:6), a banner given to those who fear you, which he glosses as to be raised and lifted up; and כִּי אַבְנֵי־נֵזֶר מִתְנוֹסְסוֹת עַל־אַדְמָתוֹ (Zecharyah 9:16), crown stones held high on his land.

The sail is called נֵס as well, since they raise it on the mast: בַּל־פָּרְשׂוּ נֵס (Yeshayahu 33:23), they did not spread a sail, and וְכַנֵּס עַל־הַגִּבְעָה (Yeshayahu 30:17), like a banner on the hill.

תרן.sense: The mast, the tall timber on a ship by which the sail is let down and set up.

more.t: כַּתֹּרֶן עַל־רֹאשׁ הָהָר (Yeshayahu 30:17), like a mast on a mountain top; לַעֲשׂוֹת תֹּרֶן עָלָיִךְ (Yechezkel 27:5), to make a mast for you; and בַּל־יְחַזְּקוּ כֵן־תָּרְנָם (Yeshayahu 33:23), they did not hold the base of their mast firm. He closes with the foreign word for it.

עתד.sense: Ready and prepared, and what is made ready or laid up for someone; and the noun עַתּוּד, the full grown he-goat.

more.t: כְּמֶלֶךְ עָתִיד לַכִּידוֹר (Iyov 15:24), like a king made ready for the onslaught, and עֲתִידִים (Esther 8:13), the Jews being prepared; הָעֲתִידִים עֹרֵר לִוְיָתָן (Iyov 3:8), those who are ready to rouse their mourning. Of what is laid up to come: וְחָשׁ עֲתִדֹת לָמוֹ (Devarim 32:35), what is prepared to come upon them of the punishment.

עֲתוּדוֹתֵיהֶם (Yeshayahu 10:13) is what is stored up for them of treasure and things desired; or it is their borders, since he says in that same pasuk that he removed the bounds of peoples, a border and a set time being near to one another in sense.

וְעַתְּדָהּ בַּשָּׂדֶה לָךְ (Mishlei 24:27), where the heh with a mapik points back to the work just named: understand and make ready your work in the field, and afterwards build your house. And הִתְעַתְּדוּ לְגַלִּים (Iyov 15:28), houses ready to be left desolate and become heaps.

הָעֲתֻדִים הָעֹלִים עַל־הַצֹּאן (Bereishis 31:10), which he says is known: they are the males of the goats, called תְּיָשִׁים as well, the grown ones called עַתּוּדִים and תְּיָשִׁים and the young ones שְׂעִירִים.

The nobles and the great men are called by this word by way of borrowing: כָּל־עַתּוּדֵי אָרֶץ (Yeshayahu 14:9), all the he-goats of the earth, since they go before the people and lead them as the he-goats go before the flock.

מצר.sense: The narrow place a man is hemmed into, and in the words of Chazal the boundary line of a field; he weighs whether the mem belongs to the root.

more.t: כָּל־רֹדְפֶיהָ הִשִּׂיגוּהָ בֵּין הַמְּצָרִֽים (Eichah 1:3), all her pursuers overtook her between the straits, he reads as between the fences, a fence on this side and a fence on that, so that she cannot flee one way or the other. Close by it is וּמְצָרֵי שְׁאוֹל מְצָאוּנִי (Tehillim 116:3), the straits of the grave found me.

The single form of them may be מִן־ הַמֵּצַֽר (Tehillim 118:5), out of the strait, so that מֵצַר gives מְצָרִים as עֵנָב gives עֲנָבִים, except that this one doubles its middle letter. Or it may belong to another root, יָצַר or צָרַר, as he wrote at the root יָצַר; and וּמְצָרֵי שְׁאוֹל מְצָאוּנִי stands in the pattern of מְמַדֵּי, from מִי־שָׂם מְמַדֶּיהָ (Iyov 38:5), who set its measures, which would make the root צָרַר.

Chazal use the word of a boundary line (Bava Basra 26b), אילן הסמוך למצר, a tree standing close to the boundary, and מצרים הרחיב לו (Bava Basra 61b), he has widened its bounds for him. It seems to him that they hold the mem to be a letter of the root, since they say (Bava Basra 62a) מצר לו מצר ראובן מצר אחד, he set him a boundary, Reuven's boundary, as one of them.

רהב.sense: To be strong and haughty: insolence toward an elder, the strength called Rahav, which is Egypt, and putting courage into a man.

more.t: יִרְֽהֲבוּ הַנַּעַר בַּזָּקֵן (Yeshayahu 3:5), the youth will be insolent against the elder, he glosses as their growing strong and haughty. The plain form is וְרָהְבָּם עָמָל וָאָוֶן (Tehillim 90:10), and their strength is toil and trouble, which stands in the pattern of בְּשָׁמְרָם עֵקֶב רָֽב (Tehillim 19:12), in keeping them there is great reward; or else it is a noun.

לֵךְ הִתְרַפֵּס וּרְהַב רֵעֶֽיךָ (Mishlei 6:3), go, humble yourself and press your fellow, he reads as: bow before him and strengthen him with words of appeasement. Although רעיך is written with a yud and the Mesorah marks it the only one written full, the yud is either added or the word is from a root whose last letter is a heh, the yud being of the root. It can also be read as a plural with a bet missing, ברעיך, that you should set many friends upon him.

רַהַב הֵם שָֽׁבֶת (Yeshayahu 30:4 in his edition), Rahav, they are idleness, he glosses החוזק שלהם ישבת ויבטל, their strength will cease and come to nothing, and says it of Egypt, since Rahav is their strength; he gave the word another reading at the root יָשַׁב. אַזְכִּיר רַהַב וּבָבֶל (Tehillim 87:4), I will make mention of Rahav and Bavel, is Egypt too, called so because the Egyptians were possessed of strength and pride.

הַמַּחְצֶבֶת רַהַב (Yeshayahu 51:9), that hewed Rahav, and מָחַץ רָֽהַב (Iyov 26:12), he smote Rahav, are all of strength and force. וְרָהְבָּם עָמָל וָאָוֶן (Tehillim 90:10) he takes as: their vigor is emptiness, since it soon passes away. And וְֽלֹֽא־פָנָה אֶל־ רְהָבִים, and he has not turned to the rehavim, is to those who have strength and pride; the address printed beside it carries no book.

more.h: Chayuj on a word in Yeshayahu
more.t: Radak wonders at what he found in the book of pointing of Rabbi Yehudah Chayuj, who wrote וּפָחַד וְרָחַב לְבָבֵךְ (Yeshayahu 60:5), your heart shall throb and swell, with a heh, and said that the resh is kamatz and the heh patach, so as to keep it apart from רַהַב, which is patach throughout. Radak answers that we have received the reading וְרָחַב with a ches, and that Rabbi Yonah wrote it with a ches as well.

תַּרְהִבֵנִי בְנַפְשִׁי עֹֽז (Tehillim 138:3), you made me bold with strength in my soul, he glosses החזקני, strengthen me, that you put might into my soul to be strong for your service. שֶׁהֵם הִרְהִיבֻנִי (Shir HaShirim 6:5), for they have overcome me, is חזקו חשקי ואמצוני עליו, they strengthened my desire and made me bold over it.

כפתר.sense: The kaftor: the knob on the menorah, which he takes for an apple, and the lintel over a doorway, named for the flowers and knobs carved on it.

more.t: וְכַפְתֹּר תַּחַת שְׁנֵי הַקָּנִים (Shemos 25:35), a kaftor under two of the branches, and כַּפְתֹּֽרֵיהֶם וּקְנֹתָם (Shemos 25:36), their kaftorim and their branches, he explains as apples, since they were like apples bulging out of the body of the menorah.

הַךְ הַכַּפְתּוֹר וְיִרְֽעֲשׁוּ הַסִּפִּים (Amos 9:1), strike the kaftor so that the thresholds shake: the kaftor is the lintel resting on the two ספים, which are the doorposts. It carries that name because carvings of flowers and knobs are made on it. So too בְּכַפְתֹּרֶיהָ יָלִינוּ (Tzefaniah 2:14), they will lodge in its kaftorim, on which the Targum has בְּפִתּוּחַ תַּרְעַיָא, in the carved work of the gates.

אלל.sense: A thing of no use and no help, which is what an idol is; and by another pointing the same letters are a cry of woe.

more.t: רֹפְאֵי אֱלִל כֻּלְּכֶֽם (Iyov 13:4), you are all worthless healers; רֹעִי הָֽאֱלִיל (Zechariah 11:17), the worthless shepherd; וְקֶסֶם (Yirmiyahu 14:14), and divination, set beside this word; אַל־תִּפְנוּ אֶל־ הָאֱלִילִם (Vayikra 19:4), do not turn to the elilim. Their sense is emptiness and a thing that brings no benefit, and he gives the Old French word for it.

אִם־רָשַׁעְתִּי אַלְלַי לִי (Iyov 10:15), if I am wicked, woe to me, is accented on the last syllable, and accented on the one before it is אַלְלַי לִי כִּי הָיִיתִי כְּאָסְפֵּי־קַיִץ (Michah 7:1), woe to me, for I am like the gatherings of the summer fruit. The sense of both is אבוי, alas.
His brother Rabbi Moshe wrote that the alef stands in place of a yud, as יִשַׁי is also אִישַׁי, and that the word is from יְלָלָה, wailing, the yud being the one a man uses of himself.

תרף.sense: Terafim: images through which people looked to be shown what was coming, set against the eifod as idolatry is set against the service of Hashem.

more.h: Images that show what is coming
more.t: לָֽקְחָה אֶת־ הַתְּרָפִים (Bereishis 31:34), she had taken the terafim; וַתִּקַּח מִיכַל אֶת־ הַתְּרָפִים (Shmuel I 19:13), Michal took the terafim; וְאֵין אֵפוֹד וּתְרָפִֽים (Hoshea 3:4), and no eifod and terafim. They are images through which future things are seen.

He reads וְאֵין אֵפוֹד וּתְרָפִֽים along with וְאֵין זֶבַח וְאֵין מַצֵּבָה (Hoshea 3:4), and no sacrifice and no pillar: the sacrifice is to Hashem and the pillar to idolatry, and so the eifod is to Hashem and the terafim to idolatry.
Targum Yonasan rendered the phrase וְלֵית אֵפוֹד וּמְחַוֵי, there is no eifod and none who declares, and the other terafim he rendered צַלְמָנַיָא, images.

שׁקץ.sense: To hold a thing in abomination, and the abomination itself: the detestable things of idolatry, and what a man must not eat.

more.t: כִּי לֹֽא־בָזָה וְלֹא שִׁקַּץ (Tehillim 22:25), for he has not despised nor abhorred; אַל־ תְּשַׁקְּצוּ אֶת־נַפְשֹׁתֵיכֶם (Vayikra 11:43), do not make yourselves abominable; וְאֶת־נִבְלָתָם תְּשַׁקֵּֽצוּ (Vayikra 11:11), and their carcass you shall hold in abomination; שַׁקֵּץ תְּשַׁקְּצֶנּוּ (Devarim 7:26), you shall utterly abhor it.

The noun is וְלָתֵת שִׁקּוּץ שֹׁמֵם (Daniel 12:11), to set up the detestable thing that appalls, and in the plural וְעַל כְּנַף שִׁקּוּצִים מְשֹׁמֵם (Daniel 9:27), and upon the wing of detestable things one who appalls; וַתִּרְאוּ אֶת־ שִׁקּוּצֵיהֶם (Devarim 29:16), and you saw their detestable things; אִישׁ שִׁקּוּצֵי עֵינָיו הַשְׁלִיכוּ (Yechezkel 20:7), let each man cast away the detestable things of his eyes.
שֶׁקֶץ הוּא לָכֶֽם (Vayikra 11:12), it is a sheketz to you, stands in another form, which he marks as pointed with six dots. The sense of them all is abomination.

חמם.sense: Heat and growing warm: the sun that grows hot, hot bread, the heat of the day; from this the sun itself is called חַמָּה.

more.t: וְחַם הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ וְנָמָֽס (Shemos 16:21), when the sun grew hot it melted; אִם־יִשְׁכְּבוּ שְׁנַיִם וְחַם לָהֶם (Koheles 4:11), if two lie together they are warm, which he reads as their flesh being warm to them; חַמּוֹתִי רָאִיתִי אֽוּר (Yeshayahu 44:16), I have warmed myself, I have seen the fire; אַף־ יָחֹם וְיֹאמַר הֶאָח (Yeshayahu 44:16), he even grows warm and says aha. In וַיִּקַּח מֵהֶם וַיָּחָם, he takes of them and warms himself, he marks the ches with a kamatz chatuf, since the zakef stands on the yud.

The plain word in its full form is וְשֹׁרֶשׁ רְתָמִים לַחְמָֽם (Iyov 30:4), the root of the broom shrub for their warming, and אֵין־גַּחֶלֶת לַחְמָם (Yeshayahu 47:14), not a coal to warm at, in the pattern of לִשְׁכַּב אֶת־בַּֽת־יַֽעֲקֹב (Bereishis 34:7), to lie with the daughter of Yaakov.

more.h: Hot as a word of description
more.t: חַם ־לִבִּי בְּקִרְבִּי (Tehillim 39:4), my heart was hot within me, may be a verb of what has happened, since it takes a patach, while זֶה לַחְמֵנוּ חָם (Yehoshua 9:12), this bread of ours was hot, is a word of description, since it takes a kamatz; the Mesorah notes on it that it is the only one so pointed, and that a man's name of that sort is like it. In the plural, אֲשֶׁר־בְּגָדֶיךָ חַמִּים (Iyov 37:17), when your garments are warm.

לָשׂוּם לֶחֶם חֹם (Shmuel I 21:7), to set out hot bread, is another form of the word, in the pattern of מָעוֹז לַתֹּם (Mishlei 10:29), a stronghold to the upright, and הַמַּבְלִיג שֹׁד עַל־ עָז (Amos 5:9), who brings ruin upon the strong.

The noun is heat: זֶרַע וְקָצִיר וְקֹר וָחֹם (Bereishis 8:22), seedtime and harvest, cold and heat; לָבוֹשׁ וְאֵֽין־ לְחֹם לוֹ (Chaggai 1:6), dressed, and no one is warm; בְּחֻמּוֹ נִדְֽעֲכוּ מִמְּקוֹמָֽם (Iyov 6:17), in its heat they are gone from their place.

He holds it likely that וְכָל־שֶֽׂה־ חוּם (Bereishis 30:32), and every dark lamb, belongs to this root, its sense being black, since blackness comes of heat, with a shuruk standing in place of a cholam.

אֵיךְ יֵחָֽם (Koheles 4:11), how shall one be warm; כֻּלָּם יֵחַמּוּ (Hoshea 7:7), they are all heated; הַנֵּֽחָמִים בָּֽאֵלִים (Yeshayahu 57:5), you that heat yourselves among the terebinths, in the pattern of בַּמְּאֵרָה אַתֶּם נֵֽאָרִים (Malachi 3:9), you are cursed with a curse; or else they are from the root יָחַם.

וְֽעַל־עָפָר תְּחַמֵּֽם (Iyov 39:14), and she warms them on the dust, he reads of her warming her eggs; and the form that turns the act back on the doer is וּמִגֵּז כְּבָשַׂי יִתְחַמָּֽם (Iyov 31:20), he warms himself with the fleece of my sheep.

From this sense the sun is called חַמָּה: בָּרָה כַּֽחַמָּה (Shir HaShirim 6:10), clear as the sun, and כְּאוֹר הַֽחַמָּה (Yeshayahu 30:26), like the light of the sun. But וְאֵין נִסְתָּר מֵֽחַמָּתֽוֹ (Tehillim 19:6 in his edition), and nothing is hidden from its heat, is the noun of the heat itself. He holds that וְהִכְרַתִּי אֶת־ חַמָּנֵיכֶם (Vayikra 26:30), and I will cut down your chamanim, may be of this root and this sense, the nun being added, and that they were called so because sun worshippers made them.

אים.sense: Dread: the noun for terror, the Eimim who are the giants, and the graven images called by the same word in contempt.

more.t: אָיֹם וְנוֹרָא (Chavakuk 1:7), dreadful and fearsome, and אֲיֻמָּה כַּנִּדְגָּלֽוֹת (Shir HaShirim 6:10), terrible as an army with banners.

וְהִנֵּה אֵימָה (Bereishis 15:12), and behold, a dread; in construct אֵימַת מֶלֶךְ (Mishlei 20:2), the dread of a king; in the plural of the feminine וְאֵימוֹת מָוֶת (Tehillim 55:5), the terrors of death. In אֵימָתָה וָפַחַד (Shemos 15:15), dread and fear, the mark of the feminine is doubled, as it is doubled in יְשׁוּעָתָה (Tehillim 3:3), salvation.

In the plural of the masculine: יַֽהֲלֹךְ עָלָיו אֵמִֽים (Iyov 20:25), terrors go over him; נָשָׂאתִי אֵמֶיךָ (Tehillim 88:16), I have borne your terrors. הָֽאֵמִים לְפָנִים (Devarim 2:10), the Eimim of old, are the giants, called so because dread and fear fall upon those who see them.

וּבָֽאֵימִים יִתְהֹלָֽלוּ (Yirmiyahu 50:38), and they are mad over their eimim, are the graven images, and he called them eimim as a name of contempt, like עצבים, or else because those who pass by them are afraid of them. The sense of them all is fear and dread.

פחד.sense: Fear and trembling; the Fear of Yitzchak is the One whom Yitzchak feared, and in one place the word is of a limb of the body.

more.t: וּפָחַד וְרָחַב לְבָבֵךְ (Yeshayahu 60:5), your heart shall tremble and swell; פָּֽחֲדוּ בְצִיּוֹן חַטָּאִים (Yeshayahu 33:14), sinners in Tzion are afraid; שָׁם פָּֽחֲדוּ פָחַד (Tehillim 14:5), there they were in great fear.

more.h: Fear that turns a man toward Hashem
more.t: וּפָֽחֲדוּ (Hoshea 3:5), and they shall fear, said of turning to Hashem וְאֶל־טוּבוֹ, and to his goodness, he glosses as their fearing him and streaming to him and to his good. In the same way he takes וּפָֽחֲדוּ וְרָֽגְזוּ עַל כָּל־הַטּוֹבָה וְעַל כָּל־הַשָּׁלוֹם, and they shall fear and tremble over all the good and all the peace.

פָּֽחֲדוּ־ פַחַד (Tehillim 53:6), they feared a fear, he reads as: there was no fear like it. The plural is קֽוֹל־ פְּחָדִים בְּאָזְנָיו (Iyov 15:21), a sound of terrors in his ears, and with a feminine heh, וְלֹא פַחְדָּתִי אֵלַיִךְ (Yirmiyahu 2:19), and my fear was not upon you.

וּפַחַד יִצְחָק הָיָה לִי (Bereishis 31:42), and the Fear of Yitzchak was with me, is: the One whom Yitzchak fears was with me; and so וַיִּשָּׁבַע יַֽעֲקֹב בְּפַחַד אָבִיו יִצְחָֽק (Bereishis 31:53), Yaakov swore by the Fear of his father Yitzchak, by the One whom Yitzchak fears. He says the matter is put in Yitzchak's name because Yitzchak feared Hashem and gave himself over in the matter of the akeidah.

אַשְׁרֵי אָדָם מְפַחֵד תָּמִיד (Mishlei 28:14), happy is the man who is always afraid, and וַתְּפַחֵד תָּמִיד כָּל־הַיּוֹם מִפְּנֵי חֲמַת הַמֵּצִיק (Yeshayahu 51:13), and you are afraid all the day because of the fury of the oppressor, stand in the heavier form; and the form that puts fear into another is וְרֹב עַצְמוֹתַי הִפְחִֽיד (Iyov 4:14), and it terrified the mass of my bones.
פַֽחֲדָיו יְשׂרָֽגוּ (Iyov 40:17), his pachadav are knit together, is a sense apart, and the word there is of the testicles. The Targum of מְרוֹחַ אָֽשֶׁךְ (Vayikra 21:20) is מְרִיס פַּחְדִּין.

ירא.sense: To fear, of Hashem and of a man; the nouns for fear and awe, what is awesome, and the form that puts fear into somebody else.

more.t: וְלֹא יָרֵא אֱלֹהִֽים (Devarim 25:18), and he did not fear Hashem; כִּֽי־ יָֽרְאוּ הַֽמְיַלְּדֹת אֶת־הָֽאֱלֹהִים (Shemos 1:21), because the midwives feared Hashem; לֹא צָחַקְתִּי כִּי יָרֵאָה (Bereishis 18:15), I did not laugh, for she was afraid; סָמוּךְ לִבּוֹ לֹא יִירָא (Tehillim 112:8), his heart is steady, he will not fear; וָֽאִירָא כִּֽי־עֵירֹם אָנֹכִי וָאֵֽחָבֵֽא (Bereishis 3:10), and I was afraid because I was naked, and I hid; וַיִּֽירְאוּ מִגֶּשֶׁת אֵלָֽיו (Shemos 34:30), and they were afraid to come near him; וַיֹּאסֶף שָׁאוּל לֵרֹא מִפְּנֵי דָוִד (Shmuel I 18:29), and Shaul feared David still more.

לְמַעַן יְרָאתֶם (Yehoshua 4:24), so that you may fear, has a kamatz under the resh, and he notes that there is none like it. אַךְ יְראוּ (Shmuel I 12:24), only fear, ought by rule to be יִרְאוּ, but the alef is left at rest so that the word should not look like יִרְאוּ from רָאָה, to see. תִּֽרְאוּ חֲתַת וַתִּירָֽאוּ (Iyov 6:21), you see a terror and are afraid, are both written with a yud and belong to this root and this sense.

The word of description is אַשְׁרֵי־ אִישׁ יָרֵא (Tehillim 112:1), happy is the man who fears; and in construct אַשְׁרֵי כָּל־ יְרֵא (Tehillim 128:1), happy is every one who fears, יִרְאֵי (Tehillim 22:24), those who fear, and אִשָּׁה יִֽרְאַת (Mishlei 31:30), a woman who fears.

more.h: Awe, and the place of it
more.t: יֹבִילוּ שַׁי לַמּוֹרָֽא (Tehillim 76:12), they bring a gift to the awe, he takes of the Beis HaMikdash, which is the place of awe, or else as a word said of Hashem himself, as וְהוּא מוֹרַֽאֲכֶם (Yeshayahu 8:13), and he is your fear. So וְאֶת־ מֽוֹרָאוֹ לֹֽא־ תִֽירְאוּ וְלֹא תַֽעֲרִֽיצוּ (Yeshayahu 8:12), and do not fear what it fears nor be in dread of it; וּמוֹרַֽאֲכֶם וְחִתְּכֶם יִֽהְיֶה (Bereishis 9:2), and the fear of you and the dread of you shall be; מוֹרָה לָהֶם (Tehillim 9:21), set fear upon them, where the heh stands in place of an alef.

וְיִרְאָה לָהֶם (Yechezkel 1:18), and they had awe; רֵאשִׁית דָּעַת (Mishlei 1:7), in the pasuk that fear of Hashem is the beginning of knowledge; וּבַֽעֲבוּר תִּהְיֶה יִרְאָתוֹ (Shemos 20:20), and so that his fear may be upon you.

נוֹרָא מְאֹד (Shoftim 13:6), very awesome; נוֹרָאוֹת בְּצֶדֶק תַּֽעֲנֵנוּ (Tehillim 65:6), by awesome things in righteousness you answer us; לְמַעַן תִּוָּרֵֽא (Tehillim 130:4), so that you may be feared.

more.h: Why forgiveness is with Hashem alone
more.t: His father explains לְמַעַן תִּוָּרֵֽא so: Hashem gave the beings above power to do his will in the earth, but forgiveness is not with them, only with him. Why? So that men should not say in their hearts that if we sin the angels will be appeased for us and will bear our sins; he comes to make known that forgiveness is not in them, so that men should fear Hashem, since forgiveness is with him and with no other. The chacham Rabbi Avraham Ibn Ezra explained that if you do not forgive, sinners will not fear you and will do whatever their soul desires.

more.h: Rabbi Yonah on a distant people
more.t: וּמֵעַם נוָֹרא (Yeshayahu 18:7), from a people feared, and מֵאֶרֶץ נֽוֹרָאָֽה (Yeshayahu 21:1), from a fearsome land, Rabbi Yonah explained as far off, the one and the other. Radak holds they should not be taken out of their own sense, even though the plain reading of the pasuk speaks of a distant people and a distant land, since a man always fears those far from him, whose ways and whose might he does not know, more than those near him, whose ways and might he does know, and the distant ones seem in his eyes mightier and stronger.

כִּי יֵֽרְאֻנִי הָעָם (Shmuel II 14:15), for the people made me afraid, stands in the pattern of גֵּֽרְשׁוּנִי, and he glosses it הפחידוני, they frightened me. So אֲשֶׁר הָיוּ מְיָֽרְאִים אוֹתִֽי (Nechemiah 6:14), who were making me afraid; אִגְּרוֹת שָׁלַח טֽוֹבִיָּה לְיָֽרְאֵנִי (Nechemiah 6:19), Toviah sent letters to make me afraid; לְיָֽרְאָם וּלְבַֽהֲלָם (Divrei HaYamim II 32:18), to make them afraid and to terrify them.

דאג.sense: Worry: the fear and the grief a man carries over what is still to come.

more.t: וְדָאַג לָֽנוּ (Shmuel I 9:5), and he will be anxious for us; עֲוֹנִי אַגִּיד אֶדְאַג מֵֽחַטָּאתִֽי (Tehillim 38:19), I declare my sin, I am anxious over my transgression; וְהָֽרָעָב אֲשֶׁר־אַתֶּם דֹּֽאֲגִים מִמֶּנּוּ (Yirmiyahu 42:16), and the famine that you are anxious about; אֲנִי דֹאֵג אֶת־הַיְּהוּדִים (Yirmiyahu 38:19), I am anxious about the Yehudim; וְאֶת־מִי דָּאַגְתְּ וַתִּֽירְאִי (Yeshayahu 57:11), and of whom were you anxious and afraid.
וּבִשְׁנַת בַּצֹּרֶת לֹ֣א יִדְאָ֔ג (Yirmiyahu 17:8), and in a year of drought it will not be anxious, takes a kamatz with the zakef, and he marks it as said by way of a borrowed usage.
וְאִם־לֹא מִדְּאָגָה (Yehoshua 22:24), and if it was not out of anxiety. The sense of them all is the fear and the grief over what is to come.

קמח.sense: Flour; he notes that it is named for what it will become, since what a man grinds is not yet flour.

more.t: קֶמַח שְׂעֹרִים (Bamidbar 5:15), barley flour, with a segol, and וַתִּקַּח־ קֶמַח וַתָּלָשׁ (Shmuel I 28:24), and she took flour and kneaded it.

קְחִי רֵחַיִם וְטַֽחֲנִי קָמַח (Yeshayahu 47:2), take millstones and grind flour, he explains as a thing named for its end, since a man does not grind flour. So too אָפִיתִי עַל־גֶּחָלָיו לֶחֶם (Yeshayahu 44:19), I baked bread on its coals, since it is not bread until it has been baked, and others besides these, as he wrote at the root אָפָה. And so בְּלִי יַֽעֲשֶׂה־ קֶּמַח (Hoshea 8:7), it shall yield no flour, which he wrote at the root לָחַם.

סלת.sense: Solet, which he takes for the flour of a coarse grinding, the part a sieve holds back.

more.h: The flour of a coarse grinding
more.t: סֹלֶת חִטִּים (Shemos 29:2), solet of wheat, and מִסָּלְתָּהּ וּמִשַּׁמְנָהּ (Vayikra 2:2), of its solet and of its oil: it is the flour ground with a coarse grinding. So the Mishnah has it (Avos 5:15), נפה שהיא מוציאה את הקמח וקולטת את הסולת, a sieve that lets the flour out and holds back the solet.

גרשֹ.sense: Grain crushed to groats, גֶּרֶשׂ כַּרְמֶל (Vayikra 2:14), the groats of fresh grain, which he marks as pointed with six dots and explains at the root גרס.

גרשׁ.sense: To drive out and to cast up: a man driven from his place, a wife sent away from her husband, and the open land outside a city.

more.t: הִנְנִי גֹרֵשׁ מִפָּנֶיךָ (Shemos 34:11), behold, I drive out before you; וְאִשָּׁה גְּרוּשָׁה מֵֽאִישָׁהּ (Vayikra 21:7), and a woman put away from her husband; גָּרֵשׁ הָֽאָמָה הַזֹּאת (Bereishis 21:10), drive out this maidservant; and with no doer named, כִּי־ גֹֽרְשׁוּ מִמִּצְרַיִם (Shemos 12:39), for they were driven out of Egypt.

הָרִימוּ גְרֻשֹֽׁתֵיכֶם מֵעַל עַמִּי (Yechezkel 45:9), take away your exactions from my people, he reads as the taxes you heap and cast upon them, lift them off them. Targum Yonasan rendered סְלִיקוּ תִקְלַתְכוֹן מִגוֹ עַמִי, remove your burden from among my people.

more.h: The sea that casts up mire
more.t: וַיִּגְרְשׁוּ מֵימָיו רֶפֶשׁ וָטִֽיט (Yeshayahu 57:20), its waters cast up mire and mud, and כַּיָּם נִגְרָשׁ (Yeshayahu 57:20), like the tossing sea, which he reads as a sea shaking with its waves, and they go out to the shore. So נִגְרַשְׁתִּי מִנֶּגֶד עֵינֶיךָ (Yonah 2:5), I am driven out from before your eyes, and וְנִגְרְשָׁה (Amos 8:8), it heaves up, וְנִשְׁקְעָה כִּיאוֹר מִצְרָֽיִם, and sinks like the river of Egypt.

more.h: The moons that drive the fruit out
more.t: גֶּרֶשׁ יְרָחִֽים (Devarim 33:14), the yield of the moons, he marks as pointed with six dots, and reads as the season when the fruits bud and blossom with force, as though the moon were driving them outward.

more.h: The open land outside a city
more.t: With a mem added: לְמַעַן מִגְרָשָׁהּ לָבַֽז (Yechezkel 36:5), that its open land might be for spoil, which he takes as a noun standing in place of the plain form of the verb, as if it said למען גרוש אותה לבז, in order to drive it out for spoil. The word also names the open ground outside a city, וּמִגְרָשׁ לֶֽעָרִים (Bamidbar 35:2), and open land for the cities, and וּמִגְרְשֵׁי הֶֽעָרִים, the open lands of the cities. In another form, לְקוֹל זַֽעֲקַת חֹֽבְלָיִךְ יִרְֽעֲשׁוּ מִגְרֹשֽׁוֹת (Yechezkel 27:28), at the cry of your pilots the open places shake, called so because they lie outside the city, as though they had been driven out of it.

גרס.sense: To break and crush: a soul broken with longing, teeth crushed on gravel, and grain crushed small.

more.t: גָּרְסָה נַפְשִׁי לְתַֽאֲבָה (Tehillim 119:20), my soul is crushed with longing, he reads as broken and pounded from the greatness of its desire toward your judgments. The form that makes another do it is וַיַּגְרֵס בֶּֽחָצָץ שִׁנָּי (Eichah 3:17 in his edition), he crushed my teeth on gravel, which he glosses וישבר, and he broke.

more.h: Crushed grain, and a dish of it
more.t: Written with a sin: גֶּרֶשׂ כַּרְמֶל (Vayikra 2:14), pointed with six dots, and מִגִּרְשָׂהּ וּמִשַּׁמְנָהּ (Vayikra 2:16), of its groats and of its oil, which is the wheat broken and crumbled, and he gives the Old French word for it. Like it in the words of Chazal (Avodah Zarah 65b), חומץ שנפל לתוך הגריסין, vinegar that fell into the grits.

בוץ.sense: Butz is linen: וְתַכְרִיךְ בּוּץ (Esther 8:15), a robe of butz; and the Targum renders מִֽכְנְסֵי־בַד (Vayikra 6:3), linen breeches, with this word.

זמן.sense: An appointed time, a span fixed in advance.

more.t: וָאֶתְּנָה לוֹ זְמָן (Nechemiah 2:6), and I set him a time; לַכֹּל זְמָן וְעֵת (Koheles 3:1), everything has its time and its season; and יְמֵי הַפֻּרִים הָאֵלֶּה בִּזְמַנֵּיהֶם (Esther 9:31), these days of Purim at their times, which he glosses as year by year.
לְעִתִּים מְזֻמָּנִים (Ezra 10:14) and בְּעִתִּים מְזֻמָּנוֹת (Nechemiah 13:31), at times appointed; of these he says only that their sense is known.

יעד.sense: To appoint or set a time, and to designate; the noun מוֹעֵד is both the appointed time and the place where people meet at it.

more.t: מִן־הַמּוֹעֵד אֲשֶׁר יְעָדוֹ (Shmuel II 20:5), the set time he had appointed him, and וְאִם־לִבְנוֹ יִיעָדֶנָּה (Shemos 21:9), if he designates her for his son.
וְנוֹעַדְתִּי לְךָ שָׁם (Shemos 25:22), I will meet with you there, and כִּי־הִנֵּה הַמְּלָכִים נוֹעֲדוּ (Tehillim 48:5), for behold the kings had assembled. He puts the whole of it under summoning.

Rabbi Yehudah set יוֹעִידֶנִּי apart to a sense of its own; Radak says there is no need, since these too are summoning. כִּי מִי כָמוֹנִי וּמִי יֹעִידֶנִּי (Yirmiyahu 49:19) he reads as who will summon for Me one like Me, and וְאִם־לְמִשְׁפָּט מִי יוֹעִידֵנִי (Iyov 9:19) as who will summon me to judgment with Hashem.

בְּמֹעֵד שְׁנַת הַשְּׁמִטָּה (Devarim 31:10), at the set time of the shemittah year; מוֹעֵד וְשַׁבָּת (Eichah 2:6), festival and Shabbos; and לַשַּׁבָּתוֹת וְלֶחֳדָשִׁים וְלַמּוֹעֲדוֹת (Divrei HaYamim II 8:13), which he says all mean a time, times.

מֵהַבֹּקֶר וְעַד־עֵת מוֹעֵד (Shmuel II 24:15) he takes as the time of the offering, which he puts at four hours, and brings Targum Yonasan, who renders it from the slaughtering of the tamid until it is brought up.

A place where people gather at a known time is called a מוֹעֵד. שָׁאֲגוּ צֹרְרֶיךָ בְּקֶרֶב מוֹעֲדֶךָ (Tehillim 74:4), your foes roared in the midst of your meeting place, he takes of the Beis HaMikdash, where all Yisrael would meet, and so שָׂרְפוּ כָל־מוֹעֲדֵי־אֵל (Tehillim 74:8), they burned all the meeting places of Hashem. קְרִאֵי מוֹעֵד (Bamidbar 16:2) are those called when the great men met on some matter, since they were men of standing.
The אהל מועד is so called because Yisrael would gather there, and further because Hashem met with Moshe there, as וְנוֹעַדְתִּי לְךָ שָׁם (Shemos 25:22) says.

וְאֵשֵׁב בְּהַר־מוֹעֵד בְּיַרְכְּתֵי צָפוֹן (Yeshayahu 14:13), I will sit on the mount of meeting in the far north, is a place where all the kings gather to him, which he says is Bavel; וּבֵית מוֹעֵד לְכָל־חָי (Iyov 30:23), a meeting house for all the living, is the grave, where every living thing is appointed to come at its end; and עָרֵי הַמּוּעָדָה (Yehoshua 20:9) are the cities where anyone who killed by accident was to gather.

The assembly is called an עֵדָה, as קְרִיאֵי הָעֵדָה (Bamidbar 26:9), those called of the congregation, because they are summoned together in their gathering; and so a swarm, וְהִנֵּה עֲדַת דְּבוֹרִים (Shoftim 14:8), a company of bees, gathered as though each had been summoned to the next.

שׁעה.sense: To turn toward, and so to regard or rely on; in other senses, to be alarmed, and to leave off.

more.t: וְאֶל־קַיִן וְאֶל־מִנְחָתוֹ לֹא שָׁעָה (Bereishis 4:5), He did not turn to Kayin and his offering, while of Hevel, אֶל־הֶבֶל וְאֶל־מִנְחָתוֹ (Bereishis 4:4), He did turn. He glosses both as turning, in the way of אַל־תֵּפֶן אֶל־מִנְחָתָם (Bamidbar 16:15), do not turn to their offering.

יִשְׁעוּ וְאֵין מֹשִׁיעַ (Shmuel II 22:42) he reads as turning this way and that with none to save; or it is like יְשַׁוְּעוּ (Tehillim 18:42), they cry out, so that שׁוּעַ and שָׁעָה would be one sense.

In another sense, יִשְׁעֶה הָאָדָם עַל־עֹשֵׂהוּ (Yeshayahu 17:7), a man will look to his Maker; וְלֹא יִשְׁעֶה אֶל־הַמִּזְבְּחוֹת (Yeshayahu 17:8), he will not look to the altars; וְלֹא שָׁעוּ עַל־קְדוֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל (Yeshayahu 31:1), they did not look to the Holy One of Yisrael; and וְאַל־יִשְׁעוּ בְּדִבְרֵי־שָׁקֶר (Shemos 5:9), let them not look to words of falsehood. He gives the sense as trust, and adds that these may be explained from the first sense too.

וְלֹא תִשְׁעֶינָה עֵינֵי רֹאִים (Yeshayahu 32:3), the eyes of those who see will not be dimmed, and אַל־תִּשְׁתָּע כִּי־אֲנִי אֱלֹהֶיךָ (Yeshayahu 41:10), be not dismayed, for I am your God, he gives as alarm and fear. The first he also allows from וְעֵינָיו הָשַׁע (Yeshayahu 6:10), two roots with one sense.
On אַל־תִּשְׁתָּע Bereishis Rabbah reads, do not be like שעוה, wax, which is the דונג, meaning do not melt like wax before fire. Radak adds that wax is beyond doubt from this root.

שְׁעֵה מֵעָלָיו וְיֶחְדָּל (Iyov 14:6), turn away from him that he may rest, and שְׁעוּ מִנִּי אֲמָרֵר בַּבֶּכִי (Yeshayahu 22:4), leave me be, that I may weep bitterly. His father explains אַל־תִּשְׁתָּע from this sense, do not go slack.

וְאֶשְׁעָה בְחֻקֶּיךָ תָמִיד (Tehillim 119:117), I will delight in Your statutes always, he takes with תּוֹרָתְךָ שַׁעֲשֻׁעָי (Tehillim 119:92), Your Torah is my delight, the kamatz standing in for a segol; or as a sense of recounting, from the Targum of וַיְסַפֵּר (Bereishis 37:10), which is וְאִשְׁתָּעֵי. So too וְנִשְׁתָּעָה (Yeshayahu 41:23), let us tell it, where the kamatz again stands where a segol would; but Targum Yonasan renders it as looking, and on that it belongs to the first sense.
וּבְמַיִם לֹא־רֻחַצְתְּ לְמִשְׁעִי (Yechezkel 16:4), you were not washed in water, he gives no sense here, saying he has written it under the root שוע.

שׁלל.sense: To take spoil, and the spoil taken.

more.t: וְשָׁלַל שְׁלָלָהּ (Yechezkel 29:19), he will take its spoil; כִּי אַתָּה שַׁלּוֹתָ גּוֹיִם רַבִּים (Chavakuk 2:8), because you plundered many nations; and in the same pasuk יְשָׁלּוּךָ כָּל־יֶתֶר עַמִּים, all the rest of the peoples will plunder you.

שׁוֹלָל וְעָרוֹם (Michah 1:8), stripped and bare. On מוֹלִיךְ יוֹעֲצִים שׁוֹלָל (Iyov 12:17) he says each of the counsellors is led off so, his counsel availing him nothing; others take שׁוֹלָל as stripped of understanding, like וְשֹׁפְטִים יְהוֹלֵל in the same pasuk, and He makes fools of judges.

אֶשְׁתּוֹלְלוּ אַבִּירֵי לֵב (Tehillim 76:6), the stout of heart were despoiled, where the alef stands in place of a hei; and וְסָר מֵרָע מִשְׁתּוֹלֵל (Yeshayahu 59:15), which he reads as though they had despoiled the man who turns from evil, so that he is not to be found.

וְאֶת־הַמַּלְקוֹחַ וְאֶת־הַשָּׁלָל (Bamidbar 31:12), the booty and the spoil, and זֶה שְׁלַל דָּוִד (Shmuel I 30:20), this is David's spoil. וְהָיְתָה לְךָ נַפְשְׁךָ לְשָׁלָל (Yirmiyahu 39:18), your life will be yours as spoil, he glosses as gain, as though you had taken it as plunder.
שֹׁל־תָּשֹׁלּוּ לָהּ (Rus 2:16) he brings as close to this sense, meaning let ears fall for her out of the bundles.

בזז.sense: To plunder, and the plunder taken; he gives it the sense of שלל.

more.t: וּבָזַז בִּזָּהּ (Yechezkel 29:19), he will plunder its plunder; בָּזְזוּ לָהֶם בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל (Yehoshua 11:14), Bnei Yisrael plundered for themselves; בַּזּוֹנוּ לָנוּ (Devarim 3:7), we plundered for ourselves; שְׁאֵרִית עַמִּי יְבָזּוּם (Tzefaniah 2:9), the remnant of My people will plunder them; and וּשְׁלָלָם לָבוֹז (Esther 8:11), their spoil to plunder.
In וְנָבֹזָה בָהֶם עַד־אוֹר הַבֹּקֶר (Shmuel I 14:36), let us plunder among them until the morning light, the zayin is left without its dagesh, which he says belongs to it by right.
וְהִבּוֹז תִּבּוֹז (Yeshayahu 24:3), it shall surely be plundered, and חֶרֶב אֶל־אוֹצְרֹתֶיהָ וּבֻזָּזוּ (Yirmiyahu 50:37), a sword upon her treasuries, and they were plundered.
וּבַבִּזָּה לֹא שָׁלְחוּ אֶת־יָדָם (Esther 9:10), they did not put out their hand to the plunder, and without the hei, יֶתֶר הַבָּז (Bamidbar 31:32), the rest of the plunder.

לקח.sense: To take, in every use of taking; and from it a purchase, booty carried off, and a teaching received.

more.t: וְאֶתְכֶם לָקַח (Devarim 4:20), and you He took. Where the first letter drops, קָח עַל־מַיִם רַבִּים (Yechezkel 17:5), take it to abundant waters, and the kamatz keeps it apart from the command. From how heavily the word is used, both that letter and the kuf's dagesh fall away in most places, as in וְאֶקְחָה פַת־לֶחֶם (Bereishis 18:5), let me fetch a morsel of bread.

וַיִּקַּח קֹרַח (Bamidbar 16:1) he reads as Korach taking himself along with his fellows, and they took counsel in the matter; so too וַיִּקְחוּ שְׁלֹשִׁים מֵרֵעִים (Shoftim 14:12), thirty companions were taken, and וְאַבְשָׁלֹם לָקַח (Shmuel II 18:18), who took this counsel upon himself. תִּקַּח־לָהּ (Bereishis 38:23) he glosses as let her keep them for herself, and do not go after them again.

כִּי־לָקַח אֹתוֹ אֱלֹהִים (Bereishis 5:24), for Hashem took him; כִּי יִקָּחֵנִי סֶלָה (Tehillim 49:16), for He will take me; and וְאַחַר כָּבוֹד תִּקָּחֵנִי (Tehillim 73:24), and afterward You will take me in honour. These he sets apart as said of the death of the righteous.

הוּא בַּעֲוֹנוֹ נִלְקָח (Yechezkel 33:6), he is taken for his own sin; וַאֲרוֹן הָאֱלֹהִים נִלְקָחָה (Shmuel I 4:17), the Aron of Hashem was captured; and וְאֵשׁ מִתְלַקַּחַת (Shemos 9:24), fire taking hold of itself.

מַלְקוֹחַ is what is carried off: אֶת־הַשְּׁבִי וְאֶת־הַמַּלְקוֹחַ (Bamidbar 31:12) and וּמַלְקוֹחַ עָרִיץ (Yeshayahu 49:25), the booty of the tyrant. Where the three words stand together he divides them: שבי of people, מלקוח of animals, שלל of clothing and vessels. One comes in place of another all the same: וְחָצִיתָ אֶת־הַמַּלְקוֹחַ (Bamidbar 31:27) is said of man and beast alike, and זֶה שְׁלַל דָּוִד (Shmuel I 30:20) of animals.

וּמִקַּח־שֹׁחַד (Divrei HaYamim II 19:7), the taking of a bribe; הַמְבִיאִים אֶת־הַמַּקָּחוֹת (Nechemiah 10:32), those who brought in the wares; and in the words of Chazal (Bava Metzia 2a) מקח וממכר, buying and selling. From this he reads לֹקְחֵי חִטִּים (Shmuel II 4:6) as though buyers of wheat, and brings Targum Yonasan, who renders it so; and זָמְמָה שָׂדֶה וַתִּקָּחֵהוּ (Mishlei 31:16), she considered a field and bought it.

The tongs are called מלקחים because they take hold of a thing: בְּמֶלְקָחַיִם לָקַח מֵעַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ (Yeshayahu 6:6), with tongs he took from upon the mizbeach, and וּמַלְקָחֶיהָ וּמַחְתֹּתֶיהָ (Shemos 37:23), its tongs and its pans, named in the pair form since they are two. The menorah's tongs served to lift the wicks out of the oil, set them straight and draw them to the mouths of the lamps. וּלְשׁוֹנִי מֻדְבָּק מַלְקוֹחָי (Tehillim 22:16), my tongue cleaves to my palate: what lies above the tongue and beneath it is so called, since they close and take the food in chewing.

In the sense of knowledge, כִּי לֶקַח טוֹב נָתַתִּי לָכֶם (Mishlei 4:2), for I have given you a good teaching; וְיוֹסֶף לֶקַח (Mishlei 1:5), he will add learning; יַעֲרֹף כַּמָּטָר לִקְחִי (Devarim 32:2), my teaching will fall as the rain; and הִטַּתּוּ בְּרֹב לִקְחָהּ (Mishlei 7:21), she turned him with her much persuading. From this he reads הַלֹּקְחִים לְשׁוֹנָם וַיִּנְאֲמוּ נְאֻם (Yirmiyahu 23:31), who take their tongue and declare a declaration, like לְשׁוֹנָם יַחֲלִיקוּן (Tehillim 5:10), they make their tongue smooth.

Rabbi Yonah read וַיִּקְחוּ הָאֲנָשִׁים מִצֵּידָם (Yehoshua 9:14) from this sense of learning, that they learned and knew from the dryness of the provision that the truth was with them. Radak holds there is no need to take it out of the plain sense of taking: the men of Yisrael took of their provision and ate, to confirm the covenant with them. So too וַיִּקַּח וַיִּתֵּן אֶת־הָעֵדֻת (Shemos 40:20) is as it sounds, he took the luchos of the covenant and put them in the Aron.

שׁבה.sense: To take captive, and the captives taken.

more.t: אֲשֶׁר־שָׁבָה יִשְׁמָעֵאל (Yirmiyahu 41:14), whom Yishmael had taken captive; וַיִּשְׁבְּ מִמֶּנּוּ שֶׁבִי (Bamidbar 21:2 in his edition), he took captives from him; וְשָׁבִיתָ שִׁבְיוֹ (Devarim 21:10), and you take his captives; and שֹׁבִים לְשֹׁבֵיהֶם (Yeshayahu 14:2), taking their captors captive.

כִּי נִשְׁבָּה אָחִיו (Bereishis 14:14), for his brother had been taken captive, and וּנְשֵׁיהֶם וּבְנֵיהֶם וּבְנֹתֵיהֶם נִשְׁבּוּ, their wives and sons and daughters had been taken captive. Of these he says only that their sense is known.
שְׁבִיָּה בַּת־צִיּוֹן (Yeshayahu 52:2), captive daughter of Tzion; for a man, he says, the form would be שָׁבִי, on the pattern of עָנִי, a poor man.

קוּמִי שְּׁבִי יְרוּשָׁלָם (Yeshayahu 52:2) he brings among the nouns of captivity, and notes that Targum Yonasan took it instead from יָשַׁב, to sit: arise, sit upon the throne of honour, Yerushalayim.

וְרָאִיתָ בַּשִּׁבְיָה (Devarim 21:11), and you see among the captive women; וּבְנֹתָיו בַּשְּׁבִית (Bamidbar 21:29), his daughters in captivity; שְׁבִיתֵנוּ (Tehillim 126:4), our captivity; and with a shuruk, אֶת־שְׁבוּתְךָ (Devarim 30:3), your captivity, and שְׁבוּת אָהֳלֵי יַעֲקוֹב (Yirmiyahu 30:18), the captivity of the tents of Yaakov.
לֶשֶׁם שְׁבוֹ (Shemos 28:19), leshem and shevo, he files here, saying the shevo is one of the precious stones, and giving its Arabic name.

שׁלך.sense: To throw or cast down; and so to cast out of a place, and to cast a lot.

more.t: הִשְׁלִיךְ מִשָּׁמַיִם אֶרֶץ (Eichah 2:1), He cast earth down from heaven; וַתַּשְׁלֵךְ אֶת־הַיֶּלֶד (Bereishis 21:15), she cast the child down; הַשְׁלִיכוּ אֹתוֹ אֶל־הַבּוֹר (Bereishis 37:22), throw him into the pit; and מַשְׁלִיךְ קַרְחוֹ כְפִתִּים (Tehillim 147:17), casting His ice like crumbs. He gives the whole of it as throwing and felling.
כִּי הִשְׁלִיכוּ מִשְׁכְּנוֹתֵינוּ (Yirmiyahu 9:18) he reads as they cast us out of our dwellings, in the way of וְלֹא־תָקִיא אֶתְכֶם הָאָרֶץ (Vayikra 20:22), that the land should not vomit you out.
וּפֹה אַשְׁלִיךְ לָכֶם גּוֹרָל (Yehoshua 18:8), and here I will cast a lot for you.

וְהֻשְׁלַךְ מְכוֹן מִקְדָּשׁוֹ (Daniel 8:11), the place of His Mikdash was cast down; עָלֶיךָ הָשְׁלַכְתִּי מֵרָחֶם (Tehillim 22:11), upon You I was cast from the womb; and וַתֻּשְׁלְכִי אֶל־פְּנֵי הַשָּׂדֶה (Yechezkel 16:5), you were cast out on the open field.

וַיַּשְׁלִכוּ הָרָצִים וְהַשָּׁלִשִׁים וַיֵּלְכוּ (Melachim II 10:25), the runners and the officers flung them down and went: this he says is said by extension, from how hurried and quick they were when they were sent to the city of Beis HaBaal to break the pillars.

וְאֶת־הַשָּׁלָךְ (Vayikra 11:17) Chachamim explained (Chullin 63a) as the one that draws fish out of the sea, and Onkelos renders it in the same way. אֲשֶׁר בְּשַׁלֶּכֶת (Yeshayahu 6:13) he takes as the name of a gate of the Beis HaMikdash, the one named עִם שַׁעַר שַׁלֶּכֶת (Divrei HaYamim I 26:16), with the gate of Shalleches, while Targum Yonasan took it as a word of casting.

He brings Targum Yonasan's rendering of that pasuk entire: like the terebinth and the oak, whose leaves fall and look dry while they are still moist and keep seed in them, so the exile of Yisrael will be gathered in and returned to their land, for the holy seed is their planting.

זרק.sense: To throw, and in particular to dash or sprinkle a liquid.

more.t: וּזְרָקוֹ מֹשֶׁה הַשָּׁמַיְמָה (Shemos 9:8), Moshe threw it toward the heavens; וַחֲצִי הַדָּם זָרַק עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּחַ (Shemos 24:6), half the blood he dashed on the mizbeach; and וְזָרַקְתִּי עֲלֵיכֶם מַיִם טְהוֹרִים וּטְהַרְתֶּם (Yechezkel 36:25), I will throw pure water upon you and you will be pure.

גַּם־שֵׂיבָה זָרְקָה בּוֹ (Hoshea 7:9), grey too is scattered through him, he takes either as a verb standing on its own, the grey having been cast into him, or as saying that his own nature cast the grey into him, since grey comes of a man's nature.
כִּי מֵי נִדָּה לֹא־זֹרַק עָלָיו (Bamidbar 19:13), for the water of sprinkling was not thrown upon him.

The vessel one throws from is a מִזְרָק: וְיָעָיו וּמִזְרְקֹתָיו (Shemos 27:3), its shovels and its basins; כַּמִּזְרָקִים לִפְנֵי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ (Zechariah 14:20), like the basins before the mizbeach; and מִזְרְקֵי־כֶסֶף (Bamidbar 7:84), basins of silver.

הַשֹּׁתִים בְּמִזְרְקֵי יַיִן (Amos 6:6), who drink wine from basins: he says the governed word is missing, and they drink their wine in basins of silver or gold; or else the form stands for מזרקים. He sets חַלּוֹנֵי שְׁקֻפִים (Melachim I 6:4) and נִטְעֵי נַעֲמָנִים (Yeshayahu 17:10) beside it.

נזה.sense: To spatter or sprinkle, said of blood and of the waters of purification.

more.t: וַאֲשֶׁר יִזֶּה מִדָּמָהּ עַל־הַבֶּגֶד (Vayikra 6:20), whatever of its blood spatters on a garment, and וַיִּז מִדָּמָהּ אֶל־הַקִּיר (Melachim II 9:33), some of her blood spattered on the wall.

וְהִזָּה אֶל־הַבַּיִת (Vayikra 14:51), he shall sprinkle toward the house; יַזֶּה שֶׁבַע־פְּעָמִים (Vayikra 16:14), he shall sprinkle seven times; הַזֵּה עֲלֵיהֶם מֵי חַטָּאת (Bamidbar 8:7), sprinkle the waters of the chatas upon them; and וַיַּז מִמֶּנּוּ (Vayikra 8:11), and he sprinkled some of it. He says the sense of sprinkling is known, and that it is the sense of dripping.

more.h: The one who carries the water
more.t: On וּמַזֵּה מֵי־הַנִּדָּה (Bamidbar 19:21) he brings Chazal (Niddah 9a), that the one who sprinkles stays tahor and the pasuk speaks rather of one who carries, who takes a severe tumah that makes tamei the clothes upon him, unlike one who only touches, who need not launder his clothes; and the form מִזֵּה was used to say that he is not tamei until there is enough of it for a sprinkling. On that reading מזה is a noun on the pattern of מַטֶּה, and the pasuk means that whoever carries the sprinkling of the water of the niddah shall launder his clothes.
כֵּן יַזֶּה גּוֹיִם רַבִּים (Yeshayahu 52:15), so will he sprinkle many nations, he takes in the sense of speaking, a verb that carries an object; the edition sets a foreign word beside it.

רמה.sense: To throw, as an arrow from a bow; and in another sense, to deceive.

more.t: רָמָה בַיָּם (Shemos 15:1), He cast into the sea; פָּרָשׁ וְרֹמֵה קֶשֶׁת (Yirmiyahu 4:29), horseman and bowman; נוֹשְׁקֵי רוֹמֵי־קָשֶׁת (Tehillim 78:9), armed shooters of the bow; and רָמַת לֶחִי (Shoftim 15:17), the casting of the jawbone. The sense of throwing, he says, is well known, and from it he takes the noun in הָיוּ כְּקֶשֶׁת רְמִיָּה (Hoshea 7:16), they were like a bow that throws.

more.h: Rabbi Yonah on a hard pasuk
more.t: Rabbi Yonah read וּמִלֵּאתִי הַגֵּאָיוֹת רָמוּתֶךָ (Yechezkel 32:5) from this sense, and I will fill the valleys with what you cast down, meaning that the slain of your multitude will fall there.

כֵּן־אִישׁ רִמָּה אֶת־רֵעֵהוּ (Mishlei 26:19), so a man deceived his fellow; לָמָּה רִמִּיתָנִי (Shmuel I 28:12), why did you deceive me; הֵמָּה רִמּוּנִי (Eichah 1:19), they deceived me; and וְאִם־לְרַמּוֹתַנִי לְצָרַי (Divrei HaYamim I 12:17), but if to betray me to my foes.

וְלוֹ תְּדַבְּרוּ רְמִיָּה (Iyov 13:7), will you speak deceit for Him, on the pattern of בִּצְדִיָּה (Bamidbar 35:20); לָשׁוֹן רְמִיָּה (Tehillim 120:3), a deceitful tongue; הֶחֱזִיקוּ בַּתַּרְמִית (Yirmiyahu 8:5), they held fast to deceit; and מֹאזְנֵי מִרְמָה (Mishlei 11:1), scales of fraud.

more.h: Where his father reads a place
more.t: בְּתָרְמָה לֵאמֹר (Shoftim 9:31), in Tormah, saying, his father explains as the name of a place, since no word of that pattern with an added tav is found.

He ends that כְּקֶשֶׁת רְמִיָּה may belong to the sense of deceit instead, a bow that shoots deceitfully so that no one notices it; and so כְּתַעַר מְלֻטָּשׁ עֹשֵׂה רְמִיָּה (Tehillim 52:4), like a sharpened razor working deceit.

רטב.sense: To be moist; he gives it simply as the sense of wetness.

more.t: רָטֹב הוּא לִפְנֵי־שָׁמֶשׁ (Iyov 8:16), he is moist before the sun, and מִזֶּרֶם הָרִים יִרְטָבוּ (Iyov 24:8), they are drenched by the mountain rains. The entry holds no more than this.

רען.sense: Fresh and full of sap, as a green tree is; he gives the sense as wetness.

more.h: Verb or adjective by the stress
more.t: The word doubles its last letter. וְכִפָּתוֹ לֹא רַעֲנָנָה (Iyov 15:32), his branch will not be fresh, he calls a verb of past time, because the stress falls back; אַף־עַרְשֵׂנוּ רַעֲנָנָה (Shir HaShirim 1:16), our couch too is fresh, is an adjective, because the stress falls at the end.

כְּזַיִת רַעֲנָן (Tehillim 52:10), like a fresh olive tree; וְהָיָה עָלֵהוּ רַעֲנָן (Yirmiyahu 17:8), its leaf will stay green; and in the plural, which takes a dagesh, דְּשֵׁנִים וְרַעֲנַנִּים יִהְיוּ (Tehillim 92:15), they will be full of sap and fresh.
בְּשֶׁמֶן רַעֲנָן (Tehillim 92:11), with fresh oil, he glosses as new oil.

רטפשׁ.sense: Said of flesh made young again; from its setting he reads it as having grown soft.

more.t: רֻטֲפַשׁ בְּשָׂרוֹ מִנֹּעַר (Iyov 33:25), his flesh grew fresh again beyond a youth's; the word itself, he says, is to be taken from its place as meaning it became tender.
Some say it is two words joined, רטוב and פש, moist and increasing, the second from the Targum of פְּרוּ וּרְבוּ (Bereishis 1:28), be fruitful and multiply, which is פּוּשׁוּ וּסְגוּ.
They explained further that רטפש is רטוב by atbash, the peh standing for a vav and the shin for a beis. Its Targum is אִתְחֲלִישׁ בִּסְרֵיהּ, his flesh grew weak.

טפח.sense: A tefach, the handbreadth measure; and a verb of patting, used of rearing a child.

more.t: מִסְגֶּרֶת טֹפַח (Shemos 25:25), a rim a handbreadth wide, and שֵׁשׁ־אַמּוֹת בָּאַמָּה וָטֹפַח (Yechezkel 40:5), six cubits by the cubit and a handbreadth; in another form, וְעָבְיוֹ טֶפַח (Divrei HaYamim II 4:5), its thickness a handbreadth. In Tanach the plural is feminine, הִנֵּה טְפָחוֹת נָתַתָּה יָמַי (Tehillim 39:6), while Chazal use it as a masculine, טפחים.

The tefach is of a kind with the זרת, the span, but not of one size with it: the span is measured by the fingers of the hand spread apart and the tefach by four fingers held together, and the span is three tefachim, as he has written.

הִנֵּה טְפָחוֹת נָתַתָּה יָמַי, You have made my days handbreadths, he reads against what comes before it, וּמִדַּת יָמַי מַה־הִיא (Tehillim 39:5), what is the measure of my days: as the tefach's measure is small, so is the measure of his days. Even were he to live all a man can live, his days are handbreadths, as כִּי אֶלֶף שָׁנִים בְּעֵינֶיךָ כְּיוֹם אֶתְמוֹל (Tehillim 90:4), a thousand years in Your eyes are as yesterday.

וּמִמַּסַּד עַד־הַטְּפָחוֹת (Melachim I 7:9), from the foundation to the coping, he reads as from the foundation up to the wall above, which was built to the handbreadth measure; Targum Yonasan renders it finished by handbreadths.

וִימִינִי טִפְּחָה שָׁמָיִם (Yeshayahu 48:13), My right hand spread out the heavens, which some precise sefarim point otherwise. אֲשֶׁר־טִפַּחְתִּי וְרִבִּיתִי (Eichah 2:22), whom I reared and raised: טִפַּחְתִּי, he says, is of the rearing of children, since so they do to an infant, patting him and straightening his limbs each time they swaddle him. So too עֹלֲלֵי טִפֻּחִים (Eichah 2:20), infants who are patted and reared while small and whose upbringing is seen to, and who were then eaten.

הָבִי הַמִּטְפַּחַת אֲשֶׁר־עָלַיִךְ (Rus 3:15), give me the cloth that is upon you, he glosses as a veil, and so וְהַמִּטְפָּחוֹת וְהַחֲרִיטִים (Yeshayahu 3:22), veils. He brings Chazal (Megillah 26b), that worn mitpachos of sefarim are made into shrouds for a meis mitzvah, and that is their genizah. Some explain הַמִּטְפָּחוֹת from the first sense, as gloves, for which he gives a foreign word.

פאה.sense: The side, edge or corner of a thing; and a verb of scattering to every side.

more.t: לַפֵּאָה הָאֶחָת (Shemos 27:9), for the one side; עַל אַרְבַּע הַפֵּאֹת (Shemos 25:26), on the four corners; and וּמָחַץ פַּאֲתֵי מוֹאָב (Bamidbar 24:17), and he will smite the corners of Moav. The end of anything and its far edge, he says, is called a פאה.
